madinah.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Programme and Cambridge IGCSE subjects to students in Madinah over live video. Each one works to a named syllabus rather than to a general subject, because a Physics HL candidate and a 0625 candidate are preparing for different papers, different command terms and different internally assessed work.

intro.heading: Start with the assessment, then work back to the teaching
paragraphs: The useful way to think about IB and IGCSE support in Madinah is to look at what the student has to hand in, and who marks it. Every grade in both systems is built from components with fixed shapes. In the Diploma Programme a subject grade comes from written papers marked by examiners the student will never meet, plus an internally assessed piece that the class teacher marks against published criteria and the IB then moderates. In Cambridge IGCSE most subjects are decided entirely by written papers, with a smaller number carrying coursework or a practical component that the school marks and Cambridge moderates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs most of its subjects on written papers alone. Once a parent can see which part of the grade sits inside the school and which part leaves the building, almost every question about tutoring answers itself.

That matters more in Madinah than it would in Riyadh or Jeddah, because the number of schools here carrying a full international programme at secondary level is small, and it changes. Many families have a child in a strong bilingual school that teaches the national curriculum and offers a handful of international subjects, and they are trying to work out what has to be added from outside. Others have transferred in from Jeddah, the Eastern Province or another country part-way through a course and have discovered that the subject combination their child was promised is not running locally. In both cases the gap is specific: one Higher Level science, one maths route, one internally assessed component with nobody in the building who has marked one before.

A general tutor cannot close that kind of gap. A Mathematics teacher who knows the content of a syllabus is not the same as a teacher who knows what the Analysis and Approaches papers reward, which questions carry method marks, and how an exploration is credited against five published criteria. The same is true at IGCSE: a 0580 candidate sitting the Extended tier and a 0580 candidate sitting the Core tier are entered for different papers with different ceilings, and the right teaching for each is different. The first job of a tutor is to establish exactly what the student is entered for, in writing, from the school.

The second job is the part parents rarely hear about from a tutoring company. The marks lost in both systems are usually not knowledge marks. They are marks for command terms misread, for a conclusion that restates a result instead of evaluating it, for an exploration that explains what was done rather than why, or for a six-mark answer that gives four correct points with no development. Those losses are diagnosable from a student's own written work in a single session, and they are teachable. They are also invisible on a report card that says the student knows the material.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or licensed by the IB, Cambridge, Pearson or any Saudi authority, and it holds no partnership with any school named on this page. Lessons for families in Madinah are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Madinah address; home visits in Saudi Arabia are not a service we sell, and in-home teaching is something we offer only in India. The case for teaching this way in Madinah is practical rather than ideological, and the rest of this page sets it out subject by subject.

madinah.programmesIntro: Four programmes cover almost every Madinah enquiry. What matters for each is not its philosophy but what it makes a student produce, and when that production has to start. The notes below say what each programme asks for and what the Madinah version of it usually looks like in practice.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examination. Learning runs through transdisciplinary units of inquiry and ends with an exhibition in the final year, in which a group of students research a question and present it. Assessment is continuous and teacher-led, so a parent judges progress from the quality of a child's reasoning and writing rather than from a paper mark.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Madinah schools run the PYP itself, so most primary-age enquiries here come from bilingual schools using an English-medium scheme of work. The practical need at this stage is reading fluency, written explanation in English and number confidence, because those three decide how hard the move into an international lower secondary curriculum will be.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four published criteria each, marked out of eight and reported as achievement levels rather than percentages. The Personal Project in the final year is assessed against its own criteria and moderated. Students who learn to read criterion wording here find the Diploma far less of a jolt, because the Diploma works the same way with higher stakes.
programmes.countryNote: In Madinah the MYP is most often met part-way, as a framework a school applies to some subjects and not others. The gap that follows is usually in the criteria for scientific and mathematical investigation, since those need laboratory or data work the school may not be set up to run. A student who has never been marked against criterion wording arrives in Grade 9 writing good answers that score in the middle band.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded one to seven, plus the core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. TOK and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three further points through a published matrix, and the Diploma is awarded out of 45. Every subject carries internally assessed work alongside its papers.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is the sharpest pressure point for a Madinah family, because a school that offers it locally may still be unable to run every Higher Level combination a student wants. Where a subject is not timetabled, the student is left reading a syllabus alone. The practical questions are which Higher Levels the school can actually staff, who supervises the Extended Essay, and who has marked an internally assessed component before.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by written paper, with tiered entry on several subjects: Core or Extended on Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Foundation or Higher on Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A. Grading scales differ between the boards, and the certificate a student receives depends on the entry the school made, not on how well they were taught.
programmes.countryNote: IGCSE is the more common international route in Madinah because it needs fewer specialist staff than a full Diploma and can be examined through an examination centre. That also makes it the route where entry decisions are most often made quietly. Ask in writing which board, which syllabus code and which tier your child is entered for, and ask before the entry window rather than after it.

madinah.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Madinah families most often need from outside their school. Each note says what the subject actually assesses and where marks go missing, because that is what a tutor is being hired to fix.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, with proof, calculus and function work carrying the weight. Marks disappear in the method lines rather than the final answer: a correct result with no shown derivative or no justified step collects a fraction of the available credit. Higher Level adds depth that cannot be reached by revising Standard Level harder.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, with the graphic display calculator built into the course rather than tolerated. Students lose marks by producing a calculator output with no interpretation, or by choosing a statistical test without stating its conditions. The exploration here usually needs real data, which has to be found before it can be analysed.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Definitions are examined strictly, and so is uncertainty. A derivation that skips an assumption and a graph with no error treatment both lose credit that a confident student assumes is safe. The internally assessed investigation needs a question narrow enough to control, which is where most Madinah students need help first.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Three things decide the grade: calculation discipline, mechanism reasoning and the language of energetics and equilibrium. Students who can recite Le Chatelier lose marks explaining a shift without naming the change in concentration or temperature that caused it. Higher Level organic chemistry rewards sequence, not recall of isolated reactions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest-value skill is writing to the command term. An extended response asking a student to evaluate a method and one asking them to outline it are marked differently, and the same content earns very different scores. Data-based questions reward reading the axes carefully before reasoning about the trend.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation half of each answer are where this subject is won. A fully correct diagram with no axis labels and no stated shift scores badly, and a well-argued answer with no evaluation sits in the middle band. Higher Level adds quantitative work that punishes vague definitions of elasticity.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study discipline decides the mark. Students answer from theory instead of from the stimulus material, and lose application credit they had already earned. The internally assessed work needs a real organisation and a question that can actually be answered with the evidence available, not a broad topic.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The paper rewards analysis of how a text works on a reader, not a summary of what it says. Students in English-medium Madinah schools often read well and write confidently, then score in the middle band because they describe technique without connecting it to effect or audience.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language acquisition course, assessed across reading, writing, listening and speaking with text types that have conventions of their own. A blog, a formal letter and a speech are marked partly on whether they look like themselves. Strong speakers lose marks by ignoring register and format rather than by lacking vocabulary.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Madinah students are frequently stronger in spoken Arabic than their written assessment suggests. The A course demands literary analysis of set texts in Arabic; the B course demands controlled written registers. Choosing between them wrongly is one of the costliest subject decisions in the Diploma, and it is made early.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Examined on paper, not on a screen, which surprises students who code comfortably. Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the ability to explain an algorithm in writing carry marks. The internally assessed solution needs a genuine client and documented success criteria agreed before any code is written.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together these two contribute up to three points through the published matrix, and they are the components most often left until the pressure is on. The Extended Essay lives or dies on its research question. A tutor's role here is to interrogate the question and the argument, and to give feedback on drafts the student has written.

madinah.igcseSubjectsIntro: At IGCSE the syllabus code matters as much as the subject name, because two candidates in the same classroom can be entered for different papers. Confirm the code and the tier with the school before planning any support.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: The tier decides the grade ceiling, so this is the first thing to check. Algebraic fluency is what separates the bands: students who are secure with manipulation, indices and rearrangement score well across every topic, and students who are not lose marks in geometry and statistics questions that are really algebra in disguise.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
igcseSubjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for a mathematics-heavy Diploma or A Level route. It introduces calculus and trigonometric identities early, and it is the single most useful preparation for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches. Students underestimate the pace rather than the difficulty.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Formula recall is the smaller half of the work. The marks sit in unit handling, rearrangement under time pressure, and the practical or alternative-to-practical paper, where students who have had limited laboratory access struggle to describe a method precisely enough to be credited.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles work, ionic equations and the tests for gases and ions account for a disproportionate share of lost marks. Students who learn the qualitative analysis tables properly and practise the calculation steps in order rather than in their heads move up a band without learning new content.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: The content is large and the examination is precise. Definitions are marked against specific wording, and extended answers are marked against the command term. Diagram labelling and data interpretation are the fastest places to recover marks for a student who already knows the material.

igcseSubjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
igcseSubjects.description: Covers biology, chemistry and physics across a double award, which is often the route a school takes when it cannot staff three separate sciences. Breadth is the difficulty: students meet every major topic once and have little time to consolidate before the papers.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
igcseSubjects.levels: Single tier, with and without count-in speaking
igcseSubjects.description: The two codes differ in how speaking is treated, which is a school decision parents are rarely shown. Marks turn on reading-comprehension technique and on writing to a given text type and audience, not on vocabulary range. Summary writing is the most teachable component on the paper.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and reading analysis dominate. Strong writers lose marks by writing well in the wrong register or by analysing a passage in general terms instead of quoting and explaining specific choices. The paper rewards structure that can be seen at a glance.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 and 0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Both reward definition precision and the ability to apply a concept to the case material in front of the student. The commonest loss is an answer that explains a term correctly and never returns to the business or market the question actually named.

madinah.regionsTitle: Madinah districts, and what each one does to a weekday evening
madinah.regionsIntro: Madinah is compact next to Riyadh, but the school run and the visitor rhythm of the city still decide what time a lesson can realistically start. These are the districts most of our Madinah enquiries come from, with the scheduling consequence of each.

regions.name: Al Aziziyah
regions.note: A large residential district south-east of the centre with a dense private-school presence. Families here usually land on a slot between the end of the school day and the evening meal, and the main constraint is a sibling collection that runs later than the student's own finish time.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Residential and well connected to the ring roads, which makes a cross-city school run workable on most days. Lessons here are commonly set in the early evening, with the understanding that traffic on the Haram approaches can push a start time by fifteen minutes.

regions.name: Quba
regions.note: South of the centre and heavily residential, with families often attending schools some distance from home. The practical effect is a later start than a parent first proposes, so a single long session usually works better here than two short ones on consecutive days.

regions.name: Qurban
regions.note: Central and close to the Haram ring, where access patterns change with visitor numbers. Families here benefit most from a fixed weekly slot that does not need to be renegotiated, because the variable is the journey home rather than the student's availability.

regions.name: Sultanah
regions.note: An established district with a mix of national-curriculum and bilingual schools. Enquiries from here are often about adding one international subject to an otherwise settled timetable, which suits a single weekly hour with written work set between sessions.

regions.name: Shuran
regions.note: Newer housing to the north with longer journeys to the older school clusters. Students arrive home tired, so an early-evening session with a short, specific focus tends to hold attention better than a two-hour block.

regions.name: Al Jamiah
regions.note: The university district, home to academic households whose children are often strong readers already working above their year group. Support here is usually about assessment technique and the internally assessed components rather than about content.

regions.name: Abyar Ali
regions.note: On the Makkah road to the south-west, further from the main school clusters, with the longest school runs of any district on this list. Online delivery matters most here, because an in-home arrangement would spend more time in a car than in the lesson.

regions.name: Knowledge Economic City
regions.note: A planned development on the northern side of the city with a growing professional population. Families arriving here frequently transfer in mid-course from Jeddah, Riyadh or abroad, which makes a diagnostic first session more useful than a general subject review.

schoolClusters.city: Madinah itself
schoolClusters.note: Madinah's private sector is mostly national-curriculum schools, several of them bilingual, with a small number of English-medium schools carrying international subjects at the lower secondary stage. Diploma Programme provision is thin and it changes. Check the IB's own school directory and ask to see the school's Ministry of Education licence rather than trusting a list published by any tutoring company, this one included.

modes.title: One weekly hour on a single subject
modes.description: The default, and the right choice for most families. A fixed weekly slot on the subject with the widest gap, with written work set between sessions and marked before the next one. Progress is measured against the components of the course rather than against a general sense of confidence.

No part of an assessed piece is produced for the student, and that limit is explained to the family in the first session.

sections.heading: Who marks what, and why that decides where a tutor helps
paragraphs: Both systems split a grade between work that leaves the school and work that stays inside it, and the split changes what outside support can do. Written papers are marked by examiners against a mark scheme a student never sees. Internally assessed work is marked by the class teacher against published criteria and then checked by the board through moderation, which can move a whole cohort's marks up or down. A third category sits in between: a predicted grade, which is the school's professional judgement and is used by universities before any result exists.

For a Madinah family the practical consequence is that support divides cleanly in two. On the externally marked side, a tutor can work on anything: content, technique, timing, command terms, past papers, the lot. On the internally assessed side, the limits are strict and they come from the board rather than from us. A tutor may teach the skills the task needs, question a research question, point at a criterion the draft has not addressed and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, redraft or complete any part of it.

That line is worth stating plainly, because several pages competing for this search offer the opposite. An assessed piece produced by someone other than the student is academic misconduct. The consequence does not fall on the person who wrote it; it falls on the student, through the school, and it can cost a Diploma. A tutor who proposes to produce the work is proposing a risk the family carries alone.

The honest version is also more useful. A student who has been pushed to defend their own research question, forced to name which criterion each paragraph is serving and made to rewrite a weak evaluation themselves arrives at the examination able to do the same thing under timed conditions. The student who was handed a finished piece arrives with nothing transferable.

sections.heading: The questions to ask your Madinah school, subject by subject
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a parent in Madinah can do costs nothing: ask the school, in writing, what it has in place for each of your child's subjects. Schools answer these questions honestly when they are asked specifically. The vague version of the question produces a reassuring answer, and the specific version produces a plan.

The reason this matters here rather than everywhere is the size of the local market. A school running one Diploma cohort may have a single teacher covering a subject group, and that teacher may be excellent at Standard Level and have never taught the Higher Level extension. A school entering candidates through an examination centre may be strong on the written papers and have no laboratory for the practical component. Neither is a scandal. Both are facts a family needs before the entry window closes rather than after.

The table below is built to be taken to a meeting. Each row is a subject area, what the school needs in place for it, the question that establishes whether it is in place, and what a family does if the answer is no. In most cases the answer to a missing piece is not to move school. It is to add one specialist for one subject, which is a far smaller intervention than a transfer to Jeddah.

Write the answers down. A school that tells you in the autumn term that a Higher Level option is running, and then withdraws it when numbers fall, has changed your child's position materially. A written record is what lets you act early, which is the whole difference between a manageable gap and a scramble in the final term.

sections.heading: Why a small specialist pool is a staffing problem, not a quality problem
paragraphs: It is easy to read a thin local market as a comment on local schools. It is not. The constraint is arithmetic. A Higher Level subject needs a teacher who has taught that level, ideally one who has marked for the board, and a school needs enough candidates in that subject to justify a timetabled class. In a city with a small international cohort, both numbers are hard to reach at once, and the subject with the fewest students is the one that loses its class.

The scarcity is specific rather than general. Nobody struggles to find somebody to teach introductory mathematics. The gaps appear in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, in the Higher Level extensions of the sciences, in Economics taught by somebody who has marked the papers, and in less commonly chosen languages. These are the same subjects that cost the most per hour in every market in the region, for the same reason: the number of people who can genuinely teach them is small and they are not distributed evenly across cities.

This is the honest argument for teaching online in Madinah, and it has nothing to do with technology being fashionable. A family restricted to tutors who can physically reach their district is choosing from whoever happens to live nearby and is free at six in the evening. A family choosing online is selecting from everyone who teaches that exact syllabus, in any time zone that overlaps with a Madinah evening. For a Standard Level subject with many teachers, the difference is modest. For a scarce Higher Level subject, it is the difference between a specialist and the closest available substitute.

There is a second, quieter benefit. A tutor chosen for the syllabus rather than the postcode can be kept when the family relocates, which in the Kingdom happens often. A student who moves from Madinah to Jeddah or to the Eastern Province mid-course loses the school, the teachers and the cohort at once. Keeping the one person who knows how they write is worth more at that moment than it was before the move.

sections.heading: Command terms and criterion wording: the marks nobody teaches
paragraphs: Both the IB and the IGCSE boards publish the vocabulary they use to ask questions, and both mark against it. Describe, explain, evaluate, justify, compare, outline, discuss, deduce and show that are not synonyms. Each one tells the examiner what to look for and tells the student how much of what kind of writing earns the marks. A student who answers an evaluate question with a flawless explanation has written a good answer to a different question and will be paid accordingly.

The same applies to criterion wording on internally assessed work. MYP criteria are published with strands and achievement-level descriptors, and Diploma internal assessment criteria describe exactly what distinguishes a top band from the one below it. Students who have never read those descriptors write what they think good work looks like. Students who have read them write to the strand, and the difference is visible in a single page of text.

This is the cheapest improvement available in either system, and it is routinely skipped because it feels like a technicality rather than learning. It is not a technicality. It is the interface between what a student knows and what anybody can award them for, and it transfers across every subject they take. A session spent taking apart four of the student's own answers against four command terms will usually do more for a grade than a session spent on new content.

A tutor working this way needs the student's actual written work, not a textbook. The first session on a new subject should always start with something the student has written and had marked, because that is where the diagnosable pattern lives. Two answers are usually enough to see whether the problem is knowledge, structure or the command term, and those three problems have three completely different fixes.
bullets: Describe asks for features; explain asks for a reason; evaluate asks for a judgement supported both ways
Mark schemes award development, not repetition of the same point in new words
Criterion descriptors name the difference between bands in plain language

sections.heading: What one-to-one support costs a Madinah family
paragraphs: Rates in this market are advertised rather than regulated, and the published numbers come from tutoring companies and marketplaces describing their own pricing. They are a guide to the shape of the market, not a market average, and nothing in the table below is what IB Gram charges. What the table does show is the size of the range and what moves a family up or down inside it.

The drivers are consistent across the region. Subject scarcity comes first: a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level or Physics Higher Level specialist is priced above a Standard Level generalist everywhere, because fewer people can do the work. Marking or examining experience comes second, and it is the one families most often pay for without checking. Level comes third, with Higher Level above Standard Level, and both above MYP and IGCSE. Then comes whether a tutor has to travel, which is the loading online teaching removes. Package length comes last and usually moves the number least.

Two things are worth doing with a quoted rate. Ask what the number is high for: scarcity, experience, or a long commute built into the price. And ask what the rate includes beyond the hour, because marking written work between sessions, feedback on a draft and a written note to the parent are either in the price or they are not, and the difference is substantial over a term.

For a Madinah family the comparison with in-home teaching is mostly about who is available rather than about price. Published in-home rates in the larger Saudi cities carry a travel loading, and Madinah's smaller specialist pool means the premium buys a smaller choice. The same budget spent on an online specialist buys a tutor selected for the syllabus, and the hour is spent teaching rather than arriving.

sections.heading: When to start, by year group
paragraphs: The question parents ask is how many lessons a week. The question that decides the outcome is when support starts relative to the components. Every year group has a point where intervention is cheap and a point where it is expensive, and the gap between them is usually one term.

At MYP level the useful work is criterion literacy and the habit of investigation, because both transfer directly into IGCSE and the Diploma. A student who reaches Grade 9 able to read a descriptor and write to it has an advantage that compounds. Starting here is the cheapest intervention available in either system, and it is the one most often postponed because nothing looks wrong yet.

At IGCSE the decisive moment is the tier and code decision, which happens earlier than most families realise and sets the ceiling. The second decisive moment is the start of the final year, when the volume of content outruns the time available to consolidate it. Support that begins at the start of that year works on sequencing and past papers. Support that begins in the final term works on damage limitation, which is a worse use of the same money.

In the Diploma, the first year is where the Higher Level choices either prove right or quietly start costing points, and it is also when the internally assessed work and the Extended Essay should be moving. Students who leave both until the second year are carrying coursework into the term when they most need to be practising papers. The last stretch before a series is for technique, timing and the specific errors a student repeats, not for first contact with a topic. It is never too late to start, but what is achievable narrows as the components close.

sections.heading: Equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili from a Madinah address
paragraphs: This is the part of the pathway almost nobody writing about Saudi tutoring covers, and it is the part that decides what an international qualification is actually worth inside the Kingdom. An IB Diploma, a set of A Levels and an American high school diploma all need an equivalency decision, known as mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats the certificate as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. The qualification does not become acceptable automatically because it is well known.

Alongside that sit the two Qiyas tests, run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and is sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Its content follows the Saudi national curriculum.

That last sentence is the one that matters for a Madinah family in an international programme. Tahsili is not a harder version of the examinations a Diploma or IGCSE student has already sat. It is a test of a different syllabus. The overlap in content is real, but the framing, the ordering and the expected notation are those of the national curriculum, which is why international-curriculum students often find it tougher than their own papers. Preparing for it is a separate piece of work from preparing for the June series, and it should be timetabled as one.

Universities publish their own admission formulas combining school results with the Qiyas tests, and those weightings differ by university and by programme, with competitive science and health programmes leaning hardest on Tahsili. We do not publish thresholds or formulas on this page, because they differ by institution and by cycle and a number quoted here would be wrong somewhere. Read the criteria on the university's own site, check whether a maximum age applies to the certificate being submitted, and start the equivalency paperwork earlier than feels necessary. Madinah families with a student aiming at Taibah University or the Islamic University of Madinah go through the same national process as anyone else.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, and lessons on Arabia Standard Time
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Most tutoring copy written for other markets assumes the opposite, which is why so much of it reads as though it was translated from somewhere else. For a Madinah family the working pattern is straightforward: four weekday evenings are genuinely available for lessons, Thursday evening is the start of the weekend and behaves like a Friday elsewhere, and Friday and Saturday suit longer sessions when a student needs them.

The Kingdom keeps Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not change its clocks. That one fact prevents the commonest scheduling failure in cross-border tutoring. A slot agreed in local terms with a tutor in a country that does change its clocks will move twice a year unless the agreement is pinned to Saudi local time rather than to the tutor's. Pin it to Madinah time, in writing, at the start.

Working backwards from a Madinah evening, a tutor in India is two and a half hours ahead, which makes a Madinah early-evening slot a late-evening one for them and workable but not comfortable. A tutor in the United Kingdom is two or three hours behind depending on their season, which puts a Madinah evening in their afternoon and makes this the most comfortable overlap of all. A tutor already in the Gulf shares the clock entirely. Those three facts, rather than a biography, decide whether a tutor can hold a weekly slot for a whole year.

Two local rhythms are worth planning around. School days shorten during Ramadan and evening study patterns shift, so families often move sessions later in the evening for that period; the dates move each year, so agree the change when it approaches rather than assuming it. And Madinah's visitor seasons change traffic and the shape of a weekday evening, which is a reason to hold a slot that does not depend on anybody completing a journey first. An online lesson starts when the student sits down.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the tutor is in another city
paragraphs: Distance makes one question sharper: how does a parent know the work is their child's own? It is a fair question and it has a practical answer. Ask for the session record. A tutor working properly on an internally assessed piece leaves a trail of questions asked and criteria pointed at, and the student leaves a trail of drafts in their own words. If the drafts improve in ways the student can explain out loud, the work is theirs. If a draft arrives transformed and the student cannot defend a paragraph of it, something has gone wrong regardless of who was in the room.

The boundary itself is not ours to set. The IB publishes what constitutes academic misconduct, schools are required to act on it, and the consequence lands on the student. A tutor may teach the skills a task needs, interrogate a research question, explain a criterion, point out that a conclusion does not evaluate anything, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any part of it, may not rewrite a paragraph into better English, and may not supply a structure the student then fills in without understanding it.

Proofreading sits in the grey area and is worth settling explicitly with the school, because practice varies. The safe version is that feedback names the kind of problem rather than fixing the instance: telling a student that three paragraphs begin with the same construction teaches them something, while rewriting the three paragraphs teaches them nothing and may cross a line. Schools differ on how much language support is acceptable, and the school's position is the one that counts.

We state this limit on every page rather than hiding it, because the competing pages in this search do not. Some of them offer, in plain terms, to produce assessed work. A family buying that is buying a risk that sits entirely with their child. The alternative is slower and it is the only version that leaves the student able to do the same thing alone in an examination hall.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus, not just the subject
process.description: Board, syllabus code where there is one, level or tier, and which components are still outstanding. For a Madinah family this is the step that saves the most time, because it determines whether the need is a subject specialist, a technique block or help with an internally assessed piece.

process.title: Send two pieces of marked work
process.description: A marked paper and a piece of written coursework tell a tutor more in ten minutes than a conversation does in an hour. They show whether marks are being lost on content, on structure or on the command term, and those three problems need three different approaches.

process.title: Meet a matched tutor in a free trial lesson
process.description: The trial is a working session, not a sales call. The tutor should name the components of the course, say where this student is losing marks and explain what the first month would cover. If that does not happen, ask for a different tutor rather than continuing.

process.title: Fix the slot to Madinah time
process.description: Agree a weekly time in Arabia Standard Time, in writing, and keep it even when the tutor's own country changes its clocks. Families with a long school run usually set the slot later than first planned, and a fixed slot survives a term far better than a flexible one.

process.title: Review against the components, not a feeling
process.description: After a month, check progress against the parts of the course: a paper type, a topic, a criterion on the internally assessed piece. Progress measured against components is visible. Progress measured against confidence is not, and it is where terms quietly disappear.

whyPoints.title: The specialist, not the nearest available person
whyPoints.description: Madinah's local pool of Higher Level specialists is small, and that is a staffing fact rather than a judgement on local schools. Choosing online means selecting a tutor who teaches that exact syllabus, in any time zone that overlaps with a Madinah evening, instead of whoever is free and close.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: A 0580 Extended candidate, a 4MA1 Higher candidate and an Analysis and Approaches Standard Level student need three different teachers. We match on the entry the school has actually made, which is why the first question we ask is the code and the tier rather than the year group.

whyPoints.title: The internally assessed components taken seriously
whyPoints.description: The exploration, the investigation, the Personal Project and the Extended Essay are where students lose points quietly and late. They get their own planning and their own deadlines, with feedback on the student's own drafts and nothing produced on their behalf.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Sunday-to-Thursday week
whyPoints.description: Slots are set against the real Saudi week and pinned to Arabia Standard Time, so a tutor's own clock change cannot move them. Families adjust timings for Ramadan and for the city's busier visitor periods, which is simpler to do when nobody has to travel.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot support
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no success percentages, no ratings, and no suggestion that any board or authority approves of us. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or ETEC. Rates quoted on this page are other companies' advertised numbers, named as such.

whyPoints.title: A tutor who travels with the family
whyPoints.description: Relocation inside the Kingdom is common, and a move costs a student their school, their teachers and their cohort at once. A tutor chosen for the syllabus rather than the district keeps working through the move, which is worth more at that moment than it was before it.

faqs.question: Does an IB Diploma earned by a student in Madinah need a Ministry of Education equivalency decision before a Saudi public university will consider it?
faqs.answer: Yes. A foreign or international secondary certificate needs an equivalency decision, mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. The IB Diploma is in the same position here as A Levels or an American high school diploma: well recognised internationally, and still requiring the decision domestically. Start the paperwork earlier than feels necessary, because it sits between results and application deadlines, and check whether the university you are applying to states a maximum age for the certificate it will accept. The Ministry's own published requirements are the only reliable source for what documents are needed.

faqs.question: Which certificate does the equivalency process actually look at, the IGCSE or the final secondary qualification?
faqs.answer: Equivalency concerns the secondary-stage leaving certificate, which for an international student means the IB Diploma, A Levels or an American high school diploma. IGCSE sits below that point: it is a two-year qualification taken around Grade 10 and it functions as a foundation and an entry requirement for the next stage, not as a school-leaving certificate. That is worth knowing before a family assumes a strong set of IGCSE grades completes the domestic pathway. Keep every certificate and transcript from both stages, because the application for the final decision usually asks for the full school record rather than the last document only.

faqs.question: Why do international-curriculum students in Madinah often find Tahsili harder than their own examinations?
faqs.answer: Because Tahsili follows the Saudi national curriculum. It covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, all subjects a Diploma or IGCSE student has studied, but the sequencing, the emphasis and the expected notation are those of a different syllabus. A student who has spent two years on Analysis and Approaches meets familiar mathematics presented in an unfamiliar order, with topics weighted differently from the ones their own papers rewarded. That is a translation problem as much as a content problem, and it is best treated as a separate block of preparation rather than as revision of what the student already did.

faqs.question: Is Qudurat sat in Arabic or in English, and does the choice matter for a child taught in English in Madinah?
faqs.answer: Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is available in Arabic and in English, and it measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content. For a student schooled in English the language of the test is a real decision rather than a formality, because the verbal section depends on reading fluency in the language chosen. The sensible approach is to try practice material in both languages and pick on evidence rather than on which language the family speaks at home. Registration details and the available sittings are published by the National Center for Assessment, and the family should confirm them directly.

faqs.question: How far ahead of a university application should Qudurat and Tahsili preparation start for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families plan for, and on a separate track from Diploma revision. Both tests have their own sittings and a student can usually sit more than once, which means the first attempt is most useful when it happens well before the final school year closes in on them. Putting a Tahsili block in the same weeks as internally assessed deadlines and paper practice produces a poor result in both. Work out the sitting windows from the National Center for Assessment, place preparation where the Diploma calendar is quietest, and treat the first attempt as a diagnostic rather than as the one that counts.

faqs.question: How do Diploma points turn into an offer from a university outside the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Most overseas universities make conditional offers against a total Diploma point score plus named Higher Level subject grades, and the subject conditions are often the harder part. An engineering offer may ask for a specific Higher Level mathematics route and a Higher Level physics grade, which means a subject decision made in the first Diploma year quietly fixes which offers are reachable two years later. Check each university's stated requirements rather than a general conversion table, because they differ by country and by course, and confirm which mathematics route a course expects before choosing between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Year 4 at a Madinah school that stops before Diploma level. What should we be building now?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is extra content. First, criterion literacy: the ability to read a published descriptor and write to the strand it names, which is exactly how Diploma internal assessment is marked. Second, investigation skills, because the Personal Project and every later internally assessed piece ask a student to narrow a question until it can be answered. Third, written explanation in English at length, which is the skill most often underdeveloped in a strong bilingual school. A student who arrives at Grade 11 with those three in place can be taught any subject; a student without them struggles in all of them.

faqs.question: We are moving to Madinah part-way through the first Diploma year. What does catching up actually involve?
faqs.answer: The first job is an audit rather than teaching. Establish which syllabus each subject follows, what has been covered, what internally assessed work has started and what the new school can timetable. Mid-course arrivals usually lose less content than they fear and more coursework progress than they expect, because an exploration or investigation begun elsewhere may not transfer cleanly. From there the catch-up is specific: the topics missed, the components restarted, and the Extended Essay question settled quickly if it is not already. One intensive diagnostic session on the student's own work will shorten the whole process.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start one-to-one support in the final two terms before a series?
faqs.answer: No, but what is achievable changes. In the last two terms the realistic work is technique, timing, past papers and the specific errors a student repeats, because there is no longer room to meet a topic for the first time and consolidate it. That is often enough to move a grade, since most students at this stage are losing marks they could already be earning. What a late start cannot do is rebuild a weak foundation across a whole Higher Level course. If internally assessed work is still outstanding, deal with that first, because it has a deadline and the papers do not move.

faqs.question: What does a Madinah family typically pay per hour for Higher Level science support, and who publishes those figures?
faqs.answer: Published rates for IB subject tutoring in the Kingdom start from around SAR 180 an hour and run to roughly SAR 200 to 220 for Higher Level or premium tracks, according to tutoring companies advertising their own prices. Marketplace guides quote 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects generally. Those are advertised figures rather than a market average, and none of them is what IB Gram charges. Treat them as the shape of the range, then ask any provider which part of their number comes from subject scarcity, which from marking experience, and whether marking work between lessons is included.

faqs.question: Why is Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level quoted above Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level when both lessons are one-to-one and online?
faqs.answer: Because the two jobs are not equally hard to staff. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level demands fluency in proof, calculus and function work, plus familiarity with what the papers reward in method marks, and the number of teachers who have genuinely taught that level is small. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is taught by many more people. Level adds to the same effect, with Higher Level above Standard Level and both above IGCSE. Scarcity rather than effort is what sets the price difference, which is why a quoted rate is worth interrogating: ask what makes this tutor scarce.

faqs.question: Is a small group class ever better value than one-to-one for Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deciding factor is whether the students share a problem. A group of four Extended-tier candidates who all lose marks on algebraic manipulation can be taught together efficiently. A group containing one Core-tier candidate, one student who has missed a term and one who needs examination timing practice is three lessons running at once, and everybody gets a third of a lesson. Group teaching also cannot work from one student's own marked papers, which is the fastest diagnostic available. For a specific, diagnosed weakness, one-to-one is usually the cheaper route to the same grade.

faqs.question: What should a Madinah parent ask for in the free trial lesson before committing to a term?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor to name the components of the course and say which one this student is losing marks in, using work you have sent in advance. Ask what the first month would cover, in order. Ask how work set between lessons gets marked and returned, and what you will receive after each session. On internally assessed work, ask explicitly what the tutor will and will not do. A tutor who answers those four questions concretely is worth a term. A tutor who talks about motivation and potential without naming a component has not read the work.

faqs.question: How is feedback on internally assessed work usually priced against a weekly subject lesson?
faqs.answer: Providers in this market handle it in three ways: inside the hourly rate, as a separate per-draft charge, or not at all. The question to ask is what happens between lessons, because reading a draft properly against published criteria and writing usable feedback takes longer than the lesson it follows. A rate that includes it and a rate that does not can look identical on a price list and differ substantially over a term. Ask how many drafts are covered, what the turnaround is, and what form the feedback takes, then compare the totals rather than the hourly numbers.

faqs.question: Can lessons pause during the long summer break without losing our Madinah evening slot?
faqs.answer: That depends on the arrangement, and it is worth agreeing before the term starts rather than in the week you want to stop. A slot held through a break has a value for the tutor, who is turning other students away to keep it, so some arrangements hold it and some release it. Ask the question directly: can the slot be reserved, for how long, and on what terms. Families who are travelling for several weeks often keep one session a fortnight instead, which holds both the slot and the habit without paying for a full term of lessons nobody attends.

faqs.question: What should we budget for a year of weekly support in one Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: Do the arithmetic from advertised rates rather than from a monthly figure. A weekly hour across three school terms is somewhere around thirty to thirty-four sessions once holidays and examination weeks are removed. At the advertised IB rates in this market, roughly SAR 180 to 220 an hour, that is the band a family should be planning for, before any intensive block before a series. Those are other companies' published numbers, not ours. Then ask what else is in or out: marking between lessons, feedback on drafts, written reports, and whether a missed lesson can be rescheduled.

madinah.closingHeading: Start with the component, not the subject
madinah.closingBody: If you are weighing up IB or IGCSE support in Madinah, the first move is free and it is not a lesson. Ask the school, in writing, which syllabus code and which level or tier your child is entered for in each subject, who teaches the Higher Level content, and who checks drafts of the internally assessed work. Take the answers, two pieces of your child's marked work, and the gap you can see. From there a trial lesson with a matched specialist will tell you in an hour whether the problem is content, structure or the command term. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Arabia Standard Time, around the Sunday-to-Thursday week.

makkah.tutorsIntro: These are the specialists Makkah families ask for most often: Diploma Programme sciences and Mathematics at Higher Level, and Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE in the two years before the June series. Each one teaches a syllabus rather than a subject, and each will tell you in the trial lesson which component is costing your child marks.

intro.heading: Start from where your child sits in the year, not from a price list
paragraphs: The useful first question is not what tuition costs. It is which week of the school year you are standing in. A Diploma Programme student halfway through the autumn term of DP1 needs the gap from the previous course closed before Higher Level topics stack on top of it. The same student in the spring term of DP2 needs mark-scheme habits and timed papers, because the content is already taught and the marks are now lost in the writing. An IGCSE candidate in Year 10 can still afford to build foundations; the same candidate eight weeks before the June series cannot. Those are three different plans, three different weekly loads, and three different prices. Start anywhere else and you buy the wrong thing.

Makkah adds a second constraint that most tutoring copy ignores. International-curriculum provision in the city is thin compared with Jeddah, roughly 80km west along the expressway, so a sizeable share of families here either enrol locally in schools following the national curriculum under Ministry of Education licensing, or commute, board or stay weekly towards the Jeddah corridor. Either route eats the evening. A family in Al Shawqiyah collecting a child from a school on the western side of the city is not free at five o'clock, and a family whose child comes home only on a Thursday has a weekend-shaped week rather than a weekday-shaped one.

Lessons here are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. That is not a compromise dressed up as a feature: it is the only way a Makkah family gets a Chemistry Higher Level specialist or a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level teacher at all, rather than whoever happens to be free within a thirty-minute drive. IB Gram does not run home visits in the Kingdom; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. What a Makkah family gets instead is a choice from a national pool of subject teachers, booked into a slot pinned to Makkah's own clock.

Money gets discussed plainly on this page because vagueness reads as evasion. Advertised rates in the Saudi market run from roughly SAR 35 an hour on budget IGCSE platforms to SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects, with IB subject listings commonly starting near SAR 180 and Higher Level tracks advertised around SAR 200 to 220. Those are rates vendors publish about themselves, not a market average and not our price. What actually moves a number is subject scarcity first, then examiner or marking experience, then level, then package length. A Mathematics Applications and Interpretation Standard Level tutor is easy to find. A Physics Higher Level specialist who has marked for the board is not.

The rest of this page works forward through the year. It sets out the calendar as a sequence of decisions, maps the Makkah school run against the earliest lesson slot each district can realistically hold, puts a Sunday-to-Thursday week next to a tutor's own working week in six countries, lays out the advertised SAR bands and who publishes them, covers how Hajj and Umrah seasons reshape a study week in this city, explains what local schools generally cannot staff, and finishes with the Ministry of Education equivalency route and the Qiyas tests almost nobody writes about honestly.
