sections.heading: What the Najran school run does to the hours a lesson can occupy
paragraphs: The scheduling problem in Najran is the opposite of the one in Riyadh. There is no hour-long crawl across a dense city; there is a long drive across open ground, often twice, often in two directions, and that consumes the part of the afternoon a tutor in another country would assume was free. A family in the palm belt along the wadi can spend the whole stretch between the end of school and the evening meal in the car, which makes any slot before dinner fictional however willingly it is agreed.

The school week runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Most tutoring copy aimed at this market is inherited from British or Indian pages and assumes the reverse, which is how a Saudi family ends up offered a Saturday morning as though it were a school night. The honest weekday window here opens after the drive home and the meal, and closes when a teenager stops taking anything in. That is a narrower window than it sounds, and it is the single most important thing to establish before a tutor is matched.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. A slot agreed with a tutor in a country that observes daylight saving will move by an hour twice a year unless it is pinned to Najran local time rather than to theirs. Pin it at the outset. The drift always lands mid-term and always collides with something, and re-agreeing a slot in week six of a term is harder than agreeing it properly in week one.

School days also shorten during Ramadan and evening routines change substantially. The workable approach is to agree the Ramadan slot in advance as a different arrangement rather than improvising each week, and to treat the period as a different shape of term rather than a disruption to be absorbed. Because Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, it drifts across the academic year and falls at a different point in the course each time.

sections.heading: Why distance, not ability, is the binding constraint in the south
paragraphs: It is worth being explicit about what the problem in Najran actually is, because the honest version is more useful than the flattering one. The students are not the issue and neither are the schools. The issue is that the density of specialist teachers in any subject at any level falls with distance from the three big markets — Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam cluster — and Najran sits a long way from all three. A family here cannot solve a Higher Level chemistry problem by asking the school for another teacher, because there is not another teacher.

That changes what a family should be shopping for. In a dense market the question is which of several available tutors is best. Here the question is whether anyone at all teaches this exact syllabus at this exact level and is free in the one usable hour of the evening. Those are different problems, and the second one is solved by widening the pool rather than by negotiating harder. Widening the pool is precisely what a video lesson does: it removes travel from the matching decision entirely.

The same logic explains why the comparison families here make is not online against a local tutor but online against relocation. Boarding a child in Jeddah, Riyadh or 'Asir is a serious and sometimes correct decision, with costs that are financial, familial and academic all at once. Keeping a student at home in Najran and buying a weekly hour with a subject specialist by video is a much smaller intervention, and for a single weak subject it is usually the proportionate one. For a student who needs a whole curriculum their school cannot deliver, it is not.

There is a third route that families in the south use more than families elsewhere: a school-delivered online programme, where the school is formally responsible for the course and the student studies from home. That works, with one consistent weakness. The weekly human contact with a subject specialist is thin, and coursework discipline suffers first. Outside support in that situation is less about teaching content and more about keeping the independent components on schedule and properly understood.

sections.heading: Command terms, mark schemes, and the gap between knowing and being paid
paragraphs: Every examination board publishes the vocabulary it marks by, and both the IB and Cambridge define their command terms formally in the subject guides. A student who has read that list and practised against it is operating with information most of their cohort does not use. This is not a trick or a technique in the pejorative sense; it is the stated basis on which marks are awarded, and ignoring it is the academic equivalent of not reading the question.

The practical method is unglamorous and works. Take a past paper and, before answering anything, underline the command verb in each question and write beside it how many marks are available. A two-mark state question gets two short clauses, not a paragraph. A six-mark evaluate question needs both sides and a judgement, and a student who gives only one side has capped themselves at about half the marks no matter how good that side is. Doing this for twenty questions changes how a student reads a paper permanently.

The second half of the method is marking their own work against the published scheme. This is the part students resist most and gain most from. A mark scheme does not reward understanding; it rewards specified content in a specified form, and seeing that in writing is more persuasive than hearing it from a teacher. After a student has awarded themselves zero for an answer they believed was good, the lesson lands in a way that no amount of advice replicates.

A tutor working at distance is well placed to do exactly this, because it is document work rather than classroom work. The student's script, the question paper and the mark scheme sit side by side on a shared screen, and the tutor annotates while the student explains their reasoning. Far from being a compromise on a classroom, it is a better setting for this particular job than a room where the student cannot see what the tutor is reading.

sections.heading: The science practical papers, where good students lose marks
paragraphs: The practical and data-handling papers are where Najran students most often underperform relative to their theory, and the reason is structural rather than personal. These papers do not test recall; they test the handling of apparatus, data and uncertainty, and that is learned by doing experiments repeatedly rather than by reading about them. A school with limited laboratory time, a small cohort and one science specialist cannot easily give a student the volume of practical work that makes those papers feel familiar.

The marks in question are specific and predictable. Reading a scale to the correct precision. Recording data to a consistent number of decimal places. Choosing axes that use the grid rather than squeezing the plot into a corner. Drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points. Calculating a gradient with the triangle shown. Identifying which variable was controlled and which was merely assumed constant. Stating a source of uncertainty that is actually relevant to the method rather than naming human error.

Most of that list can be taught and practised without a laboratory, which is the useful part for a family at a distance. Data sets from past papers, printed grids, and a tutor watching the student plot and analyse in real time covers the data-handling half almost completely. What genuinely needs the laboratory is the handling of apparatus, and that is the school's job; the sensible division of labour is for the tutor to take the data and analysis work and leave the bench work to the teacher who has the bench.

The same applies to the internal investigation. Most failures there happen before a single measurement is taken, at the design stage, where a student chooses a variable that cannot be controlled, a range too narrow to show a trend, or a method that produces too few data points to analyse. Those are conversations, not experiments, and a tutor is better placed to have them early than a teacher managing twenty projects in the same week.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment or Personal Project
paragraphs: This market contains providers whose advertising is deliberately vague about who produces the coursework, and a family searching from Najran will meet them within a page or two of results. The rule itself is not vague. Assessed work must be the student's own. A school that suspects otherwise has a malpractice process it is obliged to follow, and the consequences reach as far as the qualification itself. No saving in effort is worth that exposure.

What a tutor may legitimately do is a long list. They may help the student choose a research question that can actually be investigated in the time and with the resources available. They may explain what each published criterion rewards and in what proportion. They may read a draft and say which criterion is underserved and why. They may challenge the method, point out that the conclusion does not follow from the data, ask where a claim's evidence is, and teach the referencing convention. They may teach any content the student needs in order to do the work themselves.

What a tutor may never do is write, rewrite, redraft, edit in or supply any part of the submitted work, including data, analysis or a sentence of prose. The test a parent can apply without any technical knowledge is this: ask the student to explain, in their own words and without notes, why a particular paragraph or calculation is there. If they cannot, something has gone wrong, whatever anyone says about proofreading. Schools also keep records of supervision and require students to reflect on their own process, which makes substituted work more detectable than families tend to assume.

For the Personal Project in the final MYP year and for the Extended Essay, the school supervisor owns the formal process, including the recorded meetings. An outside tutor works alongside that and should be known to the supervisor rather than hidden from them. If a provider offers to handle a draft rather than discuss one, the correct response is to end the conversation; that offer is the thing the malpractice process exists to catch.

sections.heading: Choosing a tutor when there is no local parent network to ask
paragraphs: In Riyadh or Al Khobar a family can ask three other parents at the school gate who they use. In Najran there may be no other family in the city taking that subject at that level, which removes the one informal check most parents rely on. The substitute is not a review score or a testimonial; both are unverifiable and the gate for any claim should be whether you can test it yourself in a conversation.

Four claims are worth testing and each has a question that produces a checkable answer. On examining experience, ask which board, which component and which paper, then ask what the mark scheme does with a borderline answer on that component. On syllabus knowledge, ask what the Internal Assessment criteria are called in that subject and which one students most often underserve. On level, ask which Higher Level topics have no Standard Level equivalent. On local understanding, ask what a Sunday-to-Thursday week does to their availability. Specific answers come from recent teaching; general answers come from reading.

Then there is the category of claim nobody can support. A satisfaction percentage, a star rating, a count of successful students or a promised grade improvement without a sample size, a date and a stated method is marketing rather than evidence, and the confident version should increase your scepticism rather than your confidence. The honest answer to how much a child will improve is a description of what will be measured, against what baseline, and on what date — not a number.

The most reliable substitute for a parent network is a diagnostic in writing. A tutor who, after one session with a marked script, can tell you in a paragraph which of the four faults above is costing the marks and what they intend to do about it has demonstrated the thing you were trying to verify. One who produces encouragement has not. That test costs one free session and is worth more than any amount of testimonial.

sections.heading: The year counted backwards from the examination series
paragraphs: Families in the south lose more to timing than to teaching, because the components that decide a grade are the ones with the earliest deadlines and the least supervision. Counting backwards from the series rather than forwards from today puts those deadlines in the right order, and the exercise takes twenty minutes with the school's own calendar in front of you.

Three fixed points anchor the year. The examination series itself: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series, which is the main sitting for Saudi candidates, and a November series used for resits and November-entry candidates. The entry window, which closes several months before the papers and is handled by the school's examinations officer, not by the family. And the internal deadlines for assessed coursework, which the school sets and which almost always fall earlier than students expect — before the final run of revision begins, not after it.

Working backwards, the pattern that works looks like this. Internal Assessment and project work should be substantially finished a full term before the papers, because a student revising and drafting simultaneously does both badly. Intensive paper work belongs in the final eight to ten weeks, not earlier, since timed practice on content not yet taught teaches discouragement. Content repair belongs in the term before that, which is the part families most often leave too late. And the decision about whether a subject should be taken at Higher or Standard Level belongs earlier still.

For a resit through the November series the arithmetic is tighter and the discipline has to be better: the gap between results and the next entry window is short, and a student who waits for certainty before starting has lost half the available preparation time. Confirm the entry route with the examinations officer first, because the arrangements for a candidate outside the main cities need checking rather than assuming.

process.title: Send one marked script, not a report card
process.description: The most useful thing a Najran family can send first is a recent marked paper with the mark scheme if you have it. A report card tells a tutor the grade; a script tells them which of the four faults is costing it. Add the subject and level exactly as the school writes them, and the board.

process.title: Tell us the one hour that is genuinely free
process.description: Not the hour you would like, the hour that survives the school run and the evening meal. Distance decides this in Najran more than anywhere else in the Kingdom, and a slot that looks workable on paper and collapses in week three wastes more time than it saves. Pin it to local time.

process.title: Take a free diagnostic session
process.description: A specialist reads the script with the student, identifies the recurring fault, and writes a short paragraph naming it and what they propose to do. You should finish knowing something specific you did not know before. If what comes back is encouragement rather than diagnosis, ask to meet someone else.

process.title: Fix the plan to the series, not to the month
process.description: Work backwards from the June or November series: coursework finished a term before the papers, content repair before that, timed papers in the last eight to ten weeks. Writing the sequence down once prevents the commonest southern-province failure, which is revising and drafting at the same time.

process.title: Review on the recurring-error list
process.description: The measure of progress is whether the named fault still appears in marked work. That is a checkable question with a yes or no answer, unlike whether the student seems more confident. Review it on a date fixed at the start, and change the plan or the tutor if the answer is still yes.

whyPoints.title: Distance stops being the constraint
whyPoints.description: The binding problem in Najran is that the nearest specialist in a scarce subject may be several hundred kilometres away. A live video session removes travel from the matching decision, so a student here is matched by syllabus and level to the same pool a student in Riyadh chooses from.

whyPoints.title: The fault gets named before anything is taught
whyPoints.description: Sessions start from a marked script and the published mark scheme, because a repeatable error is the cheapest thing to fix and the hardest thing to find without a specialist reading the paper. Naming the fault in writing also gives you something to review against later.

whyPoints.title: Timed to a long school run, not to a city commute
whyPoints.description: Slots are agreed around the hour that genuinely survives the drive home and the evening meal, Sunday to Thursday, pinned to Najran local time so that a tutor abroad changing their clocks does not drag the session an hour sideways mid-term.

whyPoints.title: Coursework questioned, never written
whyPoints.description: A tutor reads the student's own Internal Assessment, exploration, Extended Essay or Personal Project, maps it against the published criteria and asks what an examiner would ask. They do not draft, redraft, edit in or supply content. That boundary is not negotiable and not a formality.

whyPoints.title: Claims you can test in a conversation
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no satisfaction figures, no ratings. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ministry of Education, the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no affiliation with any school named on this page.

whyPoints.title: A straight answer when there is no match
whyPoints.description: A scarce Higher Level subject in a narrow evening hour sometimes has nobody free. We say so and offer a different hour, a wait, or a different starting subject, rather than putting a lower-level teacher in front of the student and letting you find out in week three.

faqs.question: Which Biology HL topics most often need teaching again from outside school?
faqs.answer: The ones that are conceptually dense and get taught late: nucleic acids and protein synthesis, metabolism and the detail of respiration and photosynthesis, and the plant and animal physiology options where the Higher Level treatment goes well past the Standard Level version. Genetics is the other recurring one, because a student who is shaky on the basic crosses cannot do the linked-gene and chi-squared work that follows. None of these are hard to teach; they are hard to fit into a timetable that has already used its hours on earlier topics.

faqs.question: Why do students lose marks on the Chemistry practical paper when their theory is sound?
faqs.answer: Because that paper assesses a different skill. It rewards reading a scale to the right precision, recording data consistently, choosing sensible axes, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points, and identifying a source of uncertainty that is genuinely part of the method. None of that is examined in the theory papers, and none of it is learned by reading. The fix is volume: past-paper data sets worked through with someone watching the plotting and the analysis, which is straightforward to do in a video session with a shared screen.

faqs.question: Where does weak algebra from Year 10 show up later in Mathematics AI SL?
faqs.answer: In three predictable places. Rearranging a formula to make a different variable the subject, which appears throughout the modelling topics. Handling indices and logarithms when exponential models arrive. And solving simultaneous equations in a context where the calculator will not do the setting-up for you. Students often get through the early part of the course on calculator fluency and then stall, which reads as a new difficulty but is an old one surfacing. Two or three sessions on manipulation alone usually unblocks the whole of the modelling work.

faqs.question: What makes a six-mark Geography answer score full marks rather than four?
faqs.answer: A line of argument with named, located evidence attached to it, and a judgement at the end if the command term asks for one. Four-mark answers are usually correct and general: they describe a process accurately without anchoring it to a place. Full-mark answers do the same thing with a specific named example doing the specific thing under discussion. Students lose the last two marks by listing case studies rather than using them, which is a structural habit rather than a knowledge gap and takes about two sessions to change.

faqs.question: Which definitions in IGCSE Biology are examined most strictly?
faqs.answer: The transport and exchange definitions are the strictest: diffusion, osmosis and active transport each have examined wording where a sensible paraphrase earns nothing. The characteristics of living organisms, the definitions around enzymes and denaturation, and the terminology of inheritance are close behind. These are a small amount of material relative to the marks they protect, which makes them the highest-return memorisation in the course. Learning them as written and then being tested cold on them a few minutes a week is all that is required.

faqs.question: How should a student revise Arabic A: Language and Literature differently from English B?
faqs.answer: They are different kinds of course and reward different preparation. Arabic A is a first-language course assessed on analysis of how texts produce their effects, so revision means re-reading set works with an analytical framework and practising comparison, not vocabulary building. English B is a language-acquisition course where marks go to task fulfilment, register and the right text type, so revision means practising text types against prompts and checking every element of the task was addressed. A student who revises both the same way typically underperforms in Arabic A.

faqs.question: How does a family in Najran check a tutor's subject specialism without another parent to ask?
faqs.answer: By asking questions whose answers can only come from recent teaching. Which Higher Level topics have no Standard Level equivalent in this subject? What are the Internal Assessment criteria called, and which one do students underserve? What does the mark scheme do with a borderline extended response? Then ask for a free diagnostic session and judge the written paragraph that comes out of it. A tutor who can name the recurring fault in a marked script has demonstrated the specialism; one who returns encouragement has not.

faqs.question: Should a student in a school with only one science teacher have a serving teacher as their tutor?
faqs.answer: It helps but it is not the deciding factor. A serving teacher knows the current subject guide and the rhythm of a school year, which shows up in how they sequence coursework. A full-time tutor usually has more marked scripts across more boards in front of them, which shows up in how fast they name a fault. Either can be excellent. What matters more is whether they teach this syllabus at this level now, and whether they mark written work between sessions rather than only teaching during them.

faqs.question: What does a first written report from a tutor need to contain to be worth reading?
faqs.answer: Four things. What was looked at, named specifically: which paper, which component, which draft. What the recurring fault is, in a sentence a parent can repeat. What will be done about it, as a sequence rather than an intention. And what the student has been asked to do before the next session. A report that describes attitude and effort tells you nothing you could not see at home. Ask for the specific version; a specialist can produce it in five minutes because they already know the answer.

faqs.question: How many students can one tutor carry before the marking quality drops?
faqs.answer: The honest limit is set by the marking rather than the teaching. Reading a student's written work properly against a mark scheme takes a meaningful amount of time per week, and a tutor carrying too many students starts teaching from memory of the last session rather than from what the student actually wrote. The signal to watch is not a number they quote but whether work comes back marked before the next lesson. When it starts arriving late or unannotated, the load is too high.

faqs.question: Can a family in Najran choose the gender of the tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes. One-to-one online lessons make this a straightforward preference to state rather than a logistical problem, because the pool is national rather than limited to whoever lives nearby, and no one is travelling to a home. Tell us at the enquiry stage along with the subject, the level and the hour you need, and the match is made within that constraint. It is a common request and it does not narrow the subject pool anything like as much as families expect.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with a Biology Internal Assessment draft, and what may they never do?
faqs.answer: They may help the student test whether the chosen independent variable can actually be controlled and whether the range will show a trend, explain what each published criterion rewards, read the draft and say which criterion is underserved, challenge whether the conclusion follows from the data, and teach any biology the student needs. They may never write, rewrite, redraft or edit any part of it, supply data, or produce the analysis. If the finished investigation contains a sentence the student cannot explain without notes, the line has been crossed.

faqs.question: How is the Personal Project supervised when the school has no specialist in the chosen subject?
faqs.answer: The supervisor's role in the Personal Project is process rather than subject expertise: they oversee the planning, the recorded meetings and the process journal, and they confirm the work is the student's own. A supervisor who knows nothing about the chosen topic can still do that job properly. What tends to go wrong is the journal discipline, not the content. An outside tutor can help the student keep the journal honest and current and can coach against the criteria, without contributing to the product itself.

faqs.question: What counts as academic misconduct on an Extended Essay, and how do schools detect it?
faqs.answer: Submitting work that is not the student's own, in whole or in part, including unattributed text, text produced by someone else and unacknowledged assistance that goes beyond supervision. Detection is not only software. Supervisors hold recorded meetings, students complete reflections on their own process, and a mismatch between a student's demonstrated ability and a submitted text is visible to an experienced reader. If a school suspects malpractice it is obliged to follow a formal process, and the consequences can extend to the qualification.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose an investigable variable for a science Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the most valuable hours a tutor spends, because most weak investigations are already lost at the design stage. The useful conversation tests whether the independent variable can be changed in controlled steps, whether the range is wide enough to produce a trend, whether enough data points can be collected in the time available, and whether the dependent variable can be measured with the apparatus the school actually has. The student chooses; the tutor asks the questions that expose a design that will not work.

faqs.question: How does a student keep a record proving an Extended Essay is their own work?
faqs.answer: By using the process the school already requires rather than inventing one. Keep the recorded supervision meetings and the reflections current rather than writing them at the end. Keep dated drafts, so the development of the argument is visible. Keep a reading log with notes in the student's own words, which also makes the referencing easier. If an outside tutor is involved, note that they reviewed a draft and gave feedback. A visible trail protects a student who has done the work properly.

najran.closingHeading: If your child is studying in Najran and a grade will not move
najran.closingBody: Find the most recent marked paper, note the subject and level exactly as the school writes them, and decide which hour of the evening genuinely survives the school run. Send those three things and a subject specialist will read the script with your child in a free diagnostic session, live over video, and write down which recurring fault is costing the marks and what they propose to do about it. Distance is the one problem in the south that a video call actually solves, and it is the reason a student in Najran can work with the same specialist a student in Riyadh would.

neom.tutorsIntro: The specialists NEOM families ask for are the ones a new school rarely has two of: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics, Chemistry, and Economics or Geography for students who arrived part-way through a course. Each tutor teaches one board and one level properly rather than several approximately, and each starts by reading your child's last marked script.

intro.heading: What a NEOM family is really choosing between
paragraphs: Set the options side by side before looking at any price. A family here weighing extra academic support has roughly five choices. The school's own after-hours help, which depends entirely on whether the subject teacher has capacity. A private tutor living within reach, where the pool in this corner of Tabuk Province is small and rarely subject-specific. A group centre in a larger town, which means travel and a shared pace. Self-study from past papers, which works for an organised student in a subject they already understand. Or one-to-one lessons over live video with a tutor chosen for the exact syllabus and level. This page compares those honestly, including where the online route is the wrong answer.

The thing that makes NEOM different from Riyadh or the Dammam cluster is not distance alone. It is that the school community is new. A school building a cohort from a standing start has one teacher per subject in most subjects and sometimes one teacher across two. That is not a criticism of anybody; it is arithmetic. The consequence for a parent is specific and predictable: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics at Higher Level, Chemistry at Higher Level and the second modern language are the places where a new school most often has no depth behind the one teacher who covers them. If that teacher is excellent, the student is fine. If that teacher leaves, or carries two year groups, or has never taught the Higher Level extension before, the family is on its own.

The second thing that shapes support here is how many students arrived mid-course. A high share of NEOM households moved in while a child was already inside DP1, DP2 or IGCSE Year 11, from a British school, an American one, a national curriculum or another IB school running a different subject order. Mid-course arrivals do not need general tutoring. They need a specific inventory of what transferred and what did not, and then four weeks of targeted work on the gap, which is a different purchase from a year of weekly lessons.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not run home visits in the Kingdom; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. On a page about NEOM that restriction barely matters, because the in-home option here is thin on its own terms: a family that insists on someone in the room is choosing from a handful of people, almost none of whom will have taught the specific Higher Level course the student is sitting. Online delivery is not the compromise in this market. It is the only route to a specialist.

Money is set out plainly further down. Advertised rates in the Saudi market run from roughly SAR 35 an hour on budget IGCSE platforms up to SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects, with IB listings commonly starting near SAR 180. Those are figures vendors publish about themselves, not a market average and not our price. Scarcity drives them more than anything else, which is exactly why a family in a new school market should expect to pay for specialism rather than for proximity. The rest of the page works through the comparison in detail: the options, the staffing pattern, the mid-course transfer, the weekly shape, the money, the university paperwork, and what to ask a tutor before agreeing to anything.

neom.programmesIntro: Four programmes cover almost every NEOM enquiry, and the useful question about each one is not what it contains but what a newly built school can realistically deliver of it. Programme structure is fixed by the board; depth of staffing is local, and depth is what decides whether a family needs outside help.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Level subjects, three at Standard Level, and a core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Written papers are sat in the May session; internally assessed work is marked in school and moderated by the board. The structural trap for a small cohort is subject combination: a school with one science teacher may be unable to timetable Physics and Chemistry both at Higher Level, so the student's combination gets decided by staffing rather than by their university plans.
programmes.countryNote: In NEOM the practical question to put to a school is which Higher Level subjects actually ran with the last cohort, and who taught them. A school that has run the Diploma for one or two years has not yet seen a full cycle of moderation feedback in every subject, so a family should expect to supply the depth in the one or two subjects that matter most for the course ahead.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria, each with its own strands and descriptors, ending with the Personal Project. The criteria reward planning, process and reflection rather than a single right answer, and a student arriving from an examination-led system usually reads the criteria as vague until somebody shows them the descriptors line by line. That showing is a teaching job, and it transfers directly into Diploma Internal Assessment work two years later.
programmes.countryNote: The Middle Years Programme is where NEOM families most often notice a thin bench, because non-specialists cover more lessons at this stage in any new school. A Year 9 student taught science by a generalist can still look fine on reports and arrive at the Diploma without the laboratory habits the Internal Assessment assumes.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined almost entirely by external written papers, with Core and Extended tiers in several Cambridge subjects and a tier ceiling on the grade available. Candidates in the Kingdom are entered for the June series as the main sitting, with the November series used for resits and November-entry candidates. Cambridge also runs a February and March series, but that series is sat only in India, so a NEOM family should plan around June and November and nothing else.
programmes.countryNote: Tier decisions are the ones to watch here. A new school under pressure to show results sometimes enters cautiously, and a Core entry caps the grade however well the student performs. Ask what tier the school intends, on what evidence, and when the entry is confirmed, because the examinations officer's deadline is the point after which it cannot be changed.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than separate subjects, finishing with the Exhibition. No external examinations, which means problems here are invisible until much later. The two that matter are arithmetic fluency and written English at length. A child who reaches Year 7 without secure fractions and place value will meet the consequence in Year 9 algebra, and a child who has never written five hundred words to a deadline will meet it in the Middle Years Programme.
programmes.countryNote: Primary support for a NEOM family is usually a short, defined block rather than an open arrangement: a term of number work, or writing stamina before an assessment for a school elsewhere. Receiving schools set their own entrance assessments, so ask the destination school what it tests before buying lessons aimed at it.

neom.subjectsIntro: The grid below is ordered by how often a NEOM family cannot cover the subject locally, not by how popular it is. The notes name what the subject assesses and the specific thing a transferring or under-supported student tends to be missing, because that is what a first month of lessons has to fix.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-first route, and the one most engineering and physical science degrees expect. Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers and harder calculus, with an investigative Paper 3 that cannot be revised for by memorising methods. The marks live in justification: an answer with no visible reasoning forfeits method marks, and transferring students from systems that only marked final answers lose heavily here until the habit is retrained.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, fields and energy, with Higher Level extending into rotational motion and quantum topics. The usual bottleneck is algebraic confidence rather than physics: students who cannot rearrange and substitute fluently lose marks on questions they understand conceptually. The internally assessed investigation needs a measurable, controllable variable chosen early, and a weak research question caps the achievable mark whatever the write-up does.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure, bonding, energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms, with Higher Level items routinely combining two topics in a single question. Students who revised topic by topic stall on those. Definitions are marked strictly and loose wording costs marks that content knowledge cannot recover, which is why a tutor who has read mark schemes is worth more here than one who simply knows chemistry well.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. Chosen by students expecting an easier course, it takes most of them by surprise in the statistics strands, where interpretation rather than calculation is assessed. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding modelling, and Paper 3 pays for explaining what a model fails to capture.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy content examined through precise command terms, which is the gap between what a student knows and what the scheme pays for. Outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each demand a different answer shape. Data-based questions need practice against real schemes rather than textbook summaries, and the statistical reasoning in the course is assessed more directly than most arriving students expect.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course that satisfies both the sciences and the individuals and societies requirement, which makes it useful for a student whose subject combination has been squeezed by timetabling. It is not a soft option: the assessment rewards systems reasoning, named case studies and evaluation of competing value positions, and students who treat it as general knowledge score poorly.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline decides the grade more than content recall does. Unlabelled axes, curves without shift arrows and evaluation that restates rather than weighs are where the marks go. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and an extra paper, and each internally assessed commentary must use a genuinely recent article and a different section of the syllabus from the others.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Often taught by a non-specialist in a small school, and the one subject where that shows up fastest in the Internal Assessment. Fieldwork has to generate the student's own primary data, and a question designed without a method in mind cannot be rescued later. Paper marks turn on case-study specificity: named places, figures and processes, rather than general description.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, a comparative essay, the individual oral, and an additional essay at Higher Level. Students arriving from systems that rewarded summary have to be taught to argue from the text itself. The individual oral needs a global issue and two extracts chosen early in the course; left to the final term it becomes the weakest line on the transcript.

subjects.name: Language B: French and Spanish
subjects.description: The subject a new school most often cannot staff at all, leaving students on a supervised self-taught route. Assessment covers listening, reading, writing and two speaking components, and the productive skills are the ones that cannot be self-taught from a textbook. A weekly speaking partner who marks against the published criteria is usually the minimum viable arrangement.

neom.igcseSubjectsIntro: A good share of NEOM students are inside a British-curriculum route rather than an IB one, so the IGCSE grid sits alongside the Diploma subjects. The three things to settle before lessons begin are the board, the tier, and whether the school has entered the student for the paper they have actually been taught.

igcseSubjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Tier choice caps the grade, so it must rest on evidence from timed papers rather than on how confident the student feels. Extended papers assume fluent algebra, and most lost marks sit in multi-step questions where one early slip carries through. Cambridge and Edexcel differ in paper structure and in how much is calculator-free, which changes how practice should be organised.

igcseSubjects.name: IGCSE Coordinated and Combined Sciences
igcseSubjects.description: The route many small schools use because it needs fewer specialist teachers, and the one that most often surprises families later: a combined award covers less of each science than the separate papers, which matters if the student intends Higher Level sciences in the Diploma. Check what the school has entered before assuming the route is open.

igcseSubjects.name: IGCSE Physics
igcseSubjects.description: Unit conversion and significant figures quietly remove marks across every paper, more than formula recall does. Where the school enters for the practical paper, credit goes to students who have drawn and criticised real graphs rather than read about them. Extended questions frequently ask for an explanation and receive a description, which scores part marks at best.

igcseSubjects.name: IGCSE Geography
igcseSubjects.description: Case-study specificity and command-term discipline carry the paper, and the coursework or alternative-to-coursework route depends on what the school offers. Students taught by a non-specialist tend to arrive with general description and no named examples, which is a fixable problem but not a quick one; it needs rebuilding across a term rather than cramming.

igcseSubjects.name: IGCSE Business Studies
igcseSubjects.description: Application rather than recall. Marks come from choosing the right tool for the question asked and justifying a recommendation against the case material, not from defining terms correctly. Data-response questions are where students who have only learned definitions come unstuck, and the fix is practice against real mark schemes with the reasoning made visible.

igcseSubjects.name: IGCSE English as a Second Language
igcseSubjects.description: Distinct from First Language English, and families regularly discover the difference too late. This specification assesses comprehension, summary and controlled writing against a register the mark scheme defines tightly. Confirm which qualification the school has entered the student for before buying support, because preparing for the wrong one wastes a year of effort.

neom.regionsTitle: Communities across NEOM and the north-west, and what each means for a weekly lesson
neom.regionsIntro: NEOM sits on the Gulf of Aqaba in the Kingdom's north-west corner, inside Tabuk Province, and the households inside it are spread across sites rather than concentrated in one city grid. The notes below are about what each setting does to a weekly lesson: the travel it involves, the household rhythm, and where the nearest subject specialist realistically is.

regions.name: Sharma and the coastal communities
regions.note: The residential coast on the Gulf of Aqaba, served by NEOM Bay Airport. Households here are largely relocated professionals on fixed rotations, which makes a weekly evening slot easy to hold but a travel week disruptive. Agree in advance how rotation weeks are handled rather than cancelling as they arrive.

regions.name: Oxagon and Duba
regions.note: The industrial port area on the Red Sea coast south of the main NEOM sites. Shift patterns rather than school runs shape the evening here, and a parent on shift is often unavailable at the hour the lesson runs. Written notes after each session matter more for these households than for most.

regions.name: Trojena and the mountain sites
regions.note: Higher ground inland from the coast in the Sarawat range. Journeys to anything resembling a tuition centre are measured in hours, not minutes, so the comparison between online and in-person support is not close for a family based here. Connectivity is the only practical requirement.

regions.name: Magna and the northern coast
regions.note: Coastal sites north towards the head of the Gulf of Aqaba. Families here are typically small in number and spread thinly, which means no viable group class in the subject a particular student needs. One-to-one is the only format that matches a specific syllabus at a specific level.

regions.name: Haql and the border strip
regions.note: The far north-west, close to the Jordanian border. Households here sometimes have cross-border family arrangements, and the Jordanian week runs Friday and Saturday as its weekend while the Kingdom's school week runs Sunday to Thursday. Pin the lesson to Arabia Standard Time to stop the slot drifting.

regions.name: Tabuk city
regions.note: The provincial capital inland to the east, and the nearest place with an established schooling market. Some NEOM families keep a connection there, and a few older students board or stay weekly. That produces a weekend-shaped study week, with Friday or Saturday blocks rather than school-night evenings.

regions.name: Al Bad' and the inland road
regions.note: Along the inland route between the coast and Tabuk. Travel times vary with the road rather than with traffic, so the usual urban problem of an unpredictable school run is replaced by long but reliable journeys. Fixed slots hold well here once the term's pattern is set.

regions.name: Rotational and fly-in households
regions.note: A real category rather than a place. Where one parent works a rotation, the student's week changes shape every few weeks. The arrangement that survives is a slot agreed with the student rather than with the travelling parent, plus a short written note after each lesson that the absent parent can read later.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the Red Sea coast, the nearest deep provision
schoolClusters.note: For families comparing where established IB and Cambridge teaching actually sits, the nearest concentration on this coast is far to the south. Jeddah runs as a long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, and The KAUST School serves the university campus community at Thuwal. Students we support attend schools of these kinds, and families relocating into NEOM frequently arrive from them.

schoolClusters.city: Riyadh, where Diploma choice is widest
schoolClusters.note: Riyadh carries the broadest Diploma provision in the Kingdom, which is why a NEOM family weighing an internal move usually compares against it. The relevant question is not how many schools exist but whether a specific Higher Level combination is timetabled at the destination school, because that is what a transferring student's course depends on.

schoolClusters.city: The Eastern Province cluster, for transfers inside the Kingdom
schoolClusters.note: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran behave as a single school market, with families living in one city and attending school in another, and the International Schools Group runs several campuses across it. Not every campus offers the Diploma, so confirm the programme and the subject before treating a transfer as straightforward.

neom.schoolDisclaimer: These schools are named only to describe where established provision sits around the Kingdom; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them and claims none.
neom.modesIntro: Four arrangements cover nearly everything we are asked for here, and the right one follows from the student's situation rather than the subject. A mid-course arrival, a student under-supported in one subject, and a candidate eight weeks from a series need three different shapes of week.

modes.title: One subject, one specialist, one evening
modes.description: The standard arrangement and the one that produces the steadiest movement over a year. Sixty or ninety minutes a week with the same tutor, on a slot recorded in Arabia Standard Time so it survives a tutor's own clock change. Ninety minutes suits a Higher Level science, where a full past-paper question plus feedback will not fit inside an hour without rushing one of them.
bullets: Same tutor and same slot, agreed for the whole term
Written work set, marked, and returned before the next session
A short factual note to the parent after every lesson
Reviewed properly at the end of each term

modes.title: Transfer inventory and catch-up block
modes.description: Built for a student who arrived part-way through DP1, DP2 or IGCSE Year 11. The first session is an inventory rather than a lesson: what the previous course covered, what the new one assumes, and which internally assessed work has to be started from scratch. The block that follows targets the gap for a defined number of weeks and then stops, rather than rolling into open-ended tuition.
bullets: A written gap inventory after the first session
A fixed number of weeks with a defined endpoint
Internally assessed work sequenced against the school's deadlines
Handover notes the student can take to their school teacher

modes.title: Two Higher Level subjects, two specialists
modes.description: Common from the spring term of DP1, when two Higher Level courses are both losing marks. Two specialists on two separate evenings beats one tutor covering both, and they work to one shared written plan so the student is never asked to choose between conflicting targets. Separate evenings matter: two hours back to back reliably produces one useful hour.

modes.title: Component clinic before a series
modes.description: A short dense block in the final weeks, organised by paper rather than by topic. The first session diagnoses which component is losing the most marks; everything after it attacks that component under exam timing. This only works if the content was taught earlier in the year, and specialist availability thins sharply as a series approaches, so it has to be booked well ahead.

sections.heading: Five options, set side by side
paragraphs: A family in NEOM looking for academic support is not choosing between good and bad. They are choosing between five imperfect options with different failure modes, and the honest comparison is more useful than a sales pitch for any one of them. The school's own help is free and closest to the student's actual classwork, but it depends on a teacher who already has a full timetable, and in a small cohort that teacher may be the same person the student is struggling with. A nearby private tutor gives a person in the room, but the pool in this part of Tabuk Province is small and rarely holds a specialist in the exact course and level.

A group centre in a larger town delivers structure and a lower cost per hour, at the price of travel and a shared pace that cannot follow one student's specific gap. Self-study from past papers and published mark schemes is genuinely effective and genuinely free, and it is the right answer for an organised student in a subject they understand but have not practised. It fails where the student cannot see why their own answer lost marks, which is precisely the situation most families are in when they start looking.

One-to-one lessons over live video solve the matching problem and nothing else. They give access to a teacher chosen for the board, the subject and the level, which in a new school market is the only realistic way to reach one. They do not fix motivation, they do not replace classroom teaching, and they do not help a student who will not do written work between sessions. Any provider that tells you otherwise is selling rather than advising.

Read the table below as a diagnostic rather than a recommendation. If the honest answer for your situation is the school's own support plus a disciplined past-paper routine, that is a good answer and it costs nothing. The case for paying for a specialist is strongest where the subject is scarce, the level is Higher, the component is assessed in a particular way, or the student arrived part-way through the course.

sections.heading: How a new school market is staffed, and which subjects have no local depth
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Those processes govern the school as an institution. Neither of them puts a second Physics teacher in a building, and that is where a family's real problem usually sits. A newly established school can be well run, properly evaluated, and still have exactly one person capable of teaching Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.

The pattern repeats in every new international school market, and it is predictable enough to plan around. Subjects with large teaching pools get covered twice over: English, Biology, Business Management, Mathematics at Standard Level. Subjects with small pools get covered once: Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Computer Science. Subjects with tiny pools often get covered not at all, and the school offers them through a supervised self-taught route instead, which is standard practice for a second modern language and sometimes for Music or Visual Arts at Higher Level.

What a parent sees is rarely labelled as a staffing issue. It looks like a topic covered quickly, a practical that did not happen, an Internal Assessment brief issued late, or a teacher who answers a question about Paper 3 by promising to check. None of those is evidence of a bad teacher. All of them are evidence of a thin bench, and the fix is to supply depth from outside in the one or two subjects that matter most for the student's intended course, rather than to spread support thinly across six.

Before enrolling, and again before Diploma subject choices are confirmed, put three questions to the school in writing. Which Higher Level subjects ran with the last cohort? Who taught them, and have they taught the Higher Level extension before? What happens to the subject if that teacher leaves mid-course? A school confident in its answers will give them. The answers also tell a family exactly where to spend tutoring money.

sections.heading: Arriving part-way through a course, which is the normal case here
paragraphs: A high proportion of NEOM students began their current course somewhere else. That is the defining feature of a school community built quickly, and it changes what support should be. A mid-course arrival does not need a year of weekly lessons. They need somebody to establish, in one session, exactly what transferred and what did not, and then to close the gap in a defined number of weeks before it compounds.

The inventory is the part that gets skipped. A student moving from a British school into DP1 has usually met the content but not the command terms, the Internal Assessment format or the Theory of Knowledge habit of mind. A student moving from an American curriculum has often met broader content at shallower depth, so the Higher Level science extension is the gap rather than the basics. A student moving between two IB schools may have covered the same syllabus in a different order, which means one or two whole topics are missing while everything else is secure. Those are three different problems and they are not interchangeable.

Internally assessed work is where a mid-course move costs the most. An Internal Assessment started at the previous school may not fit the new school's timetable or supervisor arrangements, and in some cases has to be restarted. Work out in the first fortnight which pieces are salvageable, which need restarting, and what the school's own deadlines are, because a restarted investigation needs lab or fieldwork access that has to be booked rather than assumed.

The last thing to settle is the predicted grade. A student who arrives in DP2 has little classroom evidence at the new school, and predicted grades rest on evidence. Getting assessed work in early, under proper conditions, gives the school something to predict from. Leaving it late produces a cautious prediction, and a cautious prediction is harder to argue with than a low mock result.

sections.heading: Distance, and why it settles the argument rather than complicating it
paragraphs: In Riyadh or the Eastern Province cluster, online and in-person tuition are genuinely competing options and a family can reasonably prefer either. In the Kingdom's north-west corner they are not competing. The nearest established schooling market is Tabuk city inland to the east; the nearest concentration of experienced IB and Cambridge teaching on this coast is far to the south. A family here is not weighing a thirty-minute drive against a video call. They are weighing a specialist against no specialist.

That makes the usual objections to online teaching easy to test rather than argue about. The objection that a student concentrates less on screen is real for some students and false for others, and a trial lesson settles it in an hour. The objection that practical subjects cannot be taught remotely is partly true: a tutor cannot run a titration for a student. What a tutor can do is design the investigation, interrogate the method, teach the uncertainty treatment and mark the write-up against the criteria, which is where almost all the marks sit.

There is a further advantage that families only notice later. A tutor matched online stays with the student through a move. Households in this region move: between sites, to another city in the Kingdom, or out of the country entirely. A local arrangement ends at the gate. An online arrangement follows the student, which matters most in the middle of a two-year course when continuity is worth more than convenience.

The honest limitation is bandwidth and household environment rather than geography. A shared connection carrying several devices in the evening degrades a video lesson, and a student working in a busy room will concentrate less wherever the tutor is sitting. Both are solvable with a wired connection, headphones and an agreed quiet hour, and both are worth sorting before the first paid lesson rather than after the third disappointing one.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, and what a workable weekly shape looks like
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Almost all tutoring material in this market was adapted from British or Indian copy and quietly assumes a Monday-to-Friday week, which is why so many arrangements collapse in the second month. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not observe daylight saving, so any slot agreed with a tutor whose own country changes its clocks will move twice a year unless it is recorded in Saudi local time from the start.

The shape of the week matters more than the number of hours in it. One ninety-minute session with marked written work in between beats three scattered half-hours, because a session long enough to sit a full past-paper question and then unpick it is the smallest useful unit in a Higher Level science. Two subjects belong on two separate evenings. A rotational household should put the slot on a day the travelling parent is usually away, not on the day they are home, so that the lesson does not compete with family time.

Friday and Saturday sessions are available and are sometimes the better arrangement, particularly for students who stay nearer their school during the week, or where a parent's shift pattern makes weeknights unreliable. The trade is that weekend sessions compete with rest and family, so they work best as one longer block rather than two.

Whatever the pattern, agree it for a term and change it deliberately rather than weekly. Slots that are renegotiated often become slots that are lost: the tutor eventually fills the hour with a family who keeps it. Flag the weeks you already know will be thin when the plan is written, and the tutor can front-load content and leave marked work to cover them.

sections.heading: What the market advertises, and what each price band actually buys
paragraphs: Every rate published in this market is published by somebody selling lessons, which is worth stating before any figure appears. The bands below come from tutoring platforms, tutor marketplaces and tutoring companies operating in the Kingdom, advertising their own services. They are not audited, they are not a market average, and they are not IB Gram's price. They are useful because a family that knows the bands can recognise a quote that is out of line in either direction.

Scarcity sets the number more than anything else, and in a new school market that is the fact to plan around. Advertised rates start from roughly SAR 35 an hour on budget IGCSE platforms and from around SAR 55 for general non-specialist online tutoring. General private tuition in Saudi cities is advertised at about SAR 50 an hour for primary and at SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects. IB subject listings commonly start near SAR 180, with Higher Level and Advanced Placement tracks advertised around SAR 200 to 220. International providers quoting in dollars sit near USD 60 an hour, which leaves the family carrying the exchange rate as well as the fee.

What moves a quote within those bands, in order of weight: subject scarcity, then examiner or marking experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels, then package length. Travel loading is why in-home rates in Saudi cities sit above online rates for the same teacher, and in this region it would be the largest line in any in-home quote. IB Gram does not run home visits in the Kingdom in any case; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India.

Read the table as a guide to what each band buys rather than as a price list. The useful question is never whether a rate is high. It is whether the thing the student needs sits inside what that band typically delivers, and whether a cheaper band would simply fail to address it.

sections.heading: Equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili from a north-western address
paragraphs: A certificate from an international school is not automatically accepted by a Saudi university. It requires an equivalency decision, mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before it is treated as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, and that applies equally to the IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma. The paperwork itself is not difficult. What makes it painful is leaving it to the final term, where it competes with examinations, and for a family that has relocated internationally it is worse, because transcripts and attestations may have to be chased across two countries.

Alongside equivalency sit the two Qiyas tests. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is administered by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment and measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content; it can be taken in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last point is the one worth acting on: an IB or Cambridge student meets overlapping material framed differently, sequenced differently and examined in a different style, which is why strong international-curriculum students often find Tahsili harder than their own papers.

Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school grades with the Qiyas results, with weightings that differ by institution and by programme and competitive science, engineering and medicine programmes leaning hardest on Tahsili. No threshold or weighting formula appears on this page, because those numbers vary by institution and intake and third-party sites contradict each other. Take them from the university's own published criteria. Some universities also set a maximum age for the secondary certificate they will accept, which matters for a student considering a gap year.

For a family in the north-west the practical issues are logistical as well as academic. Test sittings and attestation steps involve travel, so they go in the calendar early and get planned around school assessment weeks rather than discovered after them. Tahsili preparation works best as its own weekly strand taught against national-curriculum framing, started in the first Diploma year, rather than squeezed into subject lessons in the last term.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework, and what the pressure of a late arrival does to that line
paragraphs: This matters more in a community full of mid-course arrivals than almost anywhere else, because the temptation is strongest exactly where a student is behind through no fault of their own. A student who joined DP2 in the spring term, facing an Internal Assessment with weeks rather than months available, is the person most likely to be offered help that crosses the line. Parts of this market will offer to supply the work. Accepting that offer risks the entire Diploma, and a school that suspects malpractice is obliged to investigate.

What a tutor legitimately does is substantial and worth paying for. They translate the assessment criteria into the subject's own language, show the student what each strand is actually asking for, test whether a research question can be answered inside the word limit, point out where a method will not generate usable data, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. They teach the student to read the criteria independently, which is the habit that carries into every other component.

What no tutor does is write, redraft or dictate any part of assessed work. We will not draft an Extended Essay, and we never produce a Theory of Knowledge essay, a Personal Project or any coursework on a student's behalf. We do not supply model answers to be adapted, and we do not rewrite paragraphs for a student to paste in. The school supervisor remains the formal supervisor of an Extended Essay, and the number of drafts formally reviewed is set by the school rather than by a tutor.

Keeping that boundary visible protects the student as well as the grade. Dated drafts, the student's own notes and a record of feedback given rather than text supplied are what demonstrate authorship if anybody ever asks. Put the question to any prospective tutor directly: what will you do with a draft, and what will you refuse to do? The answer separates a teacher from an essay mill faster than any credential.
bullets: A tutor explains criteria, tests a method and comments on the student's own draft
A tutor never writes, redrafts or dictates assessed work, however short the deadline
The school supervisor remains the formal Extended Essay supervisor
