taif.programmesIntro: Taif families arrive at this page from four different starting points: a Middle Years Programme student building towards subject choices, an IGCSE candidate in the two-year run-up to a series, a Diploma student in the first year, and a Diploma student in the final one. The teaching job is different in each, so here is what each actually asks for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme assesses against criteria rather than papers, which confuses parents who expect percentages. Each subject has four criteria, each marked out of eight, and a student can know the content well and still land in the middle band because the criterion asks for something the answer never does. Years 4 and 5 of the programme also carry the Personal Project, an independent piece with its own criteria and a process journal that is assessed alongside the product.
programmes.countryNote: For a Taif student this is the stage where a weak habit is cheapest to fix. There is usually no local cohort to compare against, so a criterion-by-criterion reading of two or three pieces of real marked work tells a parent more than a report card does. An MYP tutor in Taif works from the school's own assessment task sheets, because the criteria are published but the task wording is the school's.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and International GCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE is where syllabus codes start to matter. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and splits into a Core and an Extended route with different maximum grades; the sciences run 0610, 0620 and 0625 with a separate practical-skills paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses a different code set and, in several subjects, a single untiered entry. The two boards examine the same material with different paper structures, so revision bought for the wrong board is partly wasted.
programmes.countryNote: A Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Taif needs the code before the first lesson, because 0580 Core and 0580 Extended are not the same course taught at two speeds. Taif candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series Cambridge runs is available only in India, and a family told otherwise will plan around a sitting that does not exist for them. Your school's examinations officer holds the entry dates.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: The first Diploma year sets up everything that is marked in the second. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the creativity, activity and service requirement. Most of the internal assessment work is started here, and most of the damage done here is invisible until the mock papers. Students who coast through the first year on strong IGCSE grades are the ones who find the Higher Level extension brutal in the second.
programmes.countryNote: The first Diploma year is the right moment for a Taif family to fix Higher Level choices honestly. If the local school runs a Higher Level option with one teacher and three students, outside subject teaching is not a luxury, it is cover for a single point of failure. An IB Diploma tutor in Taif at this stage spends as much time on the internal assessment plan and the Extended Essay research question as on content.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: The final year is a deadline-management problem wearing a content problem's clothes. Internal assessments are finished and submitted, the Extended Essay goes through its reflections, Theory of Knowledge is examined, predicted grades are issued for university applications, and the written papers sit at the end of it. Exam technique becomes worth more per hour than new content from roughly the mock season onwards, because the marks are now lost on command terms and timing rather than on knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: For a Taif student applying abroad, the predicted grade issued by the school drives the offers, and it is issued well before the papers. That puts the useful work early: a tutor who can lift the quality of mock performance is working on the predicted grade as much as on the final one. Add the equivalency and Qiyas steps for a Saudi university route and the final year holds two separate deadlines sets.

taif.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Taif families ask for most, with the part of each that actually costs marks. Scarcity is uneven: a Standard Level mathematics tutor is findable almost anywhere, and a Higher Level physics or a Higher Level analysis-and-approaches specialist is not, which is why those two cost more in every market in the Kingdom.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Higher Level course adds a third paper of extended problems that Standard Level students never sit, and the proof, complex numbers and calculus extensions behind it. Marks go missing in method lines rather than final answers: a correct value with no visible working collects a fraction of the available marks. The internal exploration is a fifth of the grade and is marked on mathematical communication as much as on the mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling, statistics and technology, and students who switch into it expecting an easier ride meet a heavy graphical-display-calculator skill load instead. Standard Level candidates lose marks by writing conclusions that are not tied back to the data. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical testing, and a tutor who taught the analysis course is not automatically fluent in this one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics punishes unit and significant-figure carelessness harder than most subjects, and the long-answer paper asks for explanation chains that students compress into one sentence. The Higher Level additional topics sit on top of the shared core rather than beside it, so a weak core topic reappears twice. The scientific investigation is a fifth of the grade and is where personal engagement and methodological rigour are marked, not experimental luck.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Chemistry marks cluster in three places: mole calculations set out without working, organic mechanisms drawn without curly arrows or charges, and energetics answers that state a sign without justifying it. The data booklet is allowed and most students under-use it. Higher Level extends into further thermodynamics and equilibrium treatment, and the investigation asks for a research question narrow enough to be answered in the time available.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology looks like a memory subject and is examined as a precision subject. Definitions are marked strictly, the data-based questions want manipulation rather than description, and extended responses are marked against a list of specific points, so a fluent essay missing four of them scores poorly. Higher Level adds depth to plant biology, genetics and physiology that the Standard Level course only gestures at.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The guided textual analysis paper rewards close work on one unseen passage and is wrecked by context-dumping. Higher Level candidates also write an essay on a studied work, and the individual oral asks for a global issue explored through two texts, one in translation where relevant. Students who read widely still lose marks here by analysing content instead of technique and structure.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: English B is a language-acquisition course, not a literature one, and its paper one asks for a specific text type with a specific register and audience. Marks go on choosing the wrong format as often as on grammar. Higher Level adds literary works and a longer productive task. Many strong speakers in international schools are entered here and then under-perform on format conventions they were never taught.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Economics is a diagram subject with an essay attached. An answer without a correctly labelled, correctly shifted diagram cannot reach the top band however well written it is. Higher Level carries a third paper of quantitative questions with policy calculation, and the internal assessment is three commentaries built on recent news articles, marked on the application of a named key concept rather than on summary.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business Management is tool-driven. The examination expects named frameworks applied to the stimulus in front of the student rather than described in general, and Higher Level adds a third paper built on a pre-released case study that rewards preparation months in advance. The internal assessment differs by level, and students routinely choose an organisation that will not supply the information the commentary needs.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: History has the heaviest Higher Level extension of the humanities: a third paper on a regional option worth more than a third of the Higher Level grade, which Standard Level candidates do not sit at all. Paper one is source work with its own mark allocation per question type, and the comparison question is the most commonly mishandled part of the whole subject.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Computer Science rewards precise pseudocode and trace tables, and the Higher Level extension into abstract data structures, resource management and object-oriented programming is where candidates separate. The solution is a developed product with documented design and testing, and students who build first and document afterwards lose criterion marks that have nothing to do with how good the program is.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Psychology is examined on the use of named studies as evidence, so a student who remembers the finding but not the researcher or design cannot be credited properly. Higher Level adds extensions within each approach and a third paper on research methodology. The internal assessment is a replication of a simple experiment written to a strict structure, and the statistical treatment is marked.

taif.igcseSubjectsIntro: Because Taif's international-curriculum students are split across boards, the IGCSE picture matters as much as the Diploma one. These are the papers that decide those grades, with the Cambridge codes a family should have in front of them before buying a single hour of tuition.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
igcseSubjects.description: Core and Extended are different entries with different grade ranges, and the choice is made by the school, not the student. Extended candidates meet functions, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and more demanding algebra. Check which route your child is entered for before anything else; on the current syllabus one of the two papers is sat without a calculator, so mental and written methods carry real marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610)
igcseSubjects.description: Three papers: a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical-skills paper that many candidates meet as the alternative-to-practical written option. The practical paper is the one students revise last and lose most on, because it tests experimental design, variable control and graph plotting rather than recall of the biology itself.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620)
igcseSubjects.description: Qualitative analysis, ionic equations and mole reasoning carry the grade here. The practical-skills paper asks for observation written in the examiner's language, and students who have done the experiments but never written them up to a mark scheme describe colour changes in terms that cannot be credited. Extended candidates face the harder electrochemistry and organic content.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625)
igcseSubjects.description: Physics at IGCSE is the subject where formula recall, rearrangement and unit conversion decide the grade more than conceptual depth. Extended papers add electromagnetism and wave treatment the Core route leaves out. The practical-skills paper rewards students who can read a scale, record to a sensible precision and spot an anomalous point in someone else's data.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English
igcseSubjects.description: These are different qualifications with different purposes and should not be chosen by how good a speaker the student is. First Language English marks reading response and directed writing against demanding criteria; English as a Second Language rewards accurate, appropriate language use. Being entered for the wrong one is a grade problem that no amount of tuition fixes late.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Both reward structured application to a short case rather than general knowledge, and both are commonly taught in Taif by a teacher covering more than one humanities subject. Diagram accuracy in Economics and correct use of named business terminology are the two cheapest sources of extra marks in either subject.

taif.regionsTitle: Taif district by district, and the slot each one leaves
taif.regionsIntro: Taif is not one commute. The central districts sit on the plateau with short, predictable school runs; the escarpment settlements above and below the city do not. Because the school run decides what time a lesson can start, it is worth being specific about where a family actually lives before agreeing a weekly slot.

regions.name: Shubra
regions.note: Central Taif, around the old palace quarter, with short school runs and the densest cluster of private schools in the city. A family here can usually hold an early evening slot, which matters for a tutor working from a time zone behind Arabia Standard Time.

regions.name: Al Faisaliyah
regions.note: A large residential district with heavy school-hour traffic on the main approaches. The run is short in distance and unreliable in time, so families here tend to do better with a fixed later start than with an ambitious one they miss twice a month.

regions.name: Al Hawiyah
regions.note: North of the centre, built around Taif University's campus, so household routines here often follow a university timetable rather than a school one. Older siblings studying at home in the evening make quiet-room scheduling the real constraint rather than the drive.

regions.name: Al Shafa
regions.note: Up on the escarpment southwest of the city, higher, cooler and known for its rose and fruit farms. The descent into Taif for school is long and weather-sensitive, and an evening lesson here realistically starts after the light goes rather than straight after the school run.

regions.name: Al Hada
regions.note: On the mountain road down towards Makkah, with the same altitude advantage and the same commute penalty as Al Shafa. Families here are the clearest case for online teaching in the whole city: no in-home tutor is driving that road twice a week for a single hour.

regions.name: Al Qutbiyah
regions.note: An established central district within easy reach of the main school cluster, which makes a two-subject evening pair workable here more often than elsewhere in Taif. Two shorter sessions back to back suit a student who fades after an hour on one subject.

regions.name: Ar Rudaf
regions.note: Near the park of the same name on the southern side of the centre, mixed residential with a mixture of school destinations. Siblings at different schools with different finishing times is the common scheduling problem here, not distance.

regions.name: Al Mathnah
regions.note: Northern Taif, closer to the airport road, where families commuting out of the city for work arrive home later. Lessons that start after the evening meal rather than before it hold far better over a full term for households on this pattern.

regions.name: Al Salamah
regions.note: A newer residential area on the city's edge where a reliable fixed-time weekly slot matters more than a convenient one. Taif summer traffic, when families from the coast arrive for the cooler months, affects outbound runs here most.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the coast
schoolClusters.note: Taif families looking for an international-curriculum place, or comparing one, usually look first down the escarpment to Jeddah, which holds the nearest concentration of IB World Schools and Cambridge schools. Some families board, some relocate for the Diploma years, and some commute at the start and end of term. Students we support attend schools including these.

schoolClusters.city: Riyadh, for families who move again
schoolClusters.note: Work moves families within the Kingdom often enough that a Taif student's next school is frequently in Riyadh, which holds the largest set of Diploma and Cambridge options. Keeping the same tutor through a move is one of the few practical advantages of online teaching that a family feels immediately.

schoolClusters.city: The Eastern Province cluster
schoolClusters.note: The Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation behaves as a single school market, and the Diploma is offered at some campuses there and not others. Families transferring from Taif into that cluster often discover that their child's Higher Level combination is available at only one or two schools in the whole area.

taif.modesIntro: Four ways Taif families actually buy teaching, with what each is good for. All of them are one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, and all of them are built around a Sunday-to-Thursday school week with Friday and Saturday as the weekend.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject
modes.description: The default and the one that compounds. A fixed weekly hour on a single subject, pinned to Saudi local time so it does not drift when a tutor's own country changes its clocks. Work is set between lessons and marked before the next one, which is where most of the gain actually comes from rather than from the hour itself.

modes.title: Two subjects in one evening
modes.description: Two shorter back-to-back sessions on different subjects, which suits students in central Taif districts with a short school run and families who would rather protect one evening than two. It works when the subjects are genuinely different; two sciences in a row usually does not, because the second hour gets the tired student every week.

modes.title: Pre-series intensive block
modes.description: A compressed run of sessions in the weeks before a series, built around timed past-paper work and mark-scheme reading rather than new content. The point of the block is the marking: a paper sat under time, marked against the real mark scheme, and the pattern in the lost marks named and then drilled before the next one.

modes.title: Coursework review clinic
modes.description: Sessions built around the student's own internal assessment, Extended Essay or Personal Project draft. The tutor reads what the student has written, asks the questions a reader will ask, maps the draft against the published criteria and sends the student away to redraft. The writing stays the student's, in every session, without exception.

sections.heading: Where a Diploma grade actually comes from, subject by subject
paragraphs: A Diploma grade is not an average of impressions. It is built from a small number of components with fixed weightings, and the single most useful thing a parent can know is which component carries the most marks in their child's subject. Revision effort put into the wrong component is not half-useful, it is close to wasted. A student who is losing marks on the internal assessment and a student who is losing them on the long-answer paper need different teaching, different homework and sometimes different tutors.

The weightings also explain why Higher Level is a different purchase from Standard Level rather than a longer one. In several subjects the Higher Level grade rests on a third paper that Standard Level candidates never sit, and that paper is often the hardest single component in the course. In History it carries more than a third of the grade on its own. In Economics it is a quantitative paper with no Standard Level equivalent. A tutor who has taught the Standard Level course has not, by that fact, taught the third paper.

The table sets out how the split falls in the subjects Taif families ask about most. Treat it as the shape of the course rather than as the last word: the IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle, and the authority on which version your child sits is the school's Diploma Programme coordinator. Ask for the component weightings in writing at the start of the first year, put them on the wall, and plan every term of support against them.
bullets: Ask the coordinator which syllabus version your child is entered for
Find out which component the lost marks are actually in before buying hours

A Higher Level third paper is a separate teaching job, not an extension

sections.heading: Command terms, and the marks that vanish between knowing and scoring
paragraphs: The gap that surprises Taif parents most is between what a student knows and what a student is paid for. Both the IB and Cambridge write questions in a controlled vocabulary, and each verb in it carries an instruction about the shape of the answer. State wants a fact with no reasoning. Describe wants features without explanation. Explain wants a causal chain. Evaluate wants both sides weighed and a judgement reached. Discuss wants a balanced argument. A student who explains when the paper said state wastes time; one who describes when the paper said explain loses most of the marks on the question.

This is learnable in weeks and it is rarely taught directly, because a classroom teacher covering a syllabus to a deadline has to spend the hours on content. It is also why timed past-paper work marked against the published mark scheme is worth more per hour late in a course than another pass through the textbook. The mark scheme is the only document that tells you what the examiner will pay for, and reading it with a student is a different activity from giving them the answers.

The second half of the same problem is mark allocation. A six-mark question in a Diploma science wants six creditable points, not six sentences; a two-mark calculation wants a method line and an answer with a unit. In IGCSE practical-skills papers the credit sits in the precision of the observation rather than in the conclusion. Students who learn to read the mark total as an instruction about how much to write stop running out of time in the final papers, which is a bigger source of lost marks in Taif's small cohorts than anyone admits, because nobody has sat a full mock in a room with twenty other candidates.
bullets: Learn the command-term list for each subject and treat it as examinable
Read the mark total as an instruction about answer length
Mark one timed paper properly rather than attempting three untimed
Keep the published mark scheme in the room during revision

sections.heading: Taif's school run, and the hours it leaves for a lesson
paragraphs: A weekly slot either survives a term or it does not, and the thing that kills it is almost never the teaching. It is a start time agreed in an optimistic week. Taif makes this sharper than most Saudi cities because the city is really two geographies: a plateau centre with short, predictable runs, and the escarpment above and below it where the drive is long, winding and weather-sensitive. A family in Shubra and a family in Al Hada can be enrolled at the same school and have completely different evenings.

The honest planning method is to work backwards from the latest realistic arrival home across a normal week, add the time it takes a teenager to eat and settle, and set the slot after that. A lesson that starts fifteen minutes late every week is worse than a later lesson that starts on time, because the lost quarter hour comes out of the end, which is where the practice usually is. Families who protect one evening rather than scattering two across the week also keep their slots longer, particularly where siblings attend schools with different finishing times.

Two Taif-specific things are worth building in. The first is the summer season: when families from Jeddah, Makkah and Riyadh arrive for the cooler highland months, the roads on the city's edges behave differently from the rest of the year, and an outbound run from a newer district such as Al Salamah can take noticeably longer. The second is that lessons are delivered online, which is what makes any of this adjustable at all. A tutor reachable over video can move a session half an hour later for a term; a tutor driving across the city cannot.

sections.heading: Being the only student in the building sitting your syllabus
paragraphs: This is the part of Taif's situation that rival pages never write about, because it is specific and unflattering and cannot be fixed by enthusiasm. When a city's private-school provision is largely national-curriculum, the handful of students doing a Diploma or a Cambridge entry are structurally isolated. They have no cohort to calibrate against, so a student with a weak grasp of a topic has no way of noticing it until a mock paper says so. There is no corridor conversation about what the examiner wanted, and no classmate's annotated answer to compare with.

It changes what good teaching looks like. A tutor working with an isolated student has to supply the cohort: other students' answers at different grade levels, the range of what a mark scheme accepts, and the standard the paper is actually set to. Without that, a student calibrates against their own best previous effort, which drifts. Supplying a benchmark is a specific, teachable thing, and it is one of the few arguments for an outside tutor that holds even when the school's own teaching is good.

It also changes the Higher Level risk. In a small cohort, a Higher Level option may run with one teacher and a handful of students, which is fine until that teacher is absent, leaves mid-course or has never taught the option before. A family in that position is carrying a single point of failure on a subject that will decide a university offer. Outside subject teaching is not a vote of no confidence in the school; it is redundancy on the component that cannot be repeated.

Ask who taught that option last year and who teaches it this year
Request marked work at a range of grades, not just your child's
Treat a one-teacher Higher Level option as a risk to plan around

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: the same subject, two different papers
paragraphs: Taif's international-curriculum students are not all on one board, and the difference matters more than most families are told. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both offer international qualifications at this level, both are sat in the Kingdom, and both examine broadly the same subject content. What differs is the paper structure, the tiering and the specification detail, which is exactly what tuition in the final year is aimed at. Past papers bought for the wrong board teach the wrong paper.

The clearest difference is tiering. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics splits into Core and Extended entries with different grade ranges, and the Cambridge sciences do the same. Several Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are untiered, while Edexcel mathematics runs Foundation and Higher tiers of its own. A student entered for a lower tier cannot be awarded the top grades whatever they score, so tier confirmation belongs in the first conversation with the school, not in the term before the series.

The second difference is the practical component. Cambridge science candidates meet a practical-skills paper, often as the alternative-to-practical written option, which examines experimental design, precision of observation and graph work rather than the content. It is the paper students revise last and the one that most often costs a grade. Edexcel handles practical assessment differently, and a tutor who has only ever taught one board will not instinctively know which practice papers are even relevant. Ask the question directly at the trial lesson: which board, which code, and which papers has the tutor actually taught to a mark scheme. A specialist answers in a sentence. Anyone who needs to check the specification during the conversation is learning the course alongside your child, which is a reasonable thing for a school to absorb and an expensive thing for a family to pay for by the hour.

sections.heading: What tuition is advertised at in this market, in SAR
paragraphs: Saudi tutoring providers are unusually coy about price, and the vagueness is doing work: a number that only appears after a form is filled in is a number that moves depending on who is asking. So here are the bands that are actually published, with what kind of source publishes them. These are advertised rates collected from vendor and marketplace pages, not a market average, and not what IB Gram charges. Our own figure is quoted per match, because it depends on the subject, the level and who is free to teach it.

What moves the number, roughly in order of weight: subject scarcity first, then marking or examiner experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels, then package length. Scarcity is the one families underestimate. A Standard Level mathematics tutor is findable in most of the Kingdom; a Higher Level physics or Higher Level analysis-and-approaches specialist is not, and in a city the size of Taif the local pool for those is close to empty. That is a supply fact, not a sales argument, and it is the same reason the same subjects cost more in Riyadh.

The last column is the one to read if you are comparing quotes. A low hourly rate for a non-specialist covering a Higher Level subject is not cheaper teaching, it is a different product: you are buying supervision of homework rather than instruction in a syllabus. Both have their place, and a family on a budget is sometimes right to buy the cheaper one for a Standard Level subject while spending properly on the Higher Level one that will decide a university offer.

sections.heading: Counting the year backwards from the June and November series
paragraphs: Nobody publishes this for Saudi families, so it gets planned badly. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series, which is the main one for schools in the Kingdom, and a November series used for resits and November-entry candidates. The February and March series Cambridge operates is available only in India, so a Taif family that reads an Indian tutoring page and plans around a spring sitting is planning around something that is not open to them. Diploma candidates at Saudi schools almost all sit the May session.

Entries close months before papers are sat, and the date is set by your school as the examination centre rather than by the board's public calendar. That is the single most useful phone call a parent can make in the first term: ask the examinations officer for the internal entry deadline, the tier or route your child is entered for, and the date internal assessment work is due at school. Those three facts shape every decision about when to buy teaching, and all three are held locally.

Working backwards from a series rather than forwards from today also fixes the most common timing error, which is starting support in the term the papers are sat. By then the useful work has narrowed to exam technique, because there is no time to build anything. The term before is when content gaps can still be closed. The year before is when a Higher Level choice can still be changed. Internal assessment work sits earlier still, and once it is submitted, that portion of the grade is fixed no matter how well the papers go.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: This needs saying plainly, because parts of this market are selling something else. The internal assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Middle Years Programme Personal Project are assessed pieces that must be the student's own work. A tutor who drafts, rewrites or produces any of them has not helped; they have exposed the student to a malpractice finding that can cost the whole Diploma. No grade is worth that trade, and a provider offering it is telling you exactly how much they care about the outcome.

What a good tutor does instead is narrower and more useful. They read the student's own draft. They map it against the published criteria, which is a skill in itself because the criteria are written for examiners rather than for sixteen-year-olds. They ask the questions a reader will ask, name what is missing, and send the student away to redraft it themselves. They help narrow a research question from something unanswerable to something that can be answered inside the word limit. They explain what the reflection requirement is for. They never put a sentence into the document.

A family can check this easily. Ask the tutor what they will do if the draft arrives two days before the school deadline and is in poor shape. The honest answer involves telling the student and, where appropriate, the school, and working on what can be improved by the student in the time available. The dishonest answer involves a quiet offer to tidy it up. Keep the written feedback, because a record of what was discussed and what the student then changed is the clearest evidence that the work is their own.
bullets: Assessed work must be written by the student, in every component
A tutor reviews, questions and maps against criteria, and nothing more

sections.heading: Equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili: the step after the grade
paragraphs: A strong international certificate is not automatically a Saudi university entry ticket, and the step in between catches families late. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision, the mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. This applies to the IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. It is a document process with its own requirements, and some universities also state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept.

Alongside that sit the Qiyas tests, run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and is sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. The important fact for a Taif family is that Tahsili content follows the Saudi national curriculum, which is why international-curriculum students often find it harder than their own examinations. The material overlaps; the framing does not.

We do not publish thresholds or weighting formulas here, and you should be wary of any page that does. Universities set their own admission formulas combining school grades with the Qiyas results, those weightings differ by university and by programme, and the competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes lean hardest on Tahsili. The only reliable source is the university's own published admission criteria for the programme your child is applying to. Read it in the first Diploma year, not the last, because it may change which subjects your child should be sitting at Higher Level.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus, not just the subject
process.description: Board, subject, level and code where there is one: Chemistry HL, or Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended. Add the school, the year group and which component the marks are going missing in if you know. That one message is the difference between a specialist match and a generalist with a free evening.

process.title: Say what the week actually looks like
process.description: Your district in Taif, the realistic arrival home across a normal Sunday-to-Thursday week, and any evening that is already committed. We would rather agree a later slot that survives a full term than an early one that slips fifteen minutes every week until it stops being worth having.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: Not a sales call. The tutor teaches something, usually a question the student has already got wrong, and you see how they handle it. Ask them which paper the lost marks are on and what they would change first. A specialist answers that in one sentence; a generalist talks about confidence.

process.title: A diagnostic, then a plan with named components
process.description: The first working session establishes a starting point against the actual mark scheme rather than against a general impression. What comes out of it is a short plan naming the components to be worked on and in what order, which is the document you hold the tuition to over the following term.

process.title: Weekly work, marked between lessons
process.description: Work set after each session and marked before the next, because the marking is where the diagnosis lives. You get a short written note of what was covered, what was set and what it showed, which is also the record you can show the school if a question about coursework ever arises.

process.title: Review at the end of the term, honestly
process.description: A term is long enough to tell whether this is working. If the component that was costing marks is no longer costing them, the plan changes. If the match is wrong, we change the tutor rather than asking you to persevere, and if a second subject has become the bigger problem we will say so.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a paper, not to a postcode
whyPoints.description: The constraint in Taif is not distance, it is supply: the number of people within reach who have actually taught your child's syllabus at your child's level. Teaching online removes distance from the matching problem entirely, which is the only way a Higher Level request gets a Higher Level specialist in a city this size.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Sunday-to-Thursday week
whyPoints.description: Lessons are timed to Arabia Standard Time and to a week that ends on Thursday. Slots are pinned to Saudi local time, so a tutor whose own country changes its clocks does not drag your Tuesday evening half an hour in either direction twice a year without anybody noticing.

whyPoints.title: Rates explained rather than hidden
whyPoints.description: The advertised bands in this market are on this page with the kind of source that publishes them, because a number that only appears after a form is filled in is a number that moves. Our own figure is quoted per match, and we will tell you when a cheaper non-specialist is genuinely the right call.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that keeps the work the student's
whyPoints.description: On an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Personal Project the tutor reads, questions and maps against the criteria, then the student redrafts. Nothing is written for them. The written feedback trail is deliberate, because it is also the clearest evidence that the work is genuinely their own.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not know
whyPoints.description: Examination and results dates come from your school, not from us. Entry deadlines are set by the school as the examination centre. University admission formulas and Qiyas thresholds come from the university's own published criteria. We will point you at the right holder of a fact rather than guess at it on a web page.

whyPoints.title: A single tutor who travels with the family
whyPoints.description: Work moves families between Taif, Jeddah, Riyadh and the Eastern Province mid-course more often than anyone plans for. A tutor reached over video is one of the few parts of a child's education that survives the move intact, which matters most in the Diploma years when a change of school changes everything else.

faqs.question: How is a Diploma science grade split between the two written papers and the investigation?
faqs.answer: In the Diploma sciences the scientific investigation carries a fifth of the grade and the two written papers carry the rest, with the longer-answer paper weighted more heavily than the multiple-choice and data paper. The split is the same at Higher Level and Standard Level, which surprises families: what changes at Higher Level is the additional content layered onto the shared core, not the proportions. Confirm the exact weightings for your child's syllabus version with the school's Diploma Programme coordinator, then plan revision against them rather than against how hard each paper feels.

faqs.question: What does the Higher Level third paper add that a Standard Level student never sits?
faqs.answer: In several subjects the Higher Level grade rests partly on a third paper with no Standard Level equivalent, and it is usually the hardest component in the course. In History it is a regional-option paper worth more than a third of the grade. In Economics it is a quantitative policy paper. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches it is a set of extended multi-stage problems. In Business Management it is built on a pre-released case study. A tutor who has taught the Standard Level course has not, by that fact alone, taught any of these, so ask directly.

faqs.question: Why do grade boundaries move between one series and the next?
faqs.answer: Boundaries are set after papers are marked, not before they are sat, because they exist to keep the standard constant when the difficulty of a paper varies. If a paper turns out harder than intended, the boundary for each grade falls; if it is easier, the boundary rises. That is why last series boundaries are a planning guide and never a target. The practical consequence for a student is to aim a clear margin above the boundary they are chasing rather than at it, and to treat any single past paper's boundary as one data point.

faqs.question: What is a predicted grade, and who at a Taif school decides it?
faqs.answer: A predicted grade is the school's professional judgement of what a student is likely to achieve, issued for university applications well before the papers are sat. It is decided by the subject teacher and the coordinator, normally on the evidence of mock papers and internal assessment work, not by a tutor and not by the family. In a small Taif cohort it rests on fewer data points than it would in a large school, which makes mock performance unusually influential. That is a reason to take the mock season seriously rather than a reason to argue after the fact.

faqs.question: How does a Cambridge IGCSE 0580 tier choice change what my child can be awarded?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 runs as a Core entry and an Extended entry, and they carry different grade ranges. A Core candidate cannot be awarded the top grades however well they perform, so the entry decision sets a ceiling before any revision happens. The school makes that decision, usually on the evidence of internal assessments. If your child is aiming at a Diploma mathematics course at Higher Level, confirm the Extended entry early and in writing, because moving route late in the course is difficult and sometimes not possible.

faqs.question: What happens in a first diagnostic session for a Taif student joining mid-term?
faqs.answer: The tutor works from real evidence rather than a conversation: a recent piece of marked work, a past-paper question the student has already attempted, or a draft of an internal assessment. The point is to locate the lost marks by component and by topic, not to assess general ability. A mid-term joiner also needs a quick map of what the school has already covered and what it has not, since that differs between schools. What comes out is a short plan naming the components to work on and the order to work on them in.

faqs.question: What should the first month of tuition produce before we commit to a term?
faqs.answer: Four things. A named diagnosis: which component and which topics the marks are going missing in. A plan with an order to it. Evidence that the student is doing work between sessions, because that is where most progress actually happens. And one piece of work marked to the real mark scheme, so you can see the standard rather than take it on trust. If after a month nobody can tell you which paper the problem is on, that is information about the tutor rather than about your child.

faqs.question: How often should a tutor write to me rather than to my child?
faqs.answer: A short written note after every session, covering what was taught, what was set and what the work showed, is a reasonable baseline and takes a tutor a few minutes. A longer review at the end of each term is where honest judgement belongs: whether the component is improving, whether the plan should change, whether a different subject is now the bigger problem. Weekly essays are not useful to anyone. What matters is that you are told something specific and checkable rather than that your child is doing nicely.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor match is wrong after two lessons?
faqs.answer: We change the tutor. A match can fail for reasons that have nothing to do with competence: pace, manner, the student's willingness to admit confusion to a particular adult. Two lessons is usually enough to tell, and persevering with a bad fit wastes a term. Tell us what specifically did not work, because that is what makes the second match better than a reshuffle. A re-match should not cost you the fee for lessons that have not happened, and the new tutor should be briefed on what the first one found.

faqs.question: When should a Middle Years Programme student in Taif start building towards IGCSE or the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The useful work in the middle years is not acceleration, it is removing the weaknesses that become expensive later: algebraic fluency, writing to a brief, reading a question for what it actually asks. Years 4 and 5 of the programme are the right window, and the cheapest intervention is a criterion-by-criterion reading of two or three pieces of real marked work. For a student who is likely to be isolated in a small senior cohort, this is also when the habit of working to a published criterion rather than to a teacher's approval is established.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start Higher Level support in the second Diploma year?
faqs.answer: No, but what it can achieve narrows. In the final year the realistic gains are in exam technique, command-term discipline, timing and the two or three topics that keep costing marks. Content building needs the term before, and internal assessment work that has already been submitted is fixed. The honest version is that a term of focused work on the right component in the final year can move a grade; a term spent re-teaching a whole Higher Level course cannot. Ask the tutor to name what they expect to change, then hold them to it.

faqs.question: What should a Year 10 student have in place before the IGCSE examination year begins?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is content. Confirmation of the board and the code for every subject, because past papers for the wrong board teach the wrong paper. Confirmation of tier or route where the subject has one, since that sets the grade ceiling. And a working habit of writing to a mark scheme rather than writing until the page is full. A student who arrives in the examination year with those in place can spend the year on the subject; one who does not spends the first term discovering what they are entered for.

faqs.question: How does a November-series candidate's year differ from a June one?
faqs.answer: The whole plan shifts by roughly half a year, which is the part families get wrong. A November entry compresses revision into a period that includes the long summer break, so the summer stops being downtime and becomes the main working block. Internal deadlines at school move with it. A resit candidate also has a specific advantage worth using: the examiner's report and the marks from the first attempt show exactly where the grade was lost, which makes the second run much more targeted than the first one was.

faqs.question: What does the Personal Project ask of a Middle Years Programme student, and where may a tutor help?
faqs.answer: The Personal Project is an independent piece with its own criteria, assessed on the process as well as the product, which is why the process journal matters as much as the outcome. A tutor may help the student understand the criteria, ask the questions that narrow an over-ambitious goal into an achievable one, and discuss how to evidence the process. A tutor may not plan it for them, make the product, or write the report. If the project is in trouble, the useful intervention is scope reduction, done by the student, early.

faqs.question: Why does an evening lesson in Al Shafa or Al Hada usually start later than one in Shubra?
faqs.answer: Because the drive is a different kind of drive. The escarpment settlements above and below Taif involve a long, winding, weather-sensitive descent and climb, where the central plateau districts involve a short predictable run. A family in Shubra can often hold a late-afternoon or early-evening slot; a family on the mountain road realistically cannot, and agreeing one anyway produces a term of lessons that start fifteen minutes late. Set the slot after the latest normal arrival home, not after the best one.

faqs.question: What should the last eight weeks before the June series actually look like?
faqs.answer: Execution, not teaching. A timed paper sat properly, marked against the published mark scheme, with the pattern in the lost marks named and then drilled before the next one. Two or three recurring weaknesses worked on repeatedly rather than a sweep through the whole syllabus. Command-term discipline and timing, because that is where marks go in the final weeks. New content at this stage is almost always displacement activity, and a tutor proposing it in the last eight weeks has misread where the marks are.

taif.closingHeading: Tell us the paper, the district and the realistic evening
taif.closingBody: Those three things are enough to start. The board, subject, level and code tell us which specialist to look for; your district in Taif and the honest arrival time across a normal Sunday-to-Thursday week tell us which slot will still be standing at the end of term. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, the trial lesson is free and is taught rather than sold, and if we do not have the right specialist free for your subject we will say so rather than offer you a generalist with an opening. Bring a recent piece of marked work to the trial if you can; it is worth more than any description of the problem.

thuwal-kaust.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the Diploma Programme, the Middle Years Programme and Cambridge IGCSE one-to-one over live video. Each is matched to a named subject and level — Mathematics AA HL, Chemistry SL, Extended Mathematics 0580 — rather than to a year group, because a Thuwal evening is too short to spend on a tutor learning the course alongside your child.

intro.heading: One school, one short evening, and a syllabus that does not bend
paragraphs: Thuwal is unusual in the Kingdom. The town sits on the Red Sea coast roughly 80 km north of Jeddah, and the community that drives demand for IB and IGCSE tutors in Thuwal (KAUST) is the research campus of King Abdullah University of Science and Technology. Its families come from across the world on contracts measured in years, not decades, and their children attend The KAUST School. That produces something you will not find in Riyadh or Jeddah: a parent body in which a large share hold doctorates in the exact subjects their teenagers are now struggling with, and almost no local market of alternative schools to switch to if a subject goes wrong.

It also produces a very specific timing problem. In a large city a family has choices about where the school day ends and where the evening starts. In Thuwal the school day ends, the campus bus or the family car covers a short distance, and then the evening has to hold dinner, a prayer, siblings, sport and whatever the Diploma has set for the week. There is no realistic option of adding a 40-minute drive to a tutoring centre in Jeddah on a Tuesday. Families who have tried it stop within a month, usually in the week the first Internal Assessment deadline lands.

So the honest answer to the question a Thuwal parent is actually asking is that the lesson has to come to the evening, not the other way round. Every lesson we arrange is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. That is not a compromise forced by geography — it is what lets an eleventh-grader on this campus work with a Physics HL specialist who has marked the paper, instead of whoever happens to live within reach of the north coast road. The argument for online here is the same argument a research group makes for collaborating with the best person on a problem rather than the nearest one.

This page is built syllabus-first, because that is where the marks are. It starts with how the Diploma and Cambridge IGCSE are assessed paper by paper, then works outward: where marks are lost, what the campus evening will actually allow, what tutors around Thuwal and north Jeddah advertise per hour, what the single-school situation means when a subject cannot be staffed, and how a Diploma earned here turns into a university place either inside the Kingdom or outside it. Nothing on it depends on a calendar year, and nothing on it is a promise about a grade.

One more thing worth saying early, because it is the first question academic parents ask. A tutor's job on assessed work is to teach, question and give feedback on the student's own writing. On an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Middle Years Programme Personal Project, we do not draft, complete or produce any part of it. Several providers in this market quietly do. On a campus where academic integrity is the professional currency of every parent in the neighbourhood, that distinction matters more than anywhere else we work.

thuwal-kaust.programmesIntro: The KAUST School runs an international programme from the early years upward, and the families we support in Thuwal are usually dealing with one of four frameworks at a time. Each is assessed differently, and the difference decides what a tutor should actually be doing in a 60-minute slot.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Learning runs through transdisciplinary units of inquiry, and reporting is against learner-profile attributes and conceptual understanding rather than against a syllabus you can look up. Support at this age is therefore almost never about content coverage. It is about reading fluency, number sense, written structure and the habit of explaining reasoning aloud — the four things that decide how hard the Middle Years Programme feels later. The exhibition in the final PYP year is the first piece of extended independent work a child produces, and it is a useful early read on how they handle a long task.
programmes.countryNote: In Thuwal the PYP cohort is small and internationally mixed, so a class can hold children who have been taught arithmetic four different ways. A tutor's first job is usually to find out which method a child was actually taught before the family moved here, then reconcile it with the one the campus classroom uses, rather than overwriting it. English as an additional language is common and is handled as a reading and writing issue, not a behaviour one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP is assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with published descriptors. A student can know the content and still score in the middle band because they have answered the task rather than the criterion. The Personal Project in the final MYP year is a long independent piece assessed on its process journal as much as its product. Mathematics in the MYP splits into standard and extended routes, and the extended route is the one that makes Mathematics AA at Higher Level realistic two years later.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in Thuwal often have unusually strong science instincts and unusually weak command-term discipline, because the conversation at home is about what is true rather than about what the criterion is asking for. An MYP tutor for the KAUST campus spends a lot of time on criterion wording: what Criterion C actually rewards in a science investigation, why a conclusion that is scientifically correct can still miss the descriptor. That is coachable in weeks.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is examined externally, subject by subject, with a syllabus code you can hold a tutor to: 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English, 0455 Economics. Most subjects offer Core and Extended routes, and the Extended route is what a Diploma school will expect for Higher Level entry. Grading runs either A*-G or 9-1 depending on the variant the school enters. Papers are short, dense and relentlessly mark-scheme driven, which makes IGCSE the easiest level at which a well-prepared student visibly outperforms a merely competent one.
programmes.countryNote: Thuwal families arriving mid-year frequently discover that a child entered for Core Mathematics at a previous school needs Extended to keep Higher Level open. That move is realistic in Year 10 and hard in the second half of Year 11. IGCSE Extended Mathematics 0580 support is the single most common request we see from this campus, usually with the non-calculator paper as the specific worry.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subject grades run 1-7 for a maximum of 42 points, with up to three further points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix, giving 45. Each subject carries internally assessed work worth a fifth or so of the grade, with the rest on written papers sat in the May session for schools on a northern-hemisphere year. Higher Level is not Standard Level plus extra topics; in several subjects it changes how the shared content is examined.
programmes.countryNote: An IB Diploma tutor in Thuwal is usually brought in for one of three reasons: a Higher Level science or mathematics subject the campus cannot staff with a specialist that year, an Internal Assessment that has stalled, or a student who arrived after the Diploma started. All three are solvable, but they need different plans, and the third needs the most honesty about what two terms can recover.

thuwal-kaust.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Thuwal families ask for most, with what each one is actually assessed on. The pattern is consistent: the subjects that need outside teaching here are the ones where the campus has one specialist rather than three, and the ones where an Internal Assessment can quietly eat a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level this is two long papers plus Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper worth a fifth of the grade, and the exploration. Paper 3 is where Higher Level students who have only practised routine questions come apart, because it asks them to build an argument across an unfamiliar context. A Mathematics AA HL tutor in Thuwal spends most of the first term on proof, series and calculus technique, and most of the last on Paper 3 structure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy work, with the graphic display calculator treated as a tool rather than a last resort. Standard Level suits students heading for economics, business, psychology and most social sciences. Where it goes wrong is interpretation: a correct regression with no sentence explaining what it means scores badly. University engineering courses frequently expect Analysis and Approaches instead, so the choice needs making with the destination in view.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two written papers plus a scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Marks go missing in the extended-response questions, where a student writes what is true instead of what the mark scheme is paying for, and in uncertainty treatment, which is examined more tightly than most students expect. Higher Level adds depth that changes how shared topics are questioned rather than simply appending new ones.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The most requested science on this campus, and the one where parental expertise helps least, because university chemistry and Diploma chemistry reward different things. The data booklet is allowed and underused. Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics are the three areas where a term of structured practice moves a grade. Chemistry HL Internal Assessment feedback is a request of its own here, usually arriving three weeks later than it should.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with command terms that decide the mark: 'outline', 'explain' and 'evaluate' are three different jobs and students answer all three the same way. The scientific investigation needs a question narrow enough to generate real data and a variable the student can genuinely control, which is where most stalled Biology Internal Assessments actually failed.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper-based theory alongside a substantial internally assessed solution. Students on this campus often code well above the level the course asks for and then lose marks on documentation, success criteria and the design stage, because the assessment rewards the engineering process rather than the cleverness of the program. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and resource management.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three papers at Higher Level, including quantitative work, plus a portfolio of commentaries on real news articles. Diagrams carry marks and most students draw them carelessly: unlabelled axes and a missing new equilibrium cost more than a weak paragraph. Higher Level policy evaluation is the part that separates grades, and it is taught, not absorbed.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis, a comparative essay, an internally assessed oral built on a global issue, and at Higher Level an additional essay. The oral is where students on an international campus either shine or improvise, and improvisation is visible to an examiner. Extract choice and the link between text and global issue are decided weeks before the recording, not on the day.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: For students who use English confidently but did not grow up in it, which describes a good share of this campus. Reading comprehension, writing in a specified text type, and an individual oral on a course theme. The commonest avoidable loss is text type: a blog, a letter and a report are marked on conventions a student can learn in two sessions and otherwise ignores.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary subject that can count as either a science or an individuals-and-societies choice, which makes it useful for a student juggling a crowded Diploma. It rewards systems thinking and penalises vagueness; answers need named examples, and the Red Sea and coastal development around this part of the Kingdom supply unusually good ones.

thuwal-kaust.igcseSubjectsIntro: Cambridge IGCSE requests from Thuwal cluster around the subjects that gate Higher Level entry two years later. The syllabus code matters: a tutor who knows the subject but not the code is guessing at the paper structure.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
igcseSubjects.description: The Extended route is what Diploma schools expect for Higher Level mathematics. The current Extended route includes a non-calculator paper, which catches out students whose arithmetic has been outsourced for years. Algebraic manipulation, not topic knowledge, is the usual weak point.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
igcseSubjects.description: Short-answer and structured papers plus an assessment of practical skills. Mole calculations and ionic equations are where grades are decided, and both respond quickly to drilled practice rather than re-reading notes.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625)
igcseSubjects.description: Formula recall is only the entry fee. Marks go on units, significant figures, graph work and the specific wording of explanation questions. Students who are strong at mathematics often underperform here because they skip the written reasoning.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610)
igcseSubjects.description: Heavy on precise definitions and process sequencing. Examiners reward the exact term, so a nearly-right word scores nothing. Diagram labelling and experimental design questions are the fastest places to recover marks in a short run-up.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (0500)
igcseSubjects.description: Reading response and directed writing against tight assessment objectives. The commonest loss is summary technique: students narrate instead of selecting, and lose half the available marks before style is considered.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Definition, diagram, application, evaluation — in that order, every time. Students who answer in paragraphs without diagrams cap themselves. Data-response questions reward reading the figures before writing anything.

thuwal-kaust.regionsTitle: Thuwal, the campus, and the coast either side of it
thuwal-kaust.regionsIntro: Distance decides the evening here more than it does anywhere in Riyadh or Jeddah. These are the places families we support in this part of Makkah Province actually live, and what each one does to the hour a lesson can start.

regions.name: The KAUST campus residential districts
regions.note: Walking and cycling distance to the school, which is the single biggest scheduling advantage any family in the Kingdom has. A student can be home within minutes of the bell, which makes a 4.30pm or 5pm start genuinely workable rather than theoretical.

regions.name: Thuwal town
regions.note: The fishing town the campus grew next to, with a short drive to the gate. Families here manage the same evening window as campus residents, with a little more travel either side of the school day and more local prayer-time structure to fit a slot around.

regions.name: King Abdullah Economic City (KAEC)
regions.note: South along the coast, a planned city with its own residential districts and port. A commute of this length pushes a realistic lesson start past 6pm on a school night, and makes a Friday or Saturday session more attractive than a second weekday evening.

regions.name: Rabigh
regions.note: North of Thuwal on the Red Sea, with industrial and university employment of its own. Families here are often weighing boarding or weekly accommodation nearer a school, and an online slot is frequently the only way to keep a specialist subject supported during term.

regions.name: Dhahban
regions.note: On the road between Thuwal and north Jeddah, where a number of commuting families settle. The run south in afternoon traffic is unpredictable, so slots here are usually set later and pinned, rather than agreed loosely around an expected arrival time.

regions.name: Obhur, north Jeddah
regions.note: The northern end of Jeddah's coastal spine and the nearest substantial cluster of international schools. Some Thuwal-adjacent families school children here and absorb a long daily run, which compresses the evening to a single workable slot.

regions.name: North Jeddah
regions.note: Roughly 80 km south of Thuwal and the practical alternative school market for this coast. Families comparing the campus school with a Jeddah option are usually comparing subject availability at Higher Level rather than facilities.

regions.name: Makkah
regions.note: About 80 km east of Jeddah and inland from this coast. Families with ties in both places plan around Hajj and Umrah seasons, when travel across the region slows and a fixed online slot is easier to keep than a journey.

schoolClusters.city: Thuwal and the campus itself
schoolClusters.note: The KAUST School serves the campus community and is the school almost every family on this page is dealing with. Its intake is highly international and its cohorts are small, which is a real strength for attention and a real constraint on how many specialists any one subject can have in a given year. Students we support attend it; we have no connection to it.

schoolClusters.city: North Jeddah and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: The nearest alternative market, roughly 80 km south, and the one families compare against when a subject at Higher Level is not available on campus. Several of these schools run the Diploma, Cambridge courses or both, and their term dates differ from each other and from the Ministry of Education school year.

schoolClusters.city: Riyadh and the Eastern Province, where campus families transfer to and from
schoolClusters.note: Research contracts move families inside the Kingdom as well as out of it, and a transfer from Thuwal usually means a different board, a different term structure and a different set of Higher Level options. Knowing the receiving school's subject list before the move is worth more than any amount of catching up afterwards.

thuwal-kaust.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as ecosystem context for families choosing support in this part of the Kingdom. No affiliation, endorsement or relationship with any named school or group is implied.
thuwal-kaust.modesIntro: Four ways families on this campus actually use tutoring. All of them are one-to-one over live video, and all of them are built to fit inside the evening window the school run leaves behind.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject
modes.description: A fixed 60 or 90-minute slot on the same evening each week, pinned to Arabia Standard Time, running alongside the school's own scheme of work. This is what most Thuwal families start with and what most of them keep: predictable enough that the student stops negotiating about it, frequent enough that a misunderstanding does not survive a fortnight.
bullets: Same tutor, same slot, agreed in local time so a clock change abroad does not move it
Homework set between sessions and marked before the next one
A short written note to the parent after each session, naming what was covered and what was weak
Paused rather than cancelled during a long school break, with the slot held

modes.title: Two subjects in one evening
modes.description: Where a student needs Chemistry and Mathematics, two 60-minute sessions back to back with a break between them usually works better than two separate evenings. It costs one evening instead of two, which matters when the window is as short as it is here, and it suits students who find the switch into study mode harder than the study itself.
bullets: Two different specialists rather than one tutor stretching across both subjects
A fixed gap between sessions so the second one is not wasted on fatigue
Useful in the term before a series, less useful in the first term of DP1
Reviewed after a month, because not every student can hold two hours

modes.title: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay review
modes.description: Short, scheduled sessions around a draft the student has already written. The tutor reads it against the published criteria, asks the questions the supervisor will ask, and names what is missing. The student then rewrites it. We do not draft, complete or produce any part of assessed work, and no tutor will touch the document itself.
bullets: Feedback mapped to the criterion letters and their mark allocations
Research question and variable tested for feasibility before data collection starts
A record of what was discussed, so the school can see the work is the student's own
Timed to the school's own internal deadlines, not to ours

modes.title: Intensive block before a series
modes.description: A compressed run of sessions in the weeks before the May session or the June series, built around past papers and mark schemes rather than content. Suited to a student whose knowledge is adequate and whose technique is not. It is the least useful mode for a student who is genuinely behind on content, and we will say so rather than sell it.
bullets: Past paper under timed conditions, marked against the real scheme, then taught from the errors
Typically three to five sessions a week for a short block, not an open-ended commitment
Works best when started around eight weeks out, not two
Scheduling moves to mornings during school study leave

sections.heading: How these qualifications are actually assessed, paper by paper
paragraphs: Start here, because everything else on this page follows from it. A Diploma subject grade is built from written papers sat externally and from internally assessed work marked by the school and moderated by the IB. In the current science guides the internally assessed scientific investigation is worth a fifth of the subject grade, with the remainder split across two written papers. In Mathematics, the exploration carries the same weight, and Higher Level adds Paper 3 — an extended problem-solving paper worth a fifth of the grade on its own. That single structural fact is why Higher Level mathematics cannot be prepared for with the same routine as Standard Level.

Cambridge IGCSE works differently. There is no equivalent of the Diploma core, each subject is graded in isolation, and most subjects offer Core and Extended routes with different papers and different grade ceilings. A student entered for Core cannot be awarded the top grades, which is why the Core-to-Extended decision in Year 10 has consequences two years later at Higher Level. Practical science skills are assessed, and the mark scheme for an explanation question is specific enough that a scientifically sound answer in the wrong register scores nothing.

The practical consequence for a family in Thuwal is that tutoring should be organised around components, not around subjects. 'Help with Chemistry' is not a plan. 'Paper 2 extended response technique, then the investigation's data analysis, then equilibrium calculations' is one, and it can be sequenced against the school's own deadlines. When a tutor cannot tell you which component they are working on in a given month, they are teaching the subject and hoping the marks follow.

It also changes what a parent should ask for in writing. A first session that produces a component-by-component read on where the student stands is worth more than four sessions of general revision, and it gives you something to measure against at the end of a term.
bullets: Internally assessed work is typically a fifth of a Diploma subject grade — it is not optional practice
Higher Level mathematics carries an extra extended paper that rewards unfamiliar problems
IGCSE Core and Extended have different papers and different grade ceilings
Ask any tutor which component they are working on this month
