sections.heading: Where Thuwal students most often lose marks
paragraphs: On a campus where a large share of parents are working scientists, the failure pattern is distinctive and it is not a knowledge problem. Students here frequently understand the physics better than the paper requires and then write an answer that an examiner cannot pay for. The mark scheme is a contract: it lists what must appear, in what terms, for each mark. A true statement that is not on the list earns nothing, and a correct final answer with no working loses the method marks on the way to it.

Command terms are the second recurring loss. 'State' wants a sentence. 'Outline' wants a sequence. 'Explain' wants a mechanism with a because in it. 'Evaluate' wants both sides and a judgement. Students who have been praised at home for insight tend to answer every one of those with an argument, which over-answers two of them and under-answers the others. This is learnable in a handful of sessions, and it is the highest-yield thing a tutor can fix in a first term.

The third is the internally assessed piece, and it fails early rather than late. A scientific investigation with a research question too broad to produce controlled data cannot be rescued by good writing three weeks before the deadline; it has to be narrowed before data collection begins. The same applies to a mathematics exploration with no genuine mathematics in it, and to an Extended Essay research question that cannot be answered in four thousand words. Most stalled coursework on this campus was lost at the question stage.

Fourth, and specific to a small cohort: students here get less exam-condition practice than students in a large school, simply because there are fewer mock sittings and fewer peers to compare against. A timed paper marked honestly against the real scheme is the cheapest diagnostic available, and it is the thing most families only start doing once a report has already gone home.
bullets: Correct science in the wrong register scores nothing — the mark scheme is a list, not a judgement
Four command terms, four different answer shapes; most students use one
A coursework question that is too broad is a question problem, not a writing problem
Small cohorts mean fewer timed sittings, so timed practice has to be arranged deliberately

sections.heading: What the school run in Thuwal does to the hours a lesson can occupy
paragraphs: This is the part rival pages never write, because they are reusing copy from a city. In Thuwal, where a family lives inside a radius of a few kilometres changes the realistic start time of a lesson by ninety minutes, and that decides whether a weekly slot survives past the first month. A student who walks home from the campus school can begin at 4.30pm, eat afterwards and still be in bed at a sane hour. A student travelling back from a school in north Jeddah cannot begin before 6.30pm without the session being a negotiation about homework that has not been started.

The second factor is prayer times, which move through the year and are not negotiable. A fixed slot that sits comfortably one month can collide the next, which is why we set slots against the family's own stated window rather than against a standard timetable, and revisit them each term. The third is siblings: in a small community one family often has three children in three programmes, and the evening cannot hold three separate sessions. Stacking two subjects on one evening and leaving the next clear is usually better than spreading four sessions across four nights.

Fourth is the campus rhythm itself. Research schedules are not school schedules, and a parent who wants to sit in on the first session of a new subject has to be able to find it in their own day. Slots that land immediately after the school day are easiest for the student and hardest for the parent; slots after 7pm are the reverse. We would rather set that trade-off deliberately than discover it in week three.

The table below is what families in each location have actually settled on. It is a planning aid, not a rule — but if your proposed start time is an hour outside the band for where you live, the slot will slip, and it is better to know that before the term starts than after.

sections.heading: Sunday to Thursday, Arabia Standard Time, and a tutor in another country
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are the weekend. That single fact invalidates most tutoring copy written for a British or Indian audience, where Monday to Friday is assumed and Sunday is treated as a rest day. A tutor based abroad who offers you a Monday-to-Friday timetable has not understood that your Sunday is a school night and your Thursday evening is a Friday one.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not observe daylight saving, so the clocks here never move. Tutors in countries that do change their clocks will drift by an hour twice a year unless the slot is pinned to Saudi local time in writing. We pin it. The practical effect is that a tutor in the United Kingdom finds your evening harder in their winter than in their summer, and a tutor in India finds it easy all year because the offset is a constant thirty minutes short of three hours in the other direction.

What this means for matching is simple: a tutor's own working week decides whether a stable slot exists at all. A classroom teacher in Europe is finishing their school day as your evening begins, which works. A tutor in East Asia is well into their night. A tutor in North America is at breakfast, which suits a Friday or Saturday morning session here and nothing on a school night. None of this is a reason to accept a non-specialist who happens to live nearby; it is a reason to check the clock before you fall in love with a profile.

The table sets Arabia Standard Time against the time zones most of our tutors actually work in, using a 7pm Thuwal start as the reference point, which is the most commonly requested slot from this campus.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Thuwal and north Jeddah, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are advertised rates, not averages, and they come from the providers themselves. Treat them as the band a family will see when they start asking, not as a measurement of the market. Tutoring platforms list general online tutoring from around SAR 55 an hour and budget IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. Tutor marketplaces quote general private tuition in the Kingdom's large cities at around SAR 50 an hour at primary level and SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring companies advertising IB subject support quote from roughly SAR 180, with Higher Level and premium tracks around SAR 200 to 220. International providers quoting in dollars land near sixty dollars an hour.

What moves the number, in order of weight: subject scarcity first, then examiner or marking experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels, then package length. A Mathematics AA HL or Physics HL specialist costs more than a Mathematics SL tutor in every market on earth, because the pool is smaller. A tutor who has marked the paper charges for knowing what the scheme pays for. Higher Level costs more than Standard Level, which costs more than MYP, which costs more than IGCSE. And travel loading is real: an in-home rate has a drive priced into it, which is one reason online one-to-one is usually the cheaper line on a like-for-like comparison.

For Thuwal specifically there is a sixth factor nobody advertises: the local pool is tiny. A family here is not choosing between twelve nearby Chemistry HL tutors on price; there may be nobody. That is exactly the situation in which an advertised in-home rate is irrelevant and an online specialist is not a downgrade but the only genuine option. We publish no price on this page because the figure depends on subject, level and length of commitment, and quoting one number for a Chemistry HL examiner and an IGCSE Biology tutor would be dishonest.

Two practical pieces of advice. Ask what the rate buys beyond the hour — marking between sessions, a written note to the parent, past papers and schemes — because providers differ enormously and the cheap hour often has nothing attached to it. And be sceptical of any rate presented as a discount for booking a long package before a single lesson has happened.

sections.heading: A single-school town: what the campus cannot always staff, and what happens when a family arrives mid-course
paragraphs: In a city with a dozen international schools, a subject the school cannot run is a reason to consider a different school. In Thuwal it is not, because the campus school is the school. A small cohort means a subject may run with one teacher, or may not run at all in a given year if too few students choose it. That is not a criticism of the school — it is arithmetic that applies to every small international school in the world — but it changes what outside support is for. Here it is often the difference between a student taking Higher Level in the subject they need for university and taking something else.

The subjects most commonly affected are the ones with the smallest natural uptake and the scarcest specialist pool: Higher Level physics, Higher Level mathematics in the Analysis and Approaches route, Computer Science at Higher Level, and second-language options outside the obvious ones. A family planning a Diploma on this campus should ask the school in the MYP years which Higher Levels have actually run in recent cohorts, rather than which appear on a subject list. The answer shapes subject choice more than any tutoring decision will.

The mid-course arrival is the other situation this town produces more than most. Research contracts begin when they begin, and children land in the middle of DP1 or two months into Year 11. A mid-course arrival into DP1 is recoverable, usually in a term, provided three things are faced honestly: which topics have been taught and not met, what internally assessed work has already been started and under what deadlines, and whether the previous school's board matches the new one. A move in the second half of DP2 is a different conversation and we will not pretend otherwise.

What actually works is a written map in the first fortnight: the subject guide, the school's scheme of work, the topics covered so far, and the internal deadlines for every piece of assessed work. Students arrive with a vague sense of being behind. The map converts that into a list, and a list can be worked through. Without it, a term of tutoring goes on whatever the student happened to mention that week.
bullets: Ask the school which Higher Levels have actually run, not which are listed
Scarce Higher Levels are where an outside specialist changes a university option

sections.heading: From a Diploma on this campus to a university place: equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili
paragraphs: This is the largest gap in the Saudi tutoring market, and it matters for Thuwal families in both directions — those staying in the Kingdom and those leaving. A foreign or international secondary certificate, the IB Diploma included, needs an equivalency decision — mu'adalah — from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university will treat it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. The same applies to A Levels and to an American high school diploma. It is an administrative step with its own requirements and timing, and families routinely discover it in the final school year rather than the one before.

Alongside the certificate sit the Qiyas tests. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, and it tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content. It can be sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects — mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English — and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That is the sentence a Thuwal parent needs: the material overlaps with a Diploma science, but the framing, sequencing and vocabulary do not. A strong Chemistry HL student can meet a Tahsili chemistry question and not recognise the house style.

Universities then publish their own admission criteria combining school grades with the Qiyas results, and the weightings differ by university and by programme. Competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes lean hardest on Tahsili. We do not publish thresholds or formulas on this page, because they differ by institution and change, and a number repeated from a third-party site is worse than no number. Read the criteria on the university's own admission pages, and read them in the year before the application, not during it.

For families heading out of the Kingdom, the Diploma travels well on its own, but the subject detail decides offers: Higher Level prerequisites, whether Mathematics AA or AI is accepted for an engineering course, and how Diploma points map onto a conditional offer. Tahsili preparation for international-curriculum students and an overseas application are not the same project, and a family should decide which one they are running before DP2 begins. Doing both badly is a common and avoidable outcome.
bullets: Ministry of Education equivalency for an IB Diploma is a separate step from any admission decision
Qudurat tests reasoning; Tahsili tests national-curriculum subject content
Tahsili's framing, not its difficulty, is what unsettles international-curriculum students
Check weightings on the university's own admission pages; we publish none

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the Personal Project
paragraphs: Every piece of internally assessed work in the Diploma and the Middle Years Programme must be the student's own. Schools require authenticity declarations, supervisors keep records of what was discussed, and plagiarism detection is routine. A breach is not a bad grade; it is a malpractice case that can cost the whole Diploma. On a research campus this is not an abstract risk — it is the same standard the parents are held to professionally, which is why we state our line explicitly rather than leaving it to be inferred.

What a tutor may do: teach the underlying content, explain the assessment criteria and their mark allocations, test whether a research question is answerable with the data or sources available, ask the questions a supervisor or examiner will ask, point at a paragraph and say that it does not evidence its claim, and teach the student how to fix a category of problem so they can fix the rest themselves. What a tutor may never do: write, draft, rewrite, complete or produce any part of the document, supply text to be pasted in, or hand over a model answer for the student's own title.

The practical version is a feedback loop the school can see. The student submits a draft they wrote. The tutor responds with questions and named criterion gaps. The student rewrites. A record of that exchange exists. If a school ever asks how the work was supported, the answer is documented and ordinary. Several providers in this market advertise coursework completion in all but name, and a parent who cannot tell the difference should ask one question: will you put anything into my child's document? The only acceptable answer is no.

This also changes what good looks like earlier in the process. Most coursework problems are feasibility problems, and feasibility is decided before any writing happens. A tutor who reads a research question in week one and says it cannot be answered has done more for the grade than one who polishes a doomed draft in week ten.
bullets: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback; the student writes every word
Criterion letters and their mark allocations are teachable and most students never see them
Keep a record of feedback so the school can see support was legitimate
Ask any provider directly whether they will put text into the document

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Not 'maths help' but 'Mathematics AA HL, Paper 3 and the exploration', or 'Extended Mathematics 0580 with the non-calculator paper as the worry'. Name the school and the year group too. On a campus this size the subject and level alone usually tell us which teacher's scheme of work the student is following and what the term's deadlines look like.

process.title: We match on syllabus, then on the clock
process.description: We look for a specialist in that exact subject and level first, and only then check whether their own working week can hold a stable Thuwal evening slot. A perfect tutor in the wrong time zone is not a match. You get the tutor's subject background and examining experience before the trial, so you can ask about it rather than take it on trust.

process.title: A free trial lesson, used as a diagnostic
process.description: The first session is not a sales call. The tutor works through a real past-paper question or a current piece of coursework, finds out what the student can and cannot do, and ends with a component-level read: what is secure, what is weak, and what order to fix it in. You get that in writing. If the fit is wrong, say so and we match again.

process.title: A fixed slot, pinned to Arabia Standard Time
process.description: We set the weekly slot against your stated evening window and write it down in Saudi local time, so a tutor abroad changing their clocks does not move it. Prayer times and term rhythms shift through the year, so the slot is reviewed each term rather than assumed to hold forever.

process.title: Short written feedback after every session
process.description: What was covered, what the student got wrong, what has been set for next week. Parents on this campus read these properly, which is useful: it means a drifting plan is visible in a fortnight rather than at the end of term. Raise anything that looks off and the plan changes.

process.title: Review at the end of each term, honestly
process.description: We look at whether the component we targeted has actually moved, using marked work rather than impressions. Sometimes the answer is to continue, sometimes to change tutor, and sometimes to stop because the student no longer needs it. We would rather lose a slot than keep billing one that has done its job.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not the nearest available adult
whyPoints.description: In a town with one school, the local pool for Higher Level Physics or Mathematics AA may be nobody at all. Online one-to-one removes the radius from the problem entirely, so the question becomes whether a tutor knows the paper rather than whether they can reach Thuwal on a Tuesday evening.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Sunday-to-Thursday week
whyPoints.description: Your Sunday is a school night and your Thursday evening is the weekend. Slots are set against that week and pinned to Arabia Standard Time, so a tutor in a country that changes its clocks does not quietly drag your lesson an hour later in their autumn.

whyPoints.title: Component-level plans, not general revision
whyPoints.description: Every plan names the paper or the criterion it is working on and the order it will work through them. That makes progress measurable against marked work at the end of a term, and it makes it obvious when a tutor is covering the subject rather than the assessment.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Feedback on the student's own drafts, mapped to the published criteria, with a record of what was discussed. No drafting, no rewriting, no model answers on the student's own title. On a research campus the distinction is not a technicality, and we would rather state it on the page than in the small print.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what a term can do
whyPoints.description: A mid-course arrival into DP1 can usually be brought level in a term with a topic map and a deadline list. A move late in DP2 is harder, and an intensive block cannot replace content a student has never been taught. We say which case you are in before you commit, not after.

whyPoints.title: No price, no promise, no score claim
whyPoints.description: We quote per subject and level rather than publishing one number that would be wrong for most families, we make no claim about grades or admissions, and we publish no statistic we cannot evidence. The SAR figures on this page are other providers' advertised rates, named as such.

faqs.question: Does a Diploma earned at a school in Thuwal still need Ministry of Education equivalency before a Saudi university will consider it?
faqs.answer: Yes. A foreign or international secondary certificate needs an equivalency decision — mu'adalah — from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, and that holds whether the Diploma was awarded in Thuwal, Jeddah or abroad. The same applies to A Levels and to an American high school diploma. It is an administrative process with its own documentary requirements, so start it in the year before the application rather than during it, and check the current requirements with the Ministry directly rather than relying on a third-party summary.

faqs.question: Why does Tahsili feel unfamiliar to a Thuwal student who is already strong in Chemistry HL?
faqs.answer: Because Tahsili's content follows the Saudi national curriculum, while your child has spent two years inside an IB subject guide. The chemistry overlaps substantially, but the sequencing, the vocabulary and the question style do not. A student used to writing extended explanations against command terms meets a shorter, more direct question format and loses time working out what is being asked. Tahsili preparation for international-curriculum students is therefore mostly translation work: mapping what they already know onto the way the test frames it, then drilling the format until it is automatic.

faqs.question: Is Qudurat sat in Arabic or English, and does that choice matter for a family that moved to the campus from abroad?
faqs.answer: Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is available in Arabic and in English, and it is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment. It tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content. For a family whose child has been schooled in English throughout, the English version usually removes an unnecessary variable, but the verbal reasoning sections differ in character between the two languages, so the sensible step is to work through official practice material in both and choose on evidence rather than on assumption.

faqs.question: Our research contract may end before DP2 finishes — how do we keep the Diploma usable for universities outside the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: The Diploma itself is portable, so the risk is not the qualification but the continuity of the internally assessed work. Before any move, get written confirmation of what has been submitted, what has been marked and what deadlines are outstanding in each subject, and ask the Diploma Programme coordinator how a transfer would be handled with the IB. Keep the subject guides and the school's scheme of work. For overseas applications, check Higher Level prerequisites early, because whether a course accepts Mathematics AI or insists on AA is settled long before the application.

faqs.question: Does Mathematics AA or Mathematics AI matter more for the engineering courses Thuwal parents tend to aim at?
faqs.answer: For engineering, many universities expect Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, because the course assumes the calculus and proof content that route carries. Applications and Interpretation suits economics, business, psychology and many social sciences, and some engineering faculties accept it, but you cannot assume it. The decision is made in the MYP years, not in DP1, so check the published entry requirements for two or three target courses before subjects are locked in. Changing route after the Diploma has started is possible and expensive in time.

faqs.question: What should an MYP student at the campus school have in place before Diploma subjects are chosen?
faqs.answer: Three things. Algebraic fluency sufficient for the extended mathematics route, because that route is what makes Mathematics AA at Higher Level realistic. A working grasp of criterion wording, so the student answers what the descriptor asks rather than what they know. And one completed long piece of independent work — the Personal Project serves — so you have seen how they handle a deadline nobody else is managing for them. Subject enthusiasm matters, but those three predict the Diploma experience more reliably than interest does.

faqs.question: Our child joins the campus school in Year 10 — is there time to move from Core to Extended Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics?
faqs.answer: In Year 10, usually yes, and it is worth doing if Higher Level mathematics is a possibility later, because Core caps the attainable grades and Diploma schools look for Extended. The work is almost always algebraic manipulation rather than new topics, plus getting comfortable without a calculator. Expect a term of focused work alongside the normal course. In the second half of Year 11 the same move is much harder, and at that point the better conversation is about which Diploma mathematics route is realistic rather than about the entry tier.

faqs.question: What does the first term of DP1 actually need to achieve for a student in Thuwal?
faqs.answer: Four things, in this order. Secure the content that the rest of the course builds on, because Diploma subjects are cumulative and a gap in the first term reappears in the final papers. Learn the command terms and what each one pays for. Choose and narrow the internally assessed question in at least one subject, so the work is not all compressed into DP2. And establish a weekly rhythm that survives the campus evening window. Points and predicted grades are not the first-term job; habits and foundations are.

faqs.question: How late into DP2 can a Thuwal student add a second tutored subject without it backfiring?
faqs.answer: Adding a second subject early in DP2 is usually fine. Adding one in the final term rarely helps, because the limiting factor by then is the student's available hours rather than their access to teaching, and a new subject takes time away from the one that was already improving. If two subjects are genuinely weak late in the course, the better move is to concentrate on the one where technique rather than content is the problem — technique moves faster — and to be explicit that the other is being managed, not fixed.

faqs.question: When should Internal Assessment work begin for a science subject at a small school like this one?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's deadline implies, because the stage that decides the grade is choosing and narrowing the research question, and that stage has no deadline attached to it. Aim to have a feasible question and an identified independent variable settled a term before data collection is due. In a small cohort, laboratory access and equipment are shared, so a question that needs a specific apparatus is competing with classmates for it. A question that cannot generate controlled data cannot be rescued by good writing later.

faqs.question: What do tutors around Thuwal and north Jeddah advertise per hour, and what makes one rate higher than another?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates in this market run from around SAR 35 an hour on budget IGCSE platforms and around SAR 55 for general online tutoring, up to SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects, with IB subject support advertised from roughly SAR 180 and Higher Level tracks around SAR 200 to 220. Those are providers' own published figures, not a market average. What moves a rate is subject scarcity first, then marking or examining experience, then level, then travel, then package length. Near Thuwal, scarcity dominates everything else.

faqs.question: Is a small group class with other campus families better value than one-to-one for Physics HL?
faqs.answer: Rarely, for Higher Level physics specifically. The reason families lose marks in that subject is individual: one student cannot handle uncertainties, another writes true statements the mark scheme will not pay for, a third is fine until Paper 2's extended responses. A group has to teach to a common gap, and the common gap is often nobody's real gap. Groups do work for content catch-up on a shared topic, for exam-technique sessions where the errors genuinely are universal, and for Theory of Knowledge discussion, where more voices help.

faqs.question: What happens to our weekly slot and our fee when the family leaves Thuwal for the long summer break?
faqs.answer: Lessons can be paused for a long break with the slot held, which matters more here than in a large city, because a specialist in a scarce Higher Level subject may not be free again in the autumn term if the slot is released. Tell us the dates as early as you have them. Fees are per lesson or per agreed block rather than an open subscription, so a pause is not a payment for nothing. If the family is relocating rather than travelling, that is a different conversation and the sooner it happens the better.

faqs.question: Before we commit to a term of lessons from Thuwal, what actually happens in the free trial?
faqs.answer: The tutor spends the session working, not selling. They take a real past-paper question or a live piece of coursework, watch how your child approaches it, and probe the places where the approach breaks down. The session ends with a component-level read: what is secure, what is weak, what to fix first and roughly how long that should take. You get that in writing, and it is useful even if you do not continue. If the match feels wrong, tell us and we match again rather than asking you to persist.

thuwal-kaust.closingHeading: Start with the subject, the level and the component
thuwal-kaust.closingBody: Tell us what your child is sitting and where it is going wrong — Mathematics AA HL and Paper 3, Chemistry and a stalled investigation, Extended Mathematics 0580 and the non-calculator paper — and we will match a specialist who teaches that exact course, then check their working week against your evening. The trial lesson is free and is used as a diagnostic, and you get the read in writing whether you continue or not. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, Sunday to Thursday, pinned to Arabia Standard Time. If no specialist in that subject is free at a workable hour, we will tell you that rather than offer a generalist.

top-ib-tutors.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are listed by subject and level, which is the pairing that matters once you know which term you are hiring for. A diagnostic appointment and a pre-series appointment are different jobs.

intro.heading: Hire for the term you are in
paragraphs: Nobody searches for a tutor in the abstract. The search happens because something specific landed: a report, a mock mark, a subject choice form, a relocation, a set of results. Which of those triggered it tells you more about the teacher you need than any ranking could. A student eight weeks from a written series needs paper technique under time pressure. A student in the first weeks of the Diploma needs somebody to find out what IGCSE actually left behind. Those are different people, and hiring the wrong one wastes a term.

Saudi families also carry a complication that most tutoring copy ignores. Two school calendars run side by side in the same city. Ministry of Education schools work a two-semester year that opens in late August and closes in late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. International and British-curriculum schools set their own dates, and most run three terms. A family with children in both systems is managing two sets of holidays, two sets of report cycles and two sets of deadlines.

Layered on top is the school-system question. Private and international schools in the Kingdom operate under a licence from the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Those documents describe institutions. They say nothing about whether a particular campus can staff Physics at Higher Level this year, which is the question that actually sends families looking for an outside teacher. There is no equivalent paperwork for tutors at all. No Saudi body licenses them, ranks them or keeps a register, so any claim to be among the top is a sentence a provider wrote about itself. What can be checked is narrower and more useful, and the right check changes with the term you are hiring for.

The last piece of the calendar is the one families discover too late. An IB Diploma is a foreign certificate in the Kingdom, and a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national secondary certificate only after an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education. The Qiyas tests, Qudurat and Tahsili, sit alongside it. Both the paperwork and the test preparation have a place in the school year, and neither belongs in the final term.

Lessons for Saudi families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. No tutor is sent to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is also what makes term-by-term hiring possible, because a family in Jazan or Tabuk can book a Chemistry Higher Level specialist for eight weeks in the spring without anyone needing to live within driving distance of the house.

top-ib-tutors.programmesIntro: The programme a student is in changes when outside teaching is worth starting. These are the three run by Saudi IB schools, with the point in each where families usually call.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects, three at Higher Level. Most of the grade comes from written papers in the May session, with internally assessed work in nearly every subject. Calls cluster in the autumn term of the first year and again after the first mocks.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision is concentrated in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province, so a family elsewhere may be at the only school within reach that offers it. Subject availability, not school quality, forces the outside hire.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups marked against criterion strands rather than by examination, finishing with the Personal Project. With no series to count back from, the useful trigger is the report cycle: two consecutive reports flagging one strand.
programmes.countryNote: A number of Saudi schools run the middle years without a Diploma above it, so Year 11 brings a decision about moving school or board. Starting that conversation a term earlier keeps the options open.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led teaching with descriptive reporting and no external examinations. The calendar matters less here; the transition year does. Weak written English or shaky number fluency carries forward into the middle years.
programmes.countryNote: Primary places are the easiest to find across the Kingdom, including cities with no secondary international provision. Families often use the final primary year to choose the city the secondary years happen in.

top-ib-tutors.subjectsIntro: Subjects differ in how late a student can usefully join them. These are the ones Saudi families ask about most, noted for what a mid-year start actually involves.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The hardest subject to join late, because each topic assumes the algebra of the one before. A spring arrival needs the foundation rebuilt first.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: More forgiving to a late start, since the statistics and modelling blocks are self-contained. Interpretation and written commentary are where marks go.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level carries topics with no Standard Level equivalent, so a level change mid-year leaves a measurable hole. Definitions are examined strictly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The internally assessed investigation sets the real deadline, usually earlier than families expect. Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most requests.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Joinable at almost any point because the content blocks stand alone, but the volume makes a late start a scheduling problem.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work and essay structure transfer from almost any curriculum; the content does not. A transferring student needs one prescribed topic rebuilt.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case studies are the transferable currency, and an arrival from another board often has strong skills attached to the wrong examples.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Productive skills under time limits decide the grade, so weekly speaking practice beats extra class time. Late joiners lag on written register.

sections.heading: The year counted backwards from a written series
paragraphs: Every useful hiring decision in the Diploma runs backwards from the papers. The May session is the one Saudi IB schools sit; Cambridge and Edexcel candidates here sit the June series and the November series. Working back from whichever applies gives a set of fixed points: when internal deadlines fall, when mocks land, when predicted grades are finalised, when entries close. Your school's examinations officer and Diploma coordinator hold the exact dates, and they differ between schools in the same city.

The table below sets those fixed points against what a tutor is actually for at each one. The pattern it exposes is that the most valuable hire is usually the earliest, and the most common one is the latest. A family who books in the autumn term of the first Diploma year buys diagnosis and foundation work; a family who books after the final mocks buys technique, which is real but narrower. Both are worth doing. They are not interchangeable.

Two of those fixed points are not academic at all. Entries close several months ahead of a written series, and a resit decision has to clear that window rather than the results date. Equivalency paperwork for a Saudi university sits in the same category: a process that runs on documents and can be started long before the final grades exist. Putting both into the calendar at the start of the final year removes the two most common sources of avoidable panic.

sections.heading: Two calendars in one city, and why it matters for booking
paragraphs: Ministry of Education schools run a two-semester year. It opens in late August and closes in late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break along the way. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars, and most of them run three terms with holidays that do not line up with the Ministry pattern. Two schools on the same Riyadh road can therefore be teaching and on holiday in different weeks.

For a family with children in both systems this is not a curiosity. It decides when a weekly slot is actually usable, when a catch-up block can be dense without colliding with a school trip, and when a tutor's own availability is worth locking in. It also explains why a generic term-dates page is useless here. The only calendar worth planning against is the one the student's own school publishes, and it is worth downloading at the start of the year rather than looked up each time.

Ramadan adds a predictable shift without a fixed date. It moves roughly eleven days earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, so across a student's school career it drifts through every term. School days shorten while it runs and evening patterns change, which moves a seven o'clock slot rather than cancelling it. Agreeing that shift a few weeks ahead with the tutor, in writing, is the difference between a slot that survives and one that quietly disappears for a month.

sections.heading: What a licence and an ETEC evaluation report tell parents
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom operate under a licence from the Ministry of Education. Separately, school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for approving the international accreditation bodies that schools choose to work with. A school offering the Diploma holds authorisation from the IB organisation for that programme specifically. Reading all three together tells a parent a great deal about an institution.

What none of them covers is subject-level staffing in a particular year. A campus can hold every document in good order and still be unable to run Physics at Higher Level because the one teacher who could left in the summer. That is the single most common reason a Saudi family ends up hiring an outside teacher, and it is invisible in any of the paperwork. The question has to be asked directly, and the answer is worth having in writing before an enrolment form is signed.

It also bears saying plainly that none of these bodies regulates tutoring. There is no national register of private tutors in Saudi Arabia, and IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from the Ministry, from the Commission or from the IB organisation. A provider implying otherwise is misrepresenting something checkable. What can be checked about a tutor is narrower and more useful: the syllabus taught, the level, the number of cohorts, and whether they have marked written papers for a board.

sections.heading: Arriving mid-course: what a transfer costs by the term it happens in
paragraphs: Relocations into the Kingdom rarely respect term boundaries. A student arriving into the first Diploma year in the autumn has lost weeks; a student arriving in the spring of the final year has lost a scheme of work and most of the internal assessment runway. The cost is not the same, and pretending otherwise is how families end up disappointed. The honest first step is a comparison of two documents: what the previous school had covered, and what this class has covered.

That comparison produces a gap list, and the gap list is the plan. Skills usually transfer better than content: a History student from another board brings source technique and needs one prescribed topic rebuilt; a Mathematics student brings nothing useful if the algebra underneath was taught differently. Internally assessed work started elsewhere is the hardest case, because the new school's coordinator decides what can be carried over and what restarts, and that conversation should happen in the first week rather than the second month.

The practical answer to a late arrival is density, not duration. Three sessions a week until the gap list clears, then a single weekly slot, costs less overall than a year of weekly lessons that never quite catch up. Where the arrival is very late in the final year, the honest conversation is about which subjects to protect and whether a November series entry is the better route. No tutor can recover two years in one term, and a provider who says otherwise is selling hours.

sections.heading: Equivalency and the Qiyas tests belong in the calendar
paragraphs: A Saudi university treats an IB Diploma, an A Level certificate or an American high school diploma as equivalent to the national secondary certificate only after an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education, known as mu'adalah. Because the process runs on documents rather than on grades, it can be started well before results exist. Some universities also state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept, which matters for a student taking a gap year or a late resit.

The Qiyas tests are separate and sit with the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, through its National Center for Assessment. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught content, and is sat in Arabic or English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, with content drawn from the Saudi national curriculum. International-curriculum students often find Tahsili the harder of the two, because the material overlaps their own syllabus while the framing does not.

Timing is the whole point of putting this in a calendar-led page. Mapping the national-curriculum topic list against what a student has actually studied is a term's work, not a fortnight's, and it sits best in the year before applications rather than alongside final paper practice. No numeric threshold or university weighting appears here: they differ by institution and by programme, and the university's own published criteria are the only reliable source. No tutor can promise an admission outcome.

sections.heading: What top can honestly mean where no register exists
paragraphs: Since no Saudi body ranks or licenses tutors, a claim to be among the top is a marketing sentence rather than a finding. What replaces it is a short set of checkable facts about one named teacher, and the useful ones change with the term you are hiring for. For an autumn diagnostic appointment, the question is how many cohorts of that exact syllabus and level the tutor has taught, and what they found in the last student who arrived at this point in the course. Breadth of experience is the thing being bought.

For a pre-series hire the question shifts to marking. A teacher who has marked written papers for a board has read several hundred attempts at one question and knows which phrasing is paid for and which is not. Ask which papers, and how recently. For an internal assessment appointment, the question is a boundary: what the tutor will and will not do with a draft. A clear limit, stated without being asked, is the strongest signal available in this market.

One check works in every term. Give the tutor a question the student lost marks on and ask what the mark scheme wanted. The answer separates a subject specialist from a well-meaning graduate faster than any credential list, because it cannot be rehearsed. A good answer names the command term and the structure the examiner is paid to look for. A weak answer explains the topic again, which is what the school already did.

sections.heading: Fitting a weekly slot into the Sunday to Thursday week
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, and Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 with no seasonal clock change. Both facts have practical consequences. A tutor in India is two and a half hours ahead, so a seven o'clock lesson here is a late one there. A tutor in the United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer, which means an unpinned slot moves twice a year without anyone deciding to move it.

The fix is mechanical. Record the slot as a Kingdom local time, confirm it in writing on both sides, and let the tutor absorb their own clock changes. Families who agree a time verbally in the tutor's local terms find out in the first week of a shift, usually by missing a lesson. The same discipline applies to the school calendar: holiday weeks are agreed from the student's own published dates, not from a generic term list.

Which evening to choose depends on the term. Early in a term, Sunday works well because no homework has accumulated, but there is little marked work to review. Later, a midweek slot gives the tutor something recent to work from. Thursday suits setting substantial written work for the weekend and suits quick correction poorly. In the final weeks before a series, two shorter sessions beat one long one, because paper practice needs marking time between attempts.

faqs.question: Which term is the realistic one to move a student from a British school into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The start of the first Diploma year is the clean move, because subject and level choices are still open and nothing has been internally assessed. A move in the spring of the first year is workable with a gap list and a dense catch-up block. A move into the final year is a different decision entirely, and the school's Diploma coordinator has to confirm what internal work can be carried over before anyone agrees to it.

faqs.question: What does a national-curriculum student have to build before IGCSE assessment makes sense?
faqs.answer: Written technique in English, mostly. The content overlap is larger than families expect; the gap is in how answers are rewarded. Command words, the structure a mark scheme pays for, and writing at length under time pressure are the three things that need building, and they take a term rather than a fortnight. Confirming the tier the school intends to enter the student for matters as much, because Core entry caps the grade available.

faqs.question: An American-curriculum student is joining Higher Level sciences late. What is actually missing?
faqs.answer: Usually depth in two or three topics rather than breadth across the course, plus the internally assessed investigation, which has a school deadline that may already be close. Laboratory skills generally transfer. The specific risk in Higher Level Physics and Chemistry is the topics with no Standard Level equivalent, since those are taught once and assumed thereafter. Compare the two schemes of work before deciding which level is realistic.

faqs.question: What happens to internally assessed work already started at the previous school?
faqs.answer: The receiving school's coordinator decides, and the answer varies by subject and by how far the work had progressed. Some components transfer with documentation, some restart. Ask in the first week of the move rather than waiting for a deadline notice, because a restart changes the whole term's plan. A tutor can help the student rebuild a research question and review their own draft, but cannot produce the work or carry it across.

faqs.question: Is it better to finish IGCSE at the old school or restart the board after a move to the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: If the student is within one series of finishing, completing the existing entries is almost always cheaper in effort than restarting. If more than a year remains, matching the new school's board avoids two part-finished courses. Entries belong to a school, so the examinations officer at both ends has to confirm what can transfer. That conversation is more useful than any general rule, and it has to happen before entry deadlines pass.

faqs.question: What should a family ask a Saudi school about subject availability before signing the enrolment form?
faqs.answer: Four questions, answered in writing. Which Higher Level options will actually run next year, not which are listed. How many students a set needs before it opens. Who teaches the subject, and how long they have taught that syllabus. And what happens if the set does not fill. Schools answer these honestly when asked directly, and the answers decide whether an outside teacher is a convenience or a requirement.

faqs.question: What does an ETEC evaluation report tell a parent that a licence does not?
faqs.answer: A licence from the Ministry of Education establishes that a school may operate. Evaluation and accreditation through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission is about quality judgements against standards, which is a different question. Read together they describe governance, provision and how the school is assessed. Neither document says whether a named teacher will be in front of your child in a particular subject next year, which is the thing parents are usually trying to find out.

faqs.question: Why do some Riyadh families drive to a school in another part of the city?
faqs.answer: Because programme and subject availability are not evenly spread. Riyadh is roughly an hour across in traffic, and a family will accept that commute for a campus running the Higher Level combination their child needs. The same logic produces the opposite choice elsewhere: a family accepts a nearer school with a narrower offer and buys the missing subject as online one-to-one teaching instead of spending two hours a day in the car.

faqs.question: What happens when a school cannot run a Higher Level option it advertised?
faqs.answer: The set usually does not open, and students are moved to Standard Level or to a different subject. It is a staffing and numbers problem rather than a broken promise, and it happens in strong schools. The practical response is to ask early, keep a second choice viable, and treat an outside specialist as the fallback for the subject that matters most. A level change mid-course leaves gaps in subjects where Higher Level content is taught once.

faqs.question: How do compound and camp schools in the Eastern Province differ from city schools?
faqs.answer: Their calendars and cohorts follow employment patterns rather than a city rhythm. Families arrive and leave mid-year with work postings, so classes change composition more than they do in a city school, and the study week is shaped by compound schedules and shift patterns. Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran behave as one school market, so a student may live in one city, attend school in another, and need an evening slot that accounts for both.

faqs.question: When in the autumn term should a weekly slot be booked to be useful by the spring?
faqs.answer: Within the first three or four weeks of term, which is early enough that the first diagnostic uses recent marked work and late enough that there is some. Booking in the final weeks of the autumn term buys mock preparation rather than foundation work, which is a narrower purchase. Specialist availability also tightens as a term progresses, and the scarcer the subject and level, the earlier that happens.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry's midyear break line up with an international school's holiday?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. Ministry of Education schools run a two-semester year with a midyear break, while most international and British-curriculum schools run three terms and set their own dates. Two schools in the same district can break in different weeks. For a family with children in both systems, the only workable approach is to take each child's holiday weeks from their own school's published calendar and agree the lesson pauses from that.

faqs.question: How many weeks before a written series does intensive work need to start?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is the shape that works for paper technique: long enough for several full timed papers with marking time between them, short enough to hold a student's attention. Content repair needs longer, which is why the diagnostic matters more than the start date. Starting earlier with a weekly slot and converting to an intensive block in the final eight weeks is the pattern most families find manageable alongside school revision.

faqs.question: Can a family keep the same weekly slot through a relocation between Saudi cities?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, since the whole Kingdom is on Arabia Standard Time with no clock change and lessons are delivered online. What changes is the school run and sometimes the school calendar, so the time of day may need moving even though the time zone does not. Tell the tutor the new school's published dates, because a move between a Ministry school and a three-term international school changes which weeks are holidays.

intro.heading: The IGCSE year makes more sense read backwards
paragraphs: Searches for top IGCSE tutors in Saudi Arabia peak in the term before the papers, which is the term in which the fewest things can still be changed. Nothing published ranks tutors, so the word itself cannot be checked from the outside. What can be checked is whether the person in front of you knows where your child sits in a two-year course and which decisions are already closed. That is a calendar question, and this page answers it by running the IGCSE year backwards from the examination series rather than forwards from today.

Counted that way the order is clear. The papers are the end point. A few weeks before them, only recoverable marks are in play. Several months before them, entries close and the tier on every tiered subject is fixed, along with the grade ceiling it carries. A few months earlier again, mock results decide predicted grades and whatever set changes a school can still make. And a full year before that, option choices decide which subjects a student sits at all.

Set against that sequence, most tutoring in this market is bought in the last two months. The hours are not wasted, but they are bought at the point where the fewest levers remain. A family that understands the countdown can spend the same money earlier and get considerably more for it. It can also ask a prospective tutor the one question that separates a specialist from a generalist: what is still open at this point in the year, and what is already settled? A tutor who answers that question with a date rather than a reassurance is usually worth the premium.

The second thread running through this page is what schools in the Kingdom can and cannot staff. Private and international schools are licensed by the Ministry of Education, with school evaluation and accreditation running through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Neither process tells a parent whether one subject has a specialist teacher. In most Saudi cities the senior Cambridge or Edexcel cohort is small enough that a subject runs as a single set, sometimes with one teacher covering two sciences, and that is the gap outside teaching exists to fill.

Lessons at IB Gram are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, on Arabia Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For a family in Al Ahsa, Tabuk or Buraidah that distinction is the difference between reaching a specialist and not reaching one, because the countdown does not slow down to suit a city with a single international school in it. The rest of this page works through that countdown, stage by stage.

sections.heading: Counting the IGCSE year backwards from the series
paragraphs: Nobody publishes a ranking of IGCSE tutors, so the phrase cannot be verified from outside. What can be verified is whether a tutor knows where your child sits in the course and what is still open. That is a calendar question, and the calendar in this market runs backwards. Entries close months before the papers. Tiers are fixed at entry. Mock results set predicted grades. Option choices a year earlier decide which subjects exist at all. A tutor who cannot name those points is guessing at the plan rather than building one.

The table below runs from the series back through the year. Read it downwards and the mismatch becomes obvious: almost everything that decides a grade is settled before the final term, and almost all tutoring is bought after it. That is why so many families feel they paid for an expensive few weeks that barely moved the number. The hours were real teaching. They were simply bought at the point in the year when the fewest things were still changeable, which is a scheduling problem rather than a quality one.

Two notes on dates. Series are named by month rather than by year here, because the pattern repeats: the June series is the main sitting for schools in the Kingdom, and the November series carries resits and November-entry candidates. And no date on this page replaces your own school's. Term structures differ between international schools and schools following the Ministry of Education calendar, and the entry deadline belongs to the examinations officer. Ask for the real dates in writing, then count backwards from them.

sections.heading: The entry deadline is the hinge of the whole year
paragraphs: Entries for a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel series close several months ahead of the papers, and the school makes them. That single administrative act fixes more than most families realise. It fixes which subjects a candidate sits. It fixes which components they sit inside each subject. And on a tiered subject it fixes the tier, which fixes the ceiling: a Core entry in a Cambridge subject is graded C to G and cannot be awarded above a C, while an Extended entry runs A* to E.

So the useful conversation about tiers happens before the deadline rather than after the mock. A student placed in a Core set in the autumn because they were struggling may be a credible Extended candidate by the spring, and the decision is reversible only while the entry is still open. Schools are usually willing to discuss it when a family asks early and brings evidence, and much less able to help when asked two weeks after entries have gone. That alone is an argument for buying teaching in the first half of the year.

Ask the examinations officer three things in writing. Which board and syllabus code each subject is entered under. Which tier, where the subject is tiered. And which components make up the entry, because a candidate who does not know they are sitting a practical paper will not revise for one. None of those questions is unusual and all of them are answered from a database in a few minutes. The families who never ask are the families who find out from the statement of entry, by which point the year is set.

sections.heading: Mock season, and what the school does with the result
paragraphs: School mocks usually land a few months ahead of the series, and they are the most consequential internal assessment of the whole course. The marks do several jobs at once. They inform set changes where a school still has flexibility. They inform tier decisions where the entry is still open. They are the main evidence behind a predicted grade for a post-16 application. And they tell a family, for the first time, what a candidate can actually do alone against a clock rather than with a textbook open.

Ask for the script, not the percentage. A predicted grade is a professional estimate rather than a promise, and the way to engage with one is to ask which components it rests on and what evidence would change it. Where a prediction is being used for a sixth-form or Diploma application, timing matters more than usual: the application may be decided before the next internal assessment, so a disputed prediction needs the conversation immediately rather than in the summer term when nothing can be revised.

What a tutor does with a mock script is a fair test of whether they are worth a premium. The useful output is a short list naming the components that lost marks, each tagged as a content gap, a method problem or a command-term error, with the recoverable ones placed first. The unhelpful output is a plan to revise the whole subject from the beginning. By mock season there is no time for that, and the candidate most at risk is the one working hard on the topics they already know well.

sections.heading: What a school in the Kingdom cannot staff, and when a family finds out
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. Neither process says anything about an individual teacher's specialism in one subject. A school can be properly licensed, well evaluated and still unable to staff Additional Mathematics, because the constraint is the local labour market rather than compliance with anything.

The practical consequence shows up as a single set. In most Saudi cities the cohort entering Cambridge or Edexcel at senior level is small, so a subject runs once, with one teacher, and occasionally with Core and Extended candidates in the same room. If that teacher is a generalist covering a second science, the class is usually taught competently and the examination technique for the harder component is often missing. Families find this out at the mock, which is late in the countdown but not fatal to the year.

This is the honest argument for outside teaching in the Kingdom, and it is a different argument from the one made in London or Dubai. The gap is not that the school is weak. It is that no school can keep a specialist for every subject a handful of candidates choose, and a non-specialist science teaching set is the normal result. Ask the school directly who teaches the senior set and how long they have taught that specification. The answer criticises nobody and tells you exactly what to buy.

sections.heading: Arriving mid-course from another system
paragraphs: Families relocate into Riyadh, Jeddah, the Eastern Province, Tabuk and NEOM part-way through a school year, and a child arriving into Year 10 or Year 11 from another system faces two problems at once. The content sequence is different, so topics have been covered in a different order and some have not been covered yet. And the assessment style is different, which is usually the larger problem of the two. A student can know the material and still lose a third of the marks to command terms and mark-scheme structure.

What transfers depends on the system left behind. A student from a Saudi national-curriculum school generally arrives with solid mathematics and needs technical English in the sciences built quickly. A CBSE or ICSE student arrives with strong content coverage and little experience of structured extended answers. An American-curriculum student has breadth and often needs depth in one or two topics. A British-curriculum student switching between Cambridge and Edexcel mid-course keeps most of the content and inherits a different component list, which is an admin problem before it is a teaching one.

Timing decides what is realistic. Joining in the autumn of Year 10 is an ordinary admission. Joining in the spring of Year 11 means triage on two or three components rather than a syllabus plan. Coursework already completed elsewhere rarely transfers cleanly, and that is a question for the new school's examinations officer before it is a question for any tutor. Ask what has been entered, what is outstanding, and what the school expects the family to arrange for itself. Then count the weeks that are left.

sections.heading: Twelve months back: the option-choice window
paragraphs: A year before the papers, the decisions being taken are not about revision at all. They are about which subjects exist. Option choices, set allocation and provisional tier placement happen in the year before the examination year in most schools here, and they bound everything that follows. A student who drops a science cannot pick it up later in the course. A student placed in a Core mathematics set carries a ceiling that will matter a great deal when post-16 choices arrive two years later.

Two choices deserve particular attention in the Kingdom. The first is mathematics, because Extended Mathematics, and in some schools Additional Mathematics on top of it, is the gate to a mathematical post-16 route including Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. The second is the sciences, where a student aiming at a competitive science programme later needs those subjects on the certificate rather than good grades in easier ones. Neither decision is reversible at the point it begins to matter, which is the whole problem with it.

This is also the cheapest point in the entire course to buy teaching, and the one families almost never use. A term of work on algebraic fluency and technical English in Year 9 changes the ceiling on every mark that follows it. The same money in the final term redistributes a handful of marks between topics. That is an uncomfortable thing to read if the papers are eight weeks away, and it is the single most useful thing to know if they are not.

sections.heading: Fitting the countdown into a Sunday-to-Thursday week
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, and the countdown has to be scheduled against that rather than against a Monday-to-Friday assumption imported from elsewhere. A Sunday evening session lands on a school night with homework due. A Thursday session is the end of the week, when a student is least able to absorb new content and best placed to sit a timed paper. Those are different hours and they suit different work.

Arabia Standard Time is three hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. Tutors in countries that do will see the slot move twice a year unless it is written as a Saudi local time. A tutor in India sits two and a half hours ahead and never shifts, so an evening lesson there is stable all year. A tutor in the United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer, which quietly moves a six o'clock lesson by a whole hour.

The table sets out how the weekly shape should change as the series approaches. The column worth reading twice is the last one, because knowing what to stop doing is the harder half of the problem. Thirty weeks out, following the school's teaching closely is exactly the right work. Six weeks out, the same activity is comfortable and almost useless. A fixed slot booked early is also easier to protect: popular evening hours in a scarce subject are gone long before the final term begins.

faqs.question: Moving from a Saudi national-curriculum school into Year 10 IGCSE, what has to be rebuilt first?
faqs.answer: Usually the language of the sciences rather than the science. Students arrive with workable mathematics and then lose marks because the question is written in technical English they have to decode before answering. Build subject vocabulary and the command terms in the first term, in parallel with content, and expect written answers to improve more slowly than calculations do. The mathematics itself often needs notation and layout work rather than new teaching.

faqs.question: How much of a CBSE or ICSE Class 9 year counts towards a Cambridge IGCSE entry?
faqs.answer: Content-wise, a great deal; procedurally, nothing. The entry is made by the new school for the subjects and tiers it enters, and prior years do not carry credit. Most students arriving from those systems know more content than their new classmates and score below them at first, because the papers reward structured extended answers against a mark scheme rather than recall. That is a technique gap and it closes with practice and feedback.

faqs.question: Can a student arriving from an American high school go straight into Year 11 IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it is the hardest version of the move. A one-year entry means covering two years of a specification while classmates revise it, and the sciences are where the depth gap shows most. Ask the admitting school which components it would enter, whether any coursework is still open, and whether a Core entry is being considered. If one year is genuinely too short, a November entry or a different year placement is the better conversation.

faqs.question: What does a British-curriculum student lose by switching board part-way through the course?
faqs.answer: Not much content, and potentially a lot of time. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel cover similar ground with different component lists, different tiering rules and different question styles. The risk is an untaught component rather than an untaught topic: a practical or alternative-to-practical paper the old board handled differently, or coursework that does not transfer. Get the new component list in writing and audit it against what has already been taught.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject is hardest to join a term late, and why?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics, followed by the sciences at Extended tier. Additional Mathematics assumes Extended Mathematics content that may not have been taught yet, and it moves quickly. In the sciences, the practical or alternative-to-practical component needs a term of method work that cannot be compressed. Languages and humanities are more forgiving, because a late arrival can still learn structure and case studies fast enough to be examined on them.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education actually license, and what does ETEC evaluate?
faqs.answer: The Ministry licenses private and international schools to operate. School evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which also operates services for approving international accreditation bodies. Both work at the level of the institution. Neither certifies an individual teacher's specialism in one subject, and neither certifies tutors at all, so no provider can honestly describe itself as approved by either of them.

faqs.question: Why does a school in the Kingdom run one Extended set and no second one?
faqs.answer: Because the cohort is small. Outside the largest cities a senior Cambridge or Edexcel year group may be a few dozen students across all subjects, which supports one set per subject and one teacher. Where numbers are tighter still, Core and Extended candidates share a room and a timetable slot. It is an arithmetic constraint rather than a quality one, and it explains why outside specialist teaching is normal here.

faqs.question: What should a family ask a school before moving a child for the sake of one subject?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which board and tier that subject is entered under. Who teaches the senior set and how long they have taught that specification. Whether the subject runs as one set or two. And whether any component is delivered as self-study or online rather than taught. A school that answers all four plainly is usually a better bet than one with a stronger prospectus and vaguer answers.

faqs.question: Our school teaches a science through a non-specialist, so what can outside teaching realistically fix?
faqs.answer: Technique and the harder components, reliably. Content coverage, partly. What it cannot fix is laboratory experience, so the practical or alternative-to-practical paper has to be taught through other people's method and data rather than through experiments. Expect a weekly hour to raise performance on extended-response and calculation questions first, because those are where a non-specialist set most often loses marks it could keep.

faqs.question: Why do families in the Eastern Province commute between Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran for school?
faqs.answer: Because the three cities behave as a single school and labour market. A family may live where the work is and attend school where the curriculum or the subject list fits, and the drive between them is routine. The practical effect on tutoring is that a school's calendar and its neighbour's may not match, so lesson scheduling has to follow your own school's term dates rather than a regional assumption.

faqs.question: How far back from the series does a weekly slot need to be booked to still exist?
faqs.answer: For a common subject, a few weeks' notice is usually enough. For a scarce one, think in terms of the autumn term. Specialists in Additional Mathematics, Extended Physics and the less common languages hold a small number of evening hours, and those fill from the start of the school year. If a family knows in the autumn that a subject will need help in the spring, booking the slot then costs nothing and secures the hour.

faqs.question: What does a lesson week look like twelve weeks out from the papers?
faqs.answer: One taught hour, one timed question set done independently, and that work marked and returned before the next session. New content only where a named gap justifies it. The hour itself should be spent on the marked work rather than on fresh teaching, because at twelve weeks the fastest gains come from correcting how answers are written. Reading through notes should have stopped being the main activity by this point.

faqs.question: The Kingdom does not change its clocks, so whose slot moves and when?
faqs.answer: The tutor's. Arabia Standard Time is fixed at three hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time all year, so a lesson agreed as a Saudi local time never moves for the student. A tutor in a country that shifts its clocks will find the same lesson an hour earlier or later in their own day twice a year. Write the slot in Saudi time and the problem stays with the person best placed to absorb it.

faqs.question: Our school moved its internal examination week, so can a fixed slot move with it?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, for a defined period, and it is worth asking early rather than on the day. A tutor holding several fixed hours can often swap two students for a fortnight. What is harder is a permanent change at short notice, because the released hour is normally taken quickly. Agree at the outset how much notice a temporary move needs, and keep the original slot as the one to return to.

top-igcse-tutors.closingHeading: Get the dates, then count backwards
top-igcse-tutors.closingBody: Ask your school's examinations officer for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the entry deadline, then count backwards from the series. Send us that, the year group and the most recent marked script, and we will put forward a tutor who teaches the specification and can say what is still open at this point in the year. The trial lesson is free, and lessons run online.
