intro.heading: Start from the marks, not from the timetable
paragraphs: Most families search for a weekend IB tutor because the weekday evenings are gone. School finishes late, the traffic is what it is, and by the time a Diploma student sits down on a Tuesday there is an hour before fatigue wins. That is a real constraint, and it is worth planning around. But it is the second reason to book a weekend. The first is that several of the ways IB students lose marks cannot be fixed in sixty minutes at all, and a family that books a weekend slot for convenience alone usually ends up buying a longer version of the same weekday lesson.

Consider what actually goes wrong. A Higher Level candidate loses marks across a whole paper because they have never finished one inside the time limit; the fix is a full timed paper and a mark-scheme walkthrough, which is a three-hour job. A student knows the content and writes a list when the question says evaluate; that is a command-term problem which needs a dozen past-paper stems in one sitting, not one a week. An Internal Assessment has drifted off its research question; the diagnosis takes the best part of an hour before any teaching starts.

None of those fit a weekday evening, and all three are routine. This page is built the other way round from the usual vendor page: it starts with the specific losses, then says what each one needs, and only then deals with when it can run and what it costs. The order matters because it changes what you buy. A parent who books two hours on a Saturday to fix pacing is purchasing something measurable; a parent who books it to feel organised is purchasing a habit.

There is a scheduling fact behind all of this that most copy on this subject gets wrong. The weekend in the Kingdom is Friday and Saturday. For a tutor in India, the UK or Europe, Friday is an ordinary working day and Saturday is their own weekend. That asymmetry is useful rather than awkward once you see it: Friday is the easiest weekend day in the Kingdom to staff from abroad, and Saturday is the one where availability thins and the family has least room to negotiate.

One thing is fixed. Lessons for Saudi families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Riyadh, Jeddah or anywhere else in the Kingdom; home visits are a service offered only in India. For long weekend work that is an advantage rather than a compromise, because a three-hour block with a Physics Higher Level specialist is available from a screen and is not available from whoever lives twenty minutes away.

sections.heading: The five marks a weekday hour never gets to
paragraphs: Pacing is the first. A candidate who has never completed a paper inside its time limit loses marks evenly across the back half of every paper they sit, and the loss is invisible in topic tests because topic tests are short. Nothing diagnoses this except a whole paper, timed, finished. An hour on a Tuesday can rehearse a question type; it cannot show a student that they spent nineteen minutes on a six-mark question.

The second is command terms. A student who writes a description when the stem says evaluate has not failed to learn the content, and more content teaching will not help. The fix is a batch of stems from several past papers read side by side, so the student sees that outline, explain, discuss and justify each ask for a different shape of answer. Doing one of those a week takes a term; doing twenty in one sitting takes a morning.

The third and fourth are Internal Assessment drift and Extended Essay scope, and both are diagnostic jobs before they are teaching jobs. Working out that an investigation has quietly stopped answering its own research question takes a careful read of the draft with the criteria open, which is forty minutes before a word of advice. The fifth is the error log nobody keeps: the same three mistakes recurring for two years because nobody has ever put a term's worth of marked work on one table and counted them.

sections.heading: A full paper under exam conditions, and what the marking reveals
paragraphs: A weekend block long enough for a full paper changes what a tutor can see. The student sits the paper with the correct booklet or calculator, to the real duration, with no questions asked. The tutor marks it in front of them against the published mark scheme rather than taking it away, because the value is in watching the student discover where a mark was available and not taken. That is uncomfortable, and it is the fastest teaching on the page.

Three patterns show up almost every time. Marks are lost to unfinished final questions, which is pacing. Marks are lost on parts worth one or two marks that the student skipped intending to return, which is sequencing. And marks are lost where the answer is right but the working is not shown in a form the examiner can credit, which is presentation and is the cheapest of the three to fix. Each produces a different instruction for the following week.

The output of the session should be written down: a per-question mark, the reason for each loss, and a short list of the question types to repeat. That list is the error log, and it is the thing that makes the second weekend worth more than the first. A tutor who marks a paper and discusses it warmly without leaving a record has sold a pleasant three hours. Ask for the record before the block is booked, not after.

sections.heading: Command terms and mark schemes: knowing it is not being paid for it
paragraphs: Command terms are the verbs at the front of a question, and they are the single widest gap between what a student knows and what a student scores. Describe asks for features. Explain asks for a reason attached to each feature. Compare asks for sustained reference to both things rather than two separate accounts. Evaluate asks for a judgement supported from both sides. A student who treats all four as an invitation to write what they know will lose marks in every subject on their timetable at once.

Mark schemes make this visible in a way no textbook does. Reading one next to a student's own answer shows that the credit sits on specified points, that a mark is often reserved for a comparison the student never made, and that a generous-sounding six-mark question has six separately earnable things in it. Students who have never read a mark scheme assume the examiner is judging quality. They are being paid for coverage against criteria.

A weekend block suits this work because it is cumulative. Twenty stems from one subject, sorted by command term, then two answers written to each of the two hardest, then both marked. By the end the student can say what the verb is asking for before planning the answer, which is a transferable habit rather than a fact. It is also the work most likely to lift several subjects from one intervention, which makes it unusually good value for a family buying a limited number of hours.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment drift, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Internal Assessment work goes wrong slowly. A research question is agreed, the student collects data or reads sources, and over several weeks the thing being investigated shifts a few degrees away from the question at the top of the page. By the time a draft exists the analysis is answering something adjacent, and the criteria that reward focus cannot be met however good the work is. Catching that needs the draft and the criteria read together, which is a weekend job.

What a tutor may do is specific and worth stating plainly, because this part of the market contains outright essay mills. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain what each one rewards, question whether a conclusion follows from the evidence, point out that a method has an uncontrolled variable, model an analysis on different data, and ask the questions a supervisor would ask. A tutor does not draft, rewrite, supply text or correct the work line by line, and nothing in a submission is produced for the candidate.

That boundary protects the student rather than the tutor. Malpractice findings fall on the candidate, not on whoever helped, and a school that suspects a submission is not a student's own work has processes that run to the board. Keep the student's own dated drafts, keep the supervisor at school informed that outside support exists, and treat any provider who offers to produce a finished piece as a risk to the Diploma rather than a shortcut to it.

sections.heading: The Saudi weekend against a tutor's own working week
paragraphs: The Kingdom's weekend is Friday and Saturday. Almost everywhere a specialist IB tutor is likely to live, the weekend is Saturday and Sunday. Half of the Saudi weekend therefore falls on somebody else's working day and half on their day off, and which half you book changes who is available and on what terms. Rival pages copied from Indian or British sites treat the weekend as Saturday and Sunday and get this backwards.

Friday is the easy day. For a tutor in India it is an ordinary Friday, two and a half hours behind Arabia Standard Time, so a Saudi mid-morning slot is a comfortable working morning for them. For a UK-based tutor it is a working Friday three hours behind in their winter, so a Saudi afternoon is their late morning. Availability on a Friday is therefore wide, and a long block is easier to agree than it would be on any school night.

Saturday is the harder day, because it is the tutor's own weekend too. Slots exist, they are fewer, and a tutor who teaches on a Saturday is giving up their rest day for it. Sunday, which some relocating families still think of as weekend, is a school day in the Kingdom and the first day of the student's week. The table below sets out how each option actually behaves, and a slot agreed in Arabia Standard Time will not drift when another country changes its clocks.

Two practical rules follow. Pin every slot to Saudi local time in writing, because the Kingdom does not change its clocks and several tutor countries do. And if a long block matters more than the day of the week, ask for Friday first.

sections.heading: What weekend IB tutoring is advertised at in the Kingdom
paragraphs: Every figure here is an advertised rate published by a tutoring company or a marketplace, not a market average and not a quote from IB Gram. Tutoring-platform listings for general, non-specialist online tutoring in the Kingdom start around SAR 55 an hour. A tutor-marketplace guide puts general private tuition in Riyadh at roughly SAR 50 an hour for primary work and over SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring-company listings advertise IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from about SAR 180 an hour, with Higher Level and premium tracks quoted near SAR 200 to 220.

A weekend block is priced as hours, so the sum is simple and often startling: a three-hour Saturday session at a Higher Level rate costs what three weekday evenings cost. The question is not whether that is a lot of money but whether the three hours buy something the three evenings cannot. For pacing, full-paper marking and Internal Assessment review, they clearly do. For working through a textbook chapter, they clearly do not, and a shorter weekday slot is the better purchase.

What moves the number, in order of weight: subject scarcity, examiner or marking experience, level, whether the tutor travels, and package length. In-home tuition carries a travel loading, which is a cost with no academic return. Some providers add a weekend or unsocial-hours premium and some do not, so ask directly whether Friday and Saturday fees differ from weekday ones, and whether marking a paper between sessions is billed as time. Those two answers change the real hourly cost more than the headline rate does.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor you only see once a week
paragraphs: A weekend-only arrangement gives a family fewer contact points, so the verification has to be sharper at the start. In the trial lesson, ask which subject and level the tutor teaches and for how many cohorts, which components they have marked, and whether that marking was for a school or for a board. Only one of those gives a view across many candidates. Then ask them to mark one question from your child's own work in front of you and justify each mark against the scheme.

Ask what will arrive after each block. A weekend tutor should leave a per-question record, a short note on what was diagnosed, and a named task for the week. Without that the following weekend starts from nothing, which is the commonest failure of weekend-only teaching and has nothing to do with the tutor's subject knowledge. Ask too how many weekend slots they hold, because marking a full paper properly takes real time and a tutor running six long blocks across two days is not doing it.

Finally, agree what happens when the pattern breaks. School trips, mock weeks and family travel all land on weekends, so settle the notice period for moving a block and whether a missed one is made up or lost before any money changes hands. Nobody can promise a grade, and a provider who offers one is making a claim no tutor can keep. What can be promised is a record you can read and a plan you can check.

faqs.question: Which Diploma topics genuinely need a two-hour weekend block rather than a weekday hour?
faqs.answer: Anything assessed over a long question or a whole paper. Mathematics Higher Level Paper 3, Physics extended response, Economics evaluation essays and English unseen analysis all need a complete attempt before the problem is visible. So does Internal Assessment review, where reading the draft against the criteria takes most of an hour before advice starts. Single topics, formula recall and homework questions are better value in a short weekday slot, and booking them into a long block wastes the length.

faqs.question: Why do strong Higher Level students still lose marks on the Paper 3 data question?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 3 rewards sustained reasoning rather than recall, and strong students are usually fast rather than patient. The question builds: a later part depends on a result from an earlier one, so a single arithmetic slip travels. Marks also go missing where a student reaches the right conclusion without writing the intermediate step the scheme credits. The fix is whole-question practice with the scheme open, which is why it sits in a weekend block rather than a weekday hour.

faqs.question: Where does weak algebra from the first Diploma year surface in Physics Higher Level?
faqs.answer: In rearrangement under pressure. A student who is slow to make a variable the subject of an equation loses time on every calculation question and then rushes the extended response at the end. It also shows in graph work, where gradients and intercepts have to be turned into physical quantities with units. The weakness is rarely conceptual by this stage; it is fluency, and twenty minutes of timed rearrangement at the start of each weekend block fixes it faster than more physics does.

faqs.question: How should a Saturday revision block be structured differently from a weekday session?
faqs.answer: A weekday hour should do one thing well: a question type, a topic, a correction set. A Saturday block should do a whole cycle. Sit the paper to time, mark it together against the scheme, extract the reasons for each lost mark, then teach the one that recurs most. Breaks matter at this length, and the last twenty minutes should produce the written record rather than more teaching. A long block spent as three consecutive weekday lessons wastes what the length was for.

faqs.question: How do we check a weekend tutor is a subject specialist rather than a generalist filling a slot?
faqs.answer: Ask which level and syllabus they teach, which components they have marked, and for which board. Then ask a question only a specialist can answer: what the scheme credits in a particular six-mark stem from your child's own past paper. A specialist answers in marks and criteria. A generalist answers in topics and reassurance. Weekend demand attracts people stretching outside their subject because the hours are available, so this check matters more on Friday and Saturday than midweek.

faqs.question: Should a weekend tutor be a serving school teacher or a full-time tutor?
faqs.answer: Both work, for different reasons. A serving teacher brings current classroom experience and the scheme of work as it is actually taught, but their weekend is their recovery time and long blocks may be hard to sustain. A full-time tutor can hold three-hour sessions comfortably and has usually seen more candidates across more schools. What matters more than either is marking experience for a board, which gives a view of where marks sit that one classroom cannot.

faqs.question: What does it mean if a tutor will only teach on Fridays, and should that worry us?
faqs.answer: Usually it means they are abroad and Friday is an ordinary working day for them, which is a practical answer rather than a warning sign. It becomes a problem only if your child's commitments also sit on Friday, since a single available day leaves no room to reschedule around a mock week or a school trip. Ask before booking what happens when a Friday is lost, and whether the block is made up or forfeited. Get that answer in writing.

faqs.question: How many weekend blocks can one tutor hold before the marking quality drops?
faqs.answer: Marking a full paper properly, question by question against the scheme, takes real time inside the session and some outside it. A tutor running back-to-back three-hour blocks across both weekend days is unlikely to be producing a per-question record for each one. Ask how many long blocks they hold on a Friday and a Saturday, and ask to see the shape of the written record they leave. A vague answer to either is the useful signal here.

faqs.question: What happens if a weekend tutor drops a slot two weeks before a mock series?
faqs.answer: The slot is rematched with a specialist in the same subject and level, and the error log and per-question records from previous blocks go with it so the replacement does not start from nothing. That handover is the reason the written record is insisted on from the first session. Expect a short diagnostic at the start of the first replacement block rather than straight teaching, because a new tutor has to see the work before they can usefully target the remaining fortnight.

faqs.question: What may a weekend tutor do with an Internal Assessment draft between Thursday and Sunday?
faqs.answer: Read it against the criteria and come back with questions. They may say that the analysis no longer answers the research question, that a variable was uncontrolled, that a conclusion overreaches the evidence, or that a criterion is simply unaddressed. They may model the technique on different data. They may not draft, rewrite, supply sentences or correct the text line by line, and nothing in the submission is produced for the candidate. Keep the student's own dated drafts as the record.

faqs.question: How many times can a tutor read an Internal Assessment draft over successive weekends?
faqs.answer: The limit that matters is the school's, not the tutor's: the number of formally reviewed drafts is set by the subject guide and your teacher's practice, and a tutor reading work outside that does not change what may be submitted. Practically, two careful reads with a redraft between them produces nearly all the available gain. More readings tend to move the work towards the reader's voice, which is both an honesty problem and a marking one, since criteria reward the candidate's own reasoning.

faqs.question: Where does a school's Extended Essay supervisor end and a weekend tutor begin?
faqs.answer: The supervisor owns the process: the formal reflection sessions, the record of them and the judgement that the work is the candidate's own. A weekend tutor works on the thinking around that, most usefully on narrowing a research question until it can actually be answered in the word limit, and on whether the sources will support an argument. Tell the supervisor that outside support exists. Where the two disagree on direction, the supervisor's view governs, because they sign the process.

faqs.question: Where is the line between tightening a Theory of Knowledge essay's phrasing and rewriting it?
faqs.answer: Pointing at a sentence and saying the claim is unsupported is teaching. Supplying the sentence is not. A tutor may ask what the knowledge question actually is, whether an example does the work claimed for it, and whether a counter-position has been considered honestly. They may not reword paragraphs or hand over phrasing. If a draft comes back reading better than the student speaks, the line has been crossed, and the candidate carries the consequence rather than the tutor.

faqs.question: How do we keep a dated record showing the Personal Project is our child's own work?
faqs.answer: Keep the process journal as the programme intends, with entries made as the work happens rather than written up afterwards. Save dated versions of the product and the report separately, so the sequence of thinking is visible. Where an outside tutor has been involved, note what was discussed and when. None of this is required paperwork for most schools, but it answers the only question that matters if the work is ever queried, and it takes minutes a week.

intro.heading: Start with the money, then work back from the series
paragraphs: Families looking for a weekend IGCSE tutor in the Kingdom are usually weighing two unknowns at once: what it costs, and whether there is still time. Both have answers that can be written down. On cost, the published numbers in this market come from tutoring companies and marketplaces rather than from any regulator, and they span a wide range. Budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one online from around SAR 35 an hour. A tutor-marketplace guide puts general private tuition in Riyadh near SAR 50 for primary work and above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring-platform listings for non-specialist online help start around SAR 55.

That spread is not noise. It reflects four things, in order of weight: how scarce a specialist in the exact syllabus is, whether the tutor has marked for a board, the level and tier being taught, and whether anybody has to travel. In-home tuition carries a travel loading, which is a cost with no academic return attached to it, and it is the single easiest item to remove from a family's bill. Package length moves the number too, usually less than families expect. Two things that do not move it reliably are years of experience in general and a provider's own description of its results, because neither tells you whether the tutor has taught the syllabus code your child is entered for.

On time, the answer depends on where the student sits in a year that runs towards a fixed series. Saudi candidates sit the June series as their main one and the November series for resits and November-entry candidates. Cambridge also runs a February and March series, but that series is for India only, and a Saudi family told otherwise has been given a fact they will act on wrongly. Entries close months ahead of the papers, and the tier decision closes with them.

That is why this page counts the year backwards. There is a point after which no amount of weekend teaching changes the tier a student is entered for, a point after which coursework components are fixed, and a point after which the only useful work is paper technique. Knowing which side of each line your child is on decides what the money should buy. It also stops a family paying for content teaching in a window where only timed practice will move anything.

One thing is fixed throughout. Lessons for Saudi families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Riyadh, Jeddah or anywhere else in the Kingdom; home visits are a service offered only in India. For IGCSE that removes the travel loading from the rate and widens the pool from whoever is local to whoever knows the code on the entry form.

sections.heading: What the advertised numbers actually are, and what they are made of
paragraphs: Every figure in this section is an advertised rate published by a tutoring company or a marketplace. None of them is a market average and none is a quote from IB Gram. Budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one online tuition from roughly SAR 35 an hour. Tutoring-platform listings for general, non-specialist online tutoring in the Kingdom start around SAR 55. A tutor-marketplace guide gives general private tuition in Riyadh at about SAR 50 an hour for primary work and over SAR 200 an hour for senior-school examination subjects. International providers quoting in dollars sit near sixty dollars an hour.

A family comparing those numbers is usually comparing different products. The SAR 35 figure buys access to somebody who can help with homework in a popular subject. The figure above SAR 200 buys a specialist in a named syllabus code who has marked the component in question. Between them sit most working arrangements. The honest way to read the spread is as a scarcity curve: the rarer the exact thing you need, the further right you sit, and tier and board narrow the pool before subject does.

Three costs hide outside the headline rate, and they are worth asking about before the first session. Marking a full paper properly takes time outside the lesson, and some providers bill it and some include it. Past-paper packs and worked solutions are sometimes supplied and sometimes expected from the family. And written reports, where they exist at all, are occasionally an extra. Ask for all three answers in one message, because together they move the real hourly cost more than a twenty-riyal difference in the advertised rate.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that caps a grade before any money is spent
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE is tiered on many subjects. Core is graded C to G. Extended is graded A* to E. A candidate entered for Core cannot be awarded above a C however well they perform on the day, which means the tier decision sets the ceiling before a single weekend lesson is bought. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 and does not split most subjects this way, so the same conversation at an Edexcel school is about paper choice and set rather than tier.

Tier entry is a school decision, and it is reversible only before the entry deadline. Schools make it on the evidence in front of them, which in practice means autumn-term assessments and a teacher's judgement about whether a student can handle the Extended content without the lower-tier marks collapsing. That judgement is reasonable and it is also made with incomplete information, which is why a family who wants Extended should ask what evidence would change it, and ask early enough to produce some.

The practical consequence for weekend teaching is stark. In the autumn, weekend work can genuinely change which tier is available, because the target is the evidence the school is weighing. After the entry closes, the same hours can only optimise inside a fixed ceiling. Both are worth buying; they are not the same purchase. Ask the school, in writing, for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the component list for every subject, and keep the reply. It is the single most useful document a family can hold.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Edexcel: the same subject, different papers
paragraphs: Two students in the same city studying the same subject can be sitting materially different examinations. The boards split content differently, weight components differently and, in Cambridge's case, tier where Edexcel usually does not. A tutor who knows one board well and the other by reputation will teach confidently and occasionally teach the wrong thing, which is why the code on the entry matters more than the subject name on the timetable.

The grading scales differ too, and families comparing children or schools often compare the wrong things. Cambridge Core sits on C to G and Extended on A* to E. Edexcel runs 9 to 1 across the subject without the tier split on most specifications. A grade that sounds equivalent in conversation may not describe comparable content coverage, and no informal conversion between the two should be relied on for a sixth-form application.

On the calendar the two boards behave similarly for Saudi candidates. Both run a June series, which is the main one for schools in the Kingdom, and both run a November series used for resits and November-entry candidates. Cambridge additionally runs a February and March series, but that one is India only, and Saudi candidates sit June and November. Entry windows, final deadlines and late-entry penalties are published by the boards and administered by your school's examinations officer, who holds the actual dates. Ask that officer rather than a tutor or a forum, because late entry attracts a fee and a missed window cannot be reopened. One more difference worth knowing: resit rules are specification-specific, so whether a single component can be retaken or the whole subject must be resat is a question only the board's own documentation answers.

sections.heading: The year counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Working forwards from today produces a plan that runs out of time. Working backwards from the series produces one that does not. The table below sets the stages out in reverse order, with what is still changeable at each point. No dates appear in it on purpose: entry windows and deadlines are published by the boards each cycle and your examinations officer holds the exact ones, so a date printed here would be wrong within a year and acted on anyway.

Two stages deserve emphasis. The tier and entry window is the only point at which the grade ceiling is negotiable, and it falls far earlier in the year than most families expect. Coursework and practical components, where a syllabus has them, close earlier still in some subjects. After both, the work that remains is paper technique, timing, command-term accuracy and the error log, and that work is genuinely valuable; it is simply a different purchase from content teaching.

The November series changes the arithmetic for a resit candidate. A student who misses a target in June has a window that is short and well defined, and the useful planning question is which components can be retaken and whether the whole subject must be. That is a syllabus-specific answer your examinations officer can give in one conversation. Autumn-term weekend blocks for resit candidates are therefore unusually efficient, because the diagnosis already exists in the June component marks and nothing has to be guessed at.

sections.heading: Why weekend blocks suit IGCSE catch-up specifically
paragraphs: IGCSE papers are shorter than Diploma ones, which makes a weekend slot a different tool here than it is at sixth form. A ninety-minute weekend session fits a full paper section, its marking and the teaching that follows, which is the complete diagnostic cycle. Two such slots on one day cover two subjects properly. That shape is hard to build on a school night in a city where the run home can take an hour and the student arrives with homework still to do.

The second argument is cumulative volume at the right time. A student carrying gaps in two or three subjects needs more contact hours than a weekday evening can supply without wrecking sleep, and in the eight weeks before a series that arithmetic becomes binding. Weekend double sessions are the only way most families find the hours, and they work best when they are whole papers rather than extra content, because by then the content has been taught and the losses are technique.

The third is the parent. Friday and Saturday are the days a parent can sit in on the first session or two, which is the simplest way to judge whether a tutor is teaching or performing. It is also when a family can read the written record together with the child rather than at the end of a working day. Neither of those is a scheduling detail; both change how quickly a wrong match is spotted and replaced.

sections.heading: How a weekend lesson runs, and what the parent sees
paragraphs: Sessions run over live video with a shared whiteboard. The tutor opens the past paper as the candidate will see it in the hall and the mark scheme alongside it, so working is built on screen rather than described. In maths and the sciences the student writes on paper and shows the page to camera, or writes directly on the shared board, and the annotated version is saved. Nothing depends on an install beyond a browser and a stable connection.

A full-paper session has a fixed shape. The student works to the real duration with the correct calculator or booklet and no questions asked. The tutor marks it live, question by question, against the published scheme. Then the reasons for each lost mark are sorted into pacing, sequencing and presentation, because those three have different fixes and mixing them produces vague advice. The session ends by writing the record rather than teaching more.

What reaches the parent afterwards is the test of the whole arrangement. Expect a per-question mark, a short note naming what was diagnosed, and one specific task for the week. A parent who does not teach the subject can still read whether the same error is appearing for the fourth weekend running. Ask whether lessons are recorded; where a recording is made it is shared with the family and the tutor and nobody else, and it is deleted on request. A Friday morning block is the easiest of all for a parent to sit in on, because a tutor based abroad is working an ordinary day while the family is not, so the slot is calm at both ends.

sections.heading: Choosing the tutor, and what a good answer sounds like
paragraphs: Ask three questions and the shortlist sorts itself. First: which board and syllabus code have you taught, and for how many cohorts? A specialist answers with the code and the component structure. Second: which components have you marked, and was that for a school or for a board? Only board marking gives a view across many candidates, and it is the thing most worth paying for. Third: mark one question from my child's own paper now, and justify each mark against the scheme.

That third request does more work than any credential. A tutor inside the syllabus will mark quickly, point at where a mark was available and not taken, and explain what the scheme credits rather than whether the answer reads well. Someone outside it will discuss the topic instead. Weekend demand attracts tutors stretching beyond their subject because the hours are free, so this test matters more on a Friday or Saturday than it does midweek.

Then settle the practical terms before money moves. How much notice is needed to move a block when a mock week or a school trip lands on it, whether a missed session is made up or forfeited, and what happens if the match is wrong after two sessions. No tutor can promise a grade, and a provider who offers one, or who quotes a success rate without saying how it was measured, is making a claim nobody can check. What can be agreed is a record you can read and a plan you can audit.

faqs.question: What does a weekend IGCSE lesson look like from the student's side of the screen?
faqs.answer: A video window, a shared whiteboard and the past paper open as it will appear in the hall. The student works questions while the tutor watches rather than narrating, then the two go through the mark scheme together on screen. Written working is either done on the board or on paper and shown to camera. Sessions on a rest day are usually ninety minutes with a short break, because attention rather than time is the limit on a Friday or Saturday.

faqs.question: How does a tutor open an IGCSE past paper and its mark scheme side by side?
faqs.answer: Both documents are loaded into the shared workspace, the paper on the left and the scheme hidden until the student has attempted the question. The tutor reveals the scheme afterwards and annotates both: the point where the mark was available on the paper, and the wording that earned it in the scheme. The annotated pair is saved so the student can revisit it. Seeing the two documents together is what teaches a candidate that credit sits on specified points.

faqs.question: What does a Year 10 student need at the desk before a Saturday science block?
faqs.answer: A laptop or desktop with a browser, a stable connection, headphones, blank paper, a pen and the correct calculator for their syllabus. For a timed paper they also need the data sheet or formula booklet their board permits, printed. A second device is not required but helps: a phone propped to show written working speeds up marking. Nothing needs installing, and the family should test audio once before the first block rather than during it.

faqs.question: Does a long weekend session need a second screen, and what would it be used for?
faqs.answer: It is not required and it does help. With one screen the paper, the whiteboard and the video compete for space, and younger students lose time switching. A second screen, or a tablet beside the laptop, lets the paper sit permanently in view while the working happens on the main display. Families who cannot arrange that usually print the paper instead, which works just as well and has the advantage of matching examination conditions more closely.

faqs.question: What arrives from a weekend IGCSE tutor afterwards, and how soon?
faqs.answer: A per-question record of the work done, a short note naming what was diagnosed, and one specific task for the coming week. It should reach the family within a day while the session is still fresh, not at the end of the following week. The record is what makes the next block worth more than the last, and it is also the only way a parent who does not teach the subject can tell whether the same error is recurring.

faqs.question: Why is an Extended-tier IGCSE weekend tutor quoted above a Core-tier one?
faqs.answer: Because the content reaches further and the pool of teachers who have taught and marked it is smaller. Extended papers examine algebra, trigonometry and analysis that Core never asks about, so a tutor has to be comfortable at the top of the syllabus rather than the middle of it. Advertised rates in the Kingdom follow the same pattern across subjects: tutoring-company listings price senior examination work well above general tuition. Scarcity and marking experience move the number more than tier alone does.

faqs.question: Is a block of weekend sessions priced differently from booking them one at a time?
faqs.answer: Often, and the saving is usually smaller than families expect. Package length is one of the weaker levers on price compared with subject scarcity or marking experience. The more important questions are what happens to unused sessions, whether the rate is held if the slot moves, and whether marking a full paper between sessions is inside the price. Ask all three before committing to a block, and ask what notice is needed to stop.

faqs.question: Do Friday and Saturday rates differ from weekday rates in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Some providers add an unsocial-hours premium to weekend work and some do not, so the only reliable answer is to ask directly and get it in writing. Friday is an ordinary working day for a tutor based abroad, so it rarely attracts a premium. Saturday is their own rest day, which is where a surcharge is most likely to appear. The difference is worth establishing before a long block is booked, because at three hours it compounds.

faqs.question: Do we pay for weekend blocks that fall inside the autumn break?
faqs.answer: Not if the arrangement is agreed properly at the start. International and British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom set their own calendars and most run three terms, so breaks fall at different times in the same city. Give the tutor your school's published calendar at the outset and mark the breaks you intend to skip. Families who want to keep working through a break often use it for whole-paper practice, since there is no homework competing for the time.

faqs.question: Is one three-hour weekend session better value than two weekday hours for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It depends what is being bought. For a whole timed paper, its live marking and the teaching that follows, the long session is clearly better, because that cycle cannot be split across two evenings without losing the diagnosis. For working through topics or correcting homework, two shorter slots are better, since attention fades and the content does not need a run-up. Most families end up with a weekday slot in term and long weekend blocks in the weeks before a series.

faqs.question: What should a tutor know about our school's component list before the first weekend block?
faqs.answer: The board, the syllabus code, the tier, which optional components the school has chosen and whether any coursework or practical assessment applies. Syllabuses within one subject offer different component combinations, and a tutor teaching the wrong combination will prepare a student for a paper they are not sitting. Send the school's written confirmation rather than your recollection of a parents' evening. A tutor who does not ask for this before the first session is guessing.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether a weekend IGCSE tutor has marked for Cambridge rather than Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than most families assume. The boards split content and weight components differently, and marking experience is board-specific: knowing what a Cambridge scheme credits does not tell you what an Edexcel one does. A tutor who has marked for the board your child is entered with can say where candidates lose marks on that specification. One who has marked for the other board is still useful, but should say so plainly rather than describing the experience as IGCSE marking.

faqs.question: What should we ask about tier entry in the first conversation with a weekend tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask which tier the school has entered, whether the deadline has passed, and what evidence the school said it was weighing. Then ask the tutor what work would change that evidence and how long it needs. A good answer is specific about assessments and timing. A weak one treats tier as a detail. The point is to establish early whether the hours you are buying can still lift the ceiling or can only optimise underneath one.

faqs.question: What if the weekend tutor is strong in maths but the real gap is physics?
faqs.answer: Then book a physics specialist for that subject rather than stretching the maths tutor across both. It happens most often with Coordinated or Combined Science, where one grade covers three subjects and the weakest of the three is dragging it. The usual arrangement is two separate specialists in two slots on the same weekend day, sharing one written record so neither works blind. That costs the same hours and teaches considerably better than one tutor covering ground they do not own.

yanbu.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE to students across Madinah Province. Each is matched to a single syllabus and level rather than to a subject in general, which is the difference that matters when a Yanbu school cannot staff a Higher Level option.

intro.heading: Yanbu is an industrial city, and that decides what its schools can teach
paragraphs: Yanbu sits on the Red Sea in Madinah Province, built outward from the refining and petrochemical complex at Yanbu Industrial City. The school population tracks the industrial workforce: it grows when a plant expands, it turns over when contracts end, and it is spread across a port city, a planned industrial city and the residential districts between them. None of that is a complaint about Yanbu. It is the single fact that explains why families here go looking for outside teaching, and why the usual advice written for Riyadh or Jeddah parents does not transfer.

A school's subject range is a staffing decision, not a demand decision. A cohort of twelve students spread across six subject groups cannot support a specialist teacher for every Higher Level option, so schools make choices: they run the options they can staff, and they ask families to accept the rest at Standard Level or not at all. In a city the size of Riyadh a family can shop between schools. In Yanbu the realistic alternatives are the school your child is already in, a long commute, or finding the specialist teaching separately.

That is where the search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Yanbu usually starts, and it is normally framed as a local question: who is nearby. The honest answer is that proximity is the least useful filter available to you. The pool of adults living within driving distance of Yanbu Al Bahr who have taught Chemistry at Higher Level and marked for a board is small, and it is smaller again once you add a subject your school could not staff. A family that insists on local is choosing from the shortest list in the Kingdom.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Yanbu or anywhere else in the Kingdom; in-home teaching is a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Saudi families are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Arabia Standard Time. The argument for that is not convenience. It is that your child gets the person who knows the paper, rather than the person who can reach your district by six o'clock, and that the match survives a relocation to Jubail, Jeddah or a posting outside the Kingdom entirely.

This page is built backwards from the place a Yanbu student's qualification eventually has to work: a Ministry of Education equivalency decision and a Saudi university's admission criteria, or an overseas application that reads Diploma points and Higher Level choices. Those endpoints decide which subjects matter, which level they need to be taken at, and how early the work has to start. Everything before them is logistics.

What follows sets the options against each other in a table, works through the equivalency and Qiyas route step by step, explains why the Achievement Test reads differently to an international-curriculum student, and says plainly what the market charges and who publishes those figures.

yanbu.programmesIntro: Students in Yanbu arrive from several systems at once: the IB continuum, Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE, and national-curriculum schooling. The four programmes below are the ones families here ask about most, with a note on what each means specifically for a student living on the Red Sea coast rather than in Riyadh or the Eastern Province cluster.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examinations. Progress is reported against learning outcomes rather than paper marks, which is why a parent moving in from a national-curriculum or Indian-curriculum school often cannot tell whether a child is ahead or behind. The useful work at this stage is in number fluency, reading stamina and writing at length in English, because those are the three things every later programme assumes and none of them teaches from scratch.
programmes.countryNote: In Yanbu the PYP question is usually a transfer question. A child arriving mid-primary from a system with weekly tests lands in one that reports against outcomes, and parents read that as a drop in rigour. It rarely is. What does need checking is English writing volume, since a child who has only written in short answers will struggle in the Middle Years Programme two years later.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each lettered A to D, and the Personal Project in the final year. Marks are awarded against criterion descriptors, so a student who knows the content but writes outside the descriptor loses marks and cannot see why. This is the programme where command-term discipline is either built or missed, and where the gap between understanding a topic and being paid for it on paper first becomes visible.
programmes.countryNote: Yanbu families frequently reach the end of the MYP and find the Diploma options they wanted are not running locally. That is the moment to decide whether to commute, move, or arrange the subject separately. Deciding it in the final MYP year leaves room to build the prerequisite work; deciding it after Diploma enrolment leaves a student taking a Higher Level subject nobody at school teaches.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, one from each of the six groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, giving 42 points, with up to three more from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix for a maximum of 45. Creativity, Activity, Service is a completion requirement and carries no points. Failing conditions exist independently of the total, which is why a strong total can still not award.
programmes.countryNote: A Yanbu Diploma student is often the only one in the cohort taking a particular Higher Level option, which means no classmates to compare working with and a teacher covering it alongside another course. Outside teaching here is not remedial. It supplies the second reader and the paper-specific drilling that a larger cohort in Jeddah or Riyadh gets from the room it sits in.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years per subject, examined externally, with most subjects offered at Extended and Core tier in the Cambridge version. Tier choice sets a grade ceiling, so it is a decision with consequences rather than a formality. Grades feed directly into Diploma or A Level entry, and a weak Mathematics or Science grade narrows Higher Level choices before a student has had a chance to argue the point.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom set their own calendars and most run three terms, so a Yanbu family and a Jeddah family sitting the same June series may have very different term dates and mock timings. Confirm the syllabus code your school enters your child under with its examinations officer, because Cambridge and Edexcel versions of the same subject differ in paper structure.

yanbu.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Yanbu families most often ask for, usually because the school runs them at one level only or covers them with a non-specialist. Each note says what the subject actually assesses and where marks go missing, which is more useful than a list of topics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries this course, and weakness from earlier years surfaces in calculus rather than in algebra itself. At Higher Level, proof and the extra calculus topics have no Standard Level equivalent, so a student who coasted through SL-level content hits a wall. Marks are lost in unjustified steps: the answer is right, the method is not shown, and the mark scheme pays for the method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: More modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work than Analysis and Approaches, with a heavier reliance on interpreting output rather than deriving it. Students lose marks by giving a number without the units, the context or the comment the question asked for. Engineering and some science degrees expect Analysis and Approaches, so the choice between the two is a university decision as much as a difficulty one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Higher Level course adds topics with no Standard Level counterpart, and the extended-response questions reward a stated principle before any algebra appears. Marks drain away in unit errors, in significant figures, and in explanations that describe what happens instead of why. The experimental work is assessed internally and is where students who are strong on paper most often underperform.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the usual pressure points, and the data booklet is only useful to a student who has practised finding things in it under time. Examiners pay for the specific term, not the paraphrase. The internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to generate real data, and most weak ones fail at that first step rather than in the analysis.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the difficulty: the content is wide, the definitions are examined strictly, and a near-miss definition earns nothing. Students who revise by reading score poorly on command terms like distinguish, outline and explain, which demand different structures. The statistical handling in the internal assessment is routinely the weakest part of an otherwise careful investigation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the correct label carry more marks than the surrounding prose. The evaluation requirement is where strong writers underperform, because they describe both sides without reaching a judgement the mark scheme can credit. Higher Level adds quantitative work that students treat as arithmetic rather than as economics, and lose the interpretation marks for it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are easy to name and hard to apply. The marks sit in applying a tool to the specific organisation in the case, with the figures given, rather than in explaining what the tool is. Higher Level questions expect a recommendation defended against a stated alternative, and answers that list advantages and disadvantages without choosing stop short of the top band.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The paper is not a comprehension exercise. It asks for an argument about how a text produces its effect, supported by close reference, and students trained on content-recall subjects write summary instead. The individual oral needs a global issue chosen early and a pair of texts that genuinely speak to it, which is a planning problem more than a writing one.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode under examination conditions is a separate skill from writing working code, and students who have only ever coded on a machine lose marks on paper. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and resource management topics that reward diagrams. The internal assessment is a solution for a real client, and projects fail the criteria when the client and the success criteria were invented late.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Often chosen as a lighter option and then found to be writing-heavy. It rewards systems thinking and precise use of models, and penalises general environmental opinion. The data-based questions want calculation followed by comment; students do one or the other. For a student in an industrial city, the case-study material is unusually easy to ground in something they can see.

yanbu.igcseSubjectsIntro: Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE subjects follow a different logic to the IB: tiering, syllabus codes and paper combinations vary between boards for the same subject name. The notes below are about where marks are lost, and every family should confirm the exact code and papers with their school's examinations officer.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Tier choice sets a grade ceiling, so it is the first thing to check rather than the last. Extended-tier students lose marks on bounds, surds and transformations more often than on anything algebraic. Working must be visible: a correct final answer with no method earns less than a flawed method honestly shown.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics
igcseSubjects.description: The formula sheet, where one is provided, is a memory aid rather than a method. Marks go missing in unit conversion, in graph gradients read from the wrong axes, and in explanation questions answered with a description. Practical papers reward precision about apparatus and control variables.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry
igcseSubjects.description: Ionic equations, mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables are the recurring weak points. Students who learn reactions as lists rather than as patterns cannot handle an unfamiliar compound. Examiners want the observation and the inference separately; one sentence covering both usually earns one mark.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology
igcseSubjects.description: Definitions are marked strictly and the syllabus is long. The commonest loss is answering a six-mark question in two lines. Experimental questions expect a named variable, a method of measurement and a control, and most answers supply only the first.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English
igcseSubjects.description: Directed-writing tasks fail on audience and form before they fail on grammar. The reading questions want selection and inference, not retelling, and the summary task is scored on points identified rather than on style. Timing is the quiet killer: strong students run out of paper on the final extended response.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language
igcseSubjects.description: Scored on accuracy and on range, and students who play safe to avoid errors cap themselves. The listening component rewards a specific detail rather than a general sense. Speaking is assessed on sustained development, so one-sentence answers lose marks that a slightly bolder answer would gain.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics
igcseSubjects.description: Definitions, a labelled diagram and an applied example carry most of the structured-question marks. The extended answers need a conclusion that chooses. Students who have seen the IB version of the course often over-write, since the IGCSE mark schemes reward compression.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies
igcseSubjects.description: The case study is the examination, not the context for it. Marks are given for using the data supplied: the figures, the stated objectives, the named stakeholders. Generic answers about motivation theory or marketing mix score the lower bands however accurate they are.

yanbu.regionsTitle: Yanbu's districts and the Red Sea coast around it
yanbu.regionsIntro: Yanbu is three settlements working as one city, with a wide and thinly served coast either side of it. Where a family lives changes the school run, the realistic evening slot and the honest answer to whether a local tutor exists at all. These are the places families on this coast actually ask about.

regions.name: Yanbu Al Bahr
regions.note: The port city and the old town, and where most residential districts and the schools serving them sit. Families here have the shortest school runs in the city and the largest local choice, which still means a handful of schools rather than a market.

regions.name: Yanbu Al Sinaiyah
regions.note: Yanbu Industrial City, planned around the refining and petrochemical complex. Household routines bend around shift patterns, and an evening slot that works for one parent's rotation may not work for the next block. A fixed weekly time matters more here than in most places.

regions.name: Yanbu Al Nakhal
regions.note: The inland palm settlement, older and more agricultural than the coastal districts. Distances to the city's schools are longer, which pushes a realistic lesson start later into the evening and makes any in-home arrangement expensive in travel time before it teaches anything.

regions.name: Royal Commission residential districts
regions.note: Planned housing for industrial-city staff, with amenities on site and a community that turns over with contracts. Mid-year arrivals and departures are normal, so catching up on work already covered, or keeping a tutor through a move, is a standing question rather than an exception.

regions.name: Umluj
regions.note: North along the coast, considerably smaller, with no realistic international-school choice and no local pool of IB or IGCSE specialists. This is where distance stops being an inconvenience and becomes the whole problem, and where online teaching is not a preference but the only version that exists.

regions.name: Madinah
regions.note: The provincial capital inland to the east, the nearest larger city and a different school market. Some Yanbu families with older children weigh a move or a boarding arrangement there. The commute is not a daily proposition from the coast.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST coast
regions.note: South down the coast road toward Jeddah, where The KAUST School serves the university campus community. Families relocating between the Red Sea industrial sites and the research campus often change curriculum as well as city, and the transfer questions are about what actually carries over.

regions.name: AlUla
regions.note: Inland to the north-east, growing quickly on tourism and heritage investment, with a school provision still catching up to the arriving workforce. Families posted there ask the same question as Umluj families and get the same honest answer about local specialist supply.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the coast road south
schoolClusters.note: The nearest substantial international-school market to Yanbu, and the one families look at when they decide the local option will not carry a Higher Level subject. Several of these schools appear in IB listings and some are Cambridge schools as well; term dates differ between them even within the same city.

schoolClusters.city: Thuwal, on the way down the coast
schoolClusters.note: The KAUST School serves the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology campus community north of Jeddah. For a Red Sea family it is the closest example of a campus school whose intake turns over with research contracts, which produces exactly the mid-course arrival pattern Yanbu industrial families know.

schoolClusters.city: Riyadh, for families who move inland
schoolClusters.note: A posting inland usually means a wider choice of programmes and a longer list of schools running the Diploma rather than only the Middle Years Programme. Families moving from the coast should ask each school which Higher Level options actually ran last intake, not which appear in the prospectus.

sections.heading: The three options in front of a Yanbu family, side by side
paragraphs: Before any discussion of tutors, it is worth naming what you are actually choosing between, because the options are not equivalent and the differences are not the ones advertising emphasises. A Yanbu family with a subject problem has five realistic routes: lean harder on the school's own department, find an adult locally who will come to the house, join a group class at a local centre, buy a recorded course, or arrange one-to-one teaching with a named specialist who is not in the city.

The school's department is the first place to push, and it is free. A head of department can move a student between sets, supply past papers, or arrange a lunchtime clinic. What a school cannot do is hire a Higher Level specialist for one student, and that is usually the actual problem in a small cohort. Asking the school what it can and cannot cover, in those words, saves everyone a term of polite vagueness.

The local in-home option is the one families reach for next, and the table below is the honest arithmetic on it. The pool is adults living within driving distance who have taught that syllabus at that level. In Yanbu that list is short before you add any constraint, and travel time is paid for either in the rate or in the hour. Group classes solve the cost problem by pitching at the middle of the room, which is useful for a student who is in the middle of the room and not otherwise.

The comparison is not a close call once the subject is specific. A student who needs Chemistry Higher Level internal assessment feedback and extended-response technique does not need somebody nearby. They need somebody who has marked that paper. The constraint on the online option is real but it is a scheduling constraint, not a supply one: the tutor has to be awake and working at the hour your evening falls.

sections.heading: Where a Yanbu student's qualification eventually has to work
paragraphs: Work backwards from the endpoint and most subject decisions answer themselves. A student finishing school in Yanbu applies in one of two directions, and sometimes both. Inside the Kingdom, a foreign or international school certificate is not automatically treated as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate: it needs an equivalency decision, the mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education. That applies to an IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike.

Alongside that, Saudi universities read scores from the national testing system. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, Qiyas, and tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Each university then publishes its own admission criteria combining school grades with those scores, and the weightings differ by university and by programme.

We do not publish a threshold for either test, and you should be wary of any page that does. The numbers differ by university, by programme and by intake, and a figure copied from a forum is worse than no figure, because a family plans around it. The university's own published admission criteria is the only source worth acting on. What is generally true, and worth knowing early, is that competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes lean hardest on the Achievement Test.

An overseas application reads a different set of signals: total Diploma points, which subjects were taken at Higher Level, and whether the mathematics course matches the degree's expectation. That last one catches Yanbu families regularly, because the Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation decision is made in the first Diploma year, long before anybody is thinking about an engineering offer. No tutor and no platform can promise an admission outcome, here or anywhere, and an offer is a university's decision from start to finish.

sections.heading: The equivalency and Qiyas route, step by step
paragraphs: Families find this process opaque mostly because it is described in fragments. Laid out in order it is not complicated, but it has dependencies: some steps cannot start until an earlier one has produced a document, and the testing steps want preparation time that has to be carved out of a final school year that is already full. The table sets out who handles each step and what it makes possible.

Two timing traps are worth naming. The first is treating the Achievement Test as something to do after results arrive. Its content follows the Saudi national curriculum, so for an international-curriculum student it needs deliberate preparation rather than revision of what school has already taught. Starting that in the same term as the final papers is a choice to do two things badly. The second is the certificate itself: nothing moves until the school has issued it in a form the Ministry will accept, and a school registrar in the middle of a results cycle is a queue.

A Yanbu family has one extra consideration, which is that these are administrative processes conducted where the offices are. Document collection, attestation steps and test centres are not always a short drive from the Red Sea coast, so the travel is part of the plan rather than an afterthought. Families in Umluj or AlUla should assume more of it, not less.

None of this is something a tutor does for you. What subject teaching can do is make the Achievement Test content a known quantity rather than a surprise, and make sure the school subjects are being taken at the level the destination programme expects. The administrative route is yours and the Ministry's, and the only authoritative description of it is the Ministry's own.

sections.heading: Why the Achievement Test reads differently to an IB or IGCSE student
paragraphs: This is the single most useful thing a Saudi family with an international-curriculum child can be told, and almost nobody writing about tutoring in the Kingdom says it. The Achievement Test covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. A student who has spent five years in Cambridge IGCSE and then the IB Diploma has met most of the underlying material, and met it in a different order, with different notation, different emphasis and a different examination style.

The overlap is real, which is what makes it deceptive. A Diploma Higher Level chemistry student is not short of chemistry. What they may be short of is familiarity with the way a particular topic is framed in the national syllabus, the proportion of the test given to topics their own course treated lightly, and the pace: a reasoning-light, coverage-heavy test rewards speed across breadth, where a Higher Level paper rewards sustained work on fewer questions. Students who are good at the second can be slow at the first.

Language adds a second variable. The tests are sat in Arabic or in English, and a student educated in English throughout will usually sit in English, but subject vocabulary does not always map cleanly between the two framings even then. A family making this choice should make it on the basis of the child's actual reading speed in each language under time pressure, not on which one the household speaks.

Practically, that means treating the test as its own object of study with its own preparation window, and treating school subjects as the thing that supplies the underlying understanding. A tutor who knows both the international syllabus and the shape of the national-curriculum content can map one onto the other and tell you which topics need actual teaching rather than revision. That mapping is the work; it is not something a generic test-prep book does.

sections.heading: What the Yanbu school market can and cannot staff
paragraphs: A school's prospectus lists subjects it is authorised to offer. The useful question is different: which options actually ran in the last intake, and who taught them. In a small cohort those two lists diverge, and the divergence is where families end up needing outside teaching. Asking a school this directly, before enrolment rather than after, is the highest-value conversation available to a parent on this coast.

Industrial-city staffing has a particular shape. Teaching posts in Yanbu compete with the same posts in Jeddah, Riyadh and the Eastern Province cluster, and with the international market generally. Specialists in the scarce subjects, Higher Level Physics, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Computer Science, and the less common group three options, are scarce everywhere, so a school outside the three largest markets fills those posts last and loses them first. One departure in June can remove an option in September.

The second shape is cohort size. A Diploma group that is small in total cannot be split many ways. If four students want one group four option and two want another, the school runs one of them, and the two students take something else. That is a reasonable institutional decision and a poor outcome for those two students, particularly if the subject they lost was a prerequisite for the degree they were aiming at.

Neither of these is solved by looking harder locally. They are solved by separating two things a school normally does together: the teaching of the course, and the specialist drilling of its assessment. The course can be taught by a capable non-specialist following the syllabus. The paper-specific work, the command terms, the mark scheme, the internal assessment design, benefits from somebody who has taught that paper repeatedly, wherever they happen to live.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week against a tutor's own working week
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. Almost every page written about online tutoring assumes the opposite, because it was written for a Monday-to-Friday market and the city name was swapped in. The consequence is practical: a Sunday evening lesson is a school-night lesson for your child and a weekend lesson for a tutor in most other countries, and a Thursday evening lesson is the reverse.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not observe daylight saving. A slot agreed with a tutor in a country that does will move twice a year unless it is pinned to Saudi local time rather than to theirs. This is the most common avoidable disruption in a cross-border tutoring arrangement, and it is entirely avoidable: agree the time in Arabia Standard Time, in writing, and let the tutor's own clock be the thing that moves.

The table below converts a seven in the evening Yanbu slot into the tutor's local time and sets it against their own working week. Read the last column rather than the second: a tutor for whom your Sunday is a weekend day may be available but is less likely to stay available for a full academic year, and a tutor for whom your evening is the middle of their night will not sustain it at all. A Yanbu family on an industrial shift rotation has a narrower window than most, which makes this worth getting right once rather than renegotiating each term.

Where a family lives inside Yanbu matters here too. A Yanbu Al Nakhal school run that ends late pushes a realistic start past the hour that works for a European tutor, which quietly narrows the pool. That is a reason to settle the slot before choosing the tutor, not after.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in this market, and who publishes those numbers
paragraphs: Rates in the Kingdom are mostly hidden behind a contact form, which trains families to assume the worst. The figures below are advertised rates published by other providers and platforms, collected as market context. They are not an average, because a set of marketing pages is not a sample, and they are not IB Gram's price. Read them as the range a Yanbu family will encounter while shopping, with the source type beside each one so you can weigh it.

What moves the number, roughly in order of weight: subject scarcity first, since a Higher Level Physics or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist costs more than a Standard Level mathematics tutor in every market; then examining or marking experience; then level, with Higher Level above Standard Level above the Middle Years Programme above IGCSE; then whether the tutor travels; then package length. A rate quoted without a named subject and level is not a rate, it is an opening position.

Travel loading is the one most often invisible. An in-home arrangement in a spread-out city pays for the drive, either as an explicit surcharge or by a higher hourly rate that absorbs it. Across a term that is a meaningful sum spent on a car rather than on teaching, and in Yanbu, where the districts are far apart, the loading is heavier than the same arrangement would carry in a dense city.

For a Yanbu family the practical advice is to price the specific thing you need. A term of weekly Chemistry Higher Level support with internal assessment feedback is a different purchase to six sessions of examination technique before the June series, and comparing a quote for one against a quote for the other tells you nothing. Ask any provider to quote per subject, per level, and per number of sessions, and ask what happens to unused sessions.
